We are 100+ people across London, Palo Alto, and New York, with rapid growth expectations to hundreds.

About the role

Volta builds and operates large scale GPU compute infrastructure for frontier AI customers. Growing this fast produces a long tail of manual internal work: invoices retyped into banking portals, expense reports chased by hand, spreadsheets reconciled every month, accounts provisioned ticket by ticket. Each task is small. Together they cost the company real time, and they multiply with every new sit and every new hire.

This role removes that work permanently. You sit with the person who owns a process, understand what it actually does, then build the integration that runs it against banking and accounting systems, Microsoft Graph / Office, Slack, Jira and Confluence, and the HR and identity stack. Most of the answer is well built API code with sound authentication, error handling, escalation, audibility and observability. Some of it uses models, for classification, extraction, or matching, where that is the right tool rather than the fashionable one. Knowing the difference is a large part of the job.

Much of this work lands inside the financial reporting path, and Volta is building toward SOX compliance alongside its existing ISO 27001 and SOC 2 obligations. An automation that touches invoices, payments, or reconciliation becomes part of the control environment the moment it goes live. That sets the bar: changes are reviewed, tested, and traceable, access is least privilege and segregated, every run leaves an audit trail an external auditor can follow, and nobody moves code into production by hand. You build to that standard from the first commit rather than retrofitting it under deadline.

Regulation shapes the work in a second way. Volta is headquartered in the UK and operates across the EU, so anything you build with AI in it sits under the EU AI Act as well as UK and EU data protection law. Automation that touches hiring, performance, or other employment decisions carries the heaviest obligations, and the line between a helpful classifier and a regulated decision system is easy to cross without noticing. You are expected to recognize where that line runs, keep a person in the loop where the law requires one, document what you deploy, and bring Legal and Security in early rather than after the build.

You sit inside Corporate IT at a fast-growing AI-forward company, which owns the tooling, accounts, and API access you build on, and which gives you engineers next to you for design discussion and code review rather than leaving you to mark your own homework. Security Engineering advises on access and compliance. The first internal customer is the accounting and finance team. After that the scope is the whole company: finance, IT, People, delivery, product, and the engineering teams for their own internal overhead. Very little here is customer facing. Initially, you are the only person doing this work full time, so you prioritize hard, ship small, and build things that keep running without you next to them.

What You Will Be Doing

  • Automate finance operations first: ingest received invoices into banking and bookkeeping systems, classify and match them, and close the loop on the exceptions

  • Work directly with process owners across finance, IT, People, and delivery: take a described workflow and turn it into a specified, testable automation

  • Work as part of Corporate IT: review their changes, have yours reviewed, and keep automation aligned with how the underlying systems are administered

  • Build and run integrations against internal systems, including Microsoft Graph, Slack, Atlassian, banking platforms, and HR and identity tooling

  • Own authentication and credentials for those integrations: OAuth flows, service principals, scoped tokens, secret rotation

  • Build every finance touching automation to withstand audit: version controlled and peer reviewed changes, automated deployment with no manual production edits, least privilege service identities, segregation of duties preserved rather than automated away, and retained evidence of what ran, when, and on whose authority

  • Work with Finance and Security Engineering on control design, so an automation replaces a manual control with a stronger automated one instead of quietly removing it

  • Apply models where they earn their place, for document extraction, classification, or matching, and use conventional code everywhere else. Keep a human decision point where a control requires one

  • Build agentic automations where a single scripted path will not hold: an agent that picks up a case, calls the tools it needs across Microsoft Graph, Slack, Atlassian and the finance stack, and stops at a human approval gate before anything with money or access impact. You define the tool surface, the permitted scope, and the blast radius, rather than handing a model a broad credential and watching what happens.

  • Keep AI use inside its regulatory boundaries: automatically classify use cases correctly under the

  • EU AI Act, apply transparency and human oversight where required, document deployed systems, and escalate anything touching employment decisions to Legal before it is built

  • Instrument what you build so failures surface immediately and the state of any run is visible without reading logs

  • Maintain what you deploy, including the unglamorous part where an upstream API changes and the process still has to run on Monday

  • Set the patterns, repositories, and review practices that keep internal automation maintainable and auditable as more of it accumulates

  • Push back when a process should be simplified or deleted instead of automated

What You Bring

  • Production software development held to the standard of an engineering team, not scripting attached to an operational role

  • Fluency across more than one software ecosystem. Internal systems arrive in whatever language, runtime, and SDK their vendor picked, and you are expected to work in what the problem needs rather than bending every problem toward one stack. Python and Go come up often here, neither is a requirement

  • Deep practical work with third party APIs: pagination, rate limits, idempotency, retries, webhooks, and how an integration behaves when the far end is having a bad day

  • Real command of authentication mechanisms, including OAuth 2.0, OIDC, service accounts, and API key and secret management

  • Disciplined engineering practice that produces an audit trail as a by-product: source control, code review, automated testing, controlled deployment, and clear separation between who builds a change and who releases it

  • Hands on experience building with LLMs, including tool use and structured extraction, plus the judgment to recognize when a model is the wrong answer

  • Hands on work with agentic patterns: tool and function calling, MCP or equivalent tool interfaces, state and retry handling across multi step runs, and testing agent behavior against realistic cases before it touches a production system.

  • Working awareness of the rules governing AI and automated decision making in a workplace context, at the level of knowing which use cases need legal review before a line of code is written

  • Ability to sit with a subject matter expert, understand a business process well enough to implement it correctly, and translate it without needing them to specify the solution

  • A track record of building reliable, secure, auditable systems rather than demos that work once

  • Comfort as the only engineer on a problem: choosing what to build next and owning the outcome

Nice to Have

  • Delivering AI systems under the EU AI Act: risk classification, technical documentation, transparency and human oversight obligations

  • Building or operating systems in SOX scope: IT general controls, change management, segregation of duties, and producing evidence for external audit

  • Finance systems experience: accounts payable, expense management, bank reconciliation, ERP integration

Face à la hausse des coûts de l'énergie, aux enjeux climatiques et aux évolutions réglementaires, les gestionnaires de patrimoine ont besoin d'outils fiables, mais aussi d'un accompagnement de qualité pour passer à l'action.

C'est pourquoi nous avons développé une plateforme SaaS qui permet de créer le jumeau numérique des bâtiments, de piloter les consommations énergétiques et de construire des trajectoires d'investissement réalistes, chiffrées et adaptées aux enjeux de chaque organisation.

Aujourd'hui, nous accompagnons plusieurs centaines de collectivités et d'entreprises partout en France dans leurs projets de transition énergétique.

Entreprise lyonnaise en forte croissance, nous recherchons des collaborateurs qui souhaitent avoir un impact concret, prendre des responsabilités et contribuer à une aventure collective porteuse de sens.

Vos missions

En lien direct avec le responsable marketing et communication, vous participerez à la mise en œuvre de la stratégie de communication de l'entreprise afin de renforcer sa notoriété, valoriser son offre et engager ses différentes cibles (B2B, secteurs privé et public).

Création de contenus audiovisuels

  • Concevoir, tourner et monter des vidéos : présentations produit, témoignages clients, interviews d'experts, formats courts pour les réseaux sociaux,

  • Réaliser des visuels et supports graphiques en cohérence avec la charte de l'entreprise,

  • Participer à la captation de contenus lors d'événements, de webinaires ou de salons,

  • Adapter les contenus aux différents canaux (sous-titrage, déclinaisons de formats, miniatures).

Rédaction & production de contenus

  • Rédiger des contenus variés : articles de blog, actualités, newsletters, cas clients, communiqués de presse,

  • Adapter le ton et le niveau de langage aux cibles (décideurs, techniciens, collectivités, partenaires),

  • Contribuer à la création de supports marketing : plaquettes, présentations, fiches produit, emailings.

Animation des réseaux sociaux

  • Participation au développement des comptes de l'entreprise (LinkedIn et YouTube),

  • Rédiger et programmer les publications, en adaptant le ton et le format à chaque plateforme,

  • Animer la communauté : veille, interactions, relais des actualités de l'entreprise et de ses collaborateurs,

  • Proposer des formats innovants pour accroître l'engagement (carrousels, vidéos courtes, témoignages, séries thématiques).

Gestion du site web (WordPress)

  • Mettre en ligne et mettre à jour les contenus sur le site : pages, articles, actualités, visuels, vidéos,

  • Veiller à la cohérence éditoriale et graphique ainsi qu'à la qualité des contenus publiés,

  • Appliquer les bonnes pratiques de base (SEO, poids des images, accessibilité, liens).

Événementiel & communication corporate

  • Participer à l'organisation et à la promotion des événements (salons, webinaires, conférences),

  • Contribuer à la communication interne et à la valorisation de la marque employeur,

  • Assurer une veille sur les tendances de communication et les actions des concurrents.

Suivi de performance & amélioration continue

  • Suivre les indicateurs clés (engagement, audience, trafic, taux d'ouverture…) via des outils type LinkedIn Analytics, GA4, outils d'emailing,

  • Réaliser des reportings réguliers et proposer des axes d'optimisation,

  • Participer à l'élaboration et au suivi du calendrier éditorial.

Vos compétences

Vous préparez une formation en communication, marketing, audiovisuel, journalisme ou équivalent (Bac+4 / Bac+5) et souhaitez développer vos compétences sur l'ensemble des leviers de la communication et du marketing.

Vous avez une plume claire et efficace, un bon sens visuel et aimez raconter des histoires, à l'écrit comme en vidéo. Vous savez adapter un message à une cible et à un canal, et transformer un sujet technique en contenu accessible et engageant.

Vous êtes à l'aise avec les réseaux sociaux et avez déjà manipulé des outils de montage vidéo et de création graphique.

Vous êtes rigoureux·se, organisé·e, créatif·ve, curieux·se, et appréciez le travail en équipe : prendre du feedback, itérer rapidement et respecter des délais.

Un plus : compétences en tournage (cadrage, lumière, son), portfolio de réalisations (vidéos, visuels, publications), projets personnels en lien avec la communication, première expérience en communication B2B ou dans le secteur de la transition énergétique.

Compétences clés

  • Excellente qualité rédactionnelle : orthographe, grammaire, style clair, capacité à vulgariser et à adapter son ton,

  • Maîtrise du montage vidéo (CapCut, Premiere Pro, Final Cut, DaVinci Resolve ou équivalent),

  • Compétences audiovisuelles appréciées : tournage, prise de son, vidéo mobile,

  • Bonne connaissance des réseaux sociaux, de leurs codes et de leurs formats,

  • Connaissance de WordPress et des bases du SEO,

Vocca in a few words

Vocca is an AI voice agent that answers 100% of the calls of medical centres. The patient calls, the AI books the appointment or answers the question, and the medical secretaries keep their time for the cases where a human is really needed.

  • $20M raised, with the founders of Alan and Datadog as investors

  • Close to 1 million calls a month going through the platform

  • More than 1,000 medical staff use our product all day

The problem

Every medical centre has its own rules. Who can book what, with which practitioner, at what time, what to do with an urgent case at 6 pm. Today these rules live in prompts and in the heads of our ops team. Each new clinic takes hours of manual work, and the ops team is the bottleneck of our growth.

We are building the platform that removes that bottleneck. A scenario engine where the behaviour of the agent is structured configuration, not free text. A self-serve onboarding where a clinic connects its software and sets itself up. A dashboard where the medical staff stop executing and start supervising: the agent handles the volume, humans check what matters.

This is the difference between selling a service and selling a product. The long term vision is simple: a clinic signs, connects its software and is live within days, without a single developer involved. You would be building that.

What you will own

  • The scenario engine and its configuration model. One product that handles the rules of thousands of medical centres without becoming a swamp.

  • The self-serve onboarding, from the backend to the dashboard. Internal tooling already took a clinic deployment from days to under an hour. The next step is zero developer ticket on a standard onboarding.

  • The dashboard our clinics use all day. Fast, reliable and clean enough that a medical secretary prefers it to the phone. We take frontend quality seriously and follow a design system written in code.

  • Your features, end to end. From the spec with the ops team to production, and the fix when something breaks, with the reason it does not happen again.

How we build

  • Experimental, not R&D. You test, you prove with data, you ship. Challenging a decision means coming back with a result, not a debate.

  • Ship, then fix the last 1%. We ship the version that works, then fix the last 1% when it shows up. With AI, this trade off is much cheaper than before. The judgment about what not to touch is yours.

  • AI, seriously. Agents in every workflow, Claude Max provided. A migration estimated at 3 months was done in 2 weeks.

  • Close to the field. Every change lands in front of more than 1,000 medical staff. You talk every day with the ops team that deploys clinics and the sales team that sells the product.

Stack

TypeScript everywhere, backend and frontend (Node, monorepo), PostgreSQL, a design system written in code. We are migrating our last Python services to TypeScript over the coming months.

Who does well here

  • 3 to 8 years building full-stack products in production, in startups that were growing fast.

  • You stayed long enough somewhere to see a system live, break and get better, and you learned from it.

  • TypeScript is your main language, backend and frontend, not a line on your CV. You have a real eye for interface quality and the discipline to follow a design system.

  • You think about the product and the business as much as the code, and you know how to build systems that hold when the volume explodes.

  • You move without waiting for a perfect frame: you try, you propose, you ship. You ask for help when you are stuck.

  • You had good practices before AI: solid system design, clean refactoring and a good nose for the risks of generated code that nobody tested.

Probably not for you if you need every feature fully specified before you start

What we expect from you

  • First week. Onboarded on the stack, your first improvement on the dashboard is in production.

  • First month. You own one feature end to end, from the spec with the ops team to production, without mockups or hand-holding.

  • First 3 months. The first version of the scenario engine is in production. A standard clinic can be onboarded without a developer ticket.

  • 6 to 12 months. Most new clinics are live within 7 days. Clinics configure their own rules in the dashboard.

Process: 4 steps, fast

  1. 45 min with Nans (Talent).

  2. 45 min with Pierrick, Head of Engineering.

  3. 1h30 in our office with the engineering team: coding without AI and a real conversation about product architecture.

  4. 30 min with Hugo, CTO.

Then references and an offer. When the match is obvious, we have made an offer in 24 hours. You get feedback at every step.

title: Staff Engineer / Paris (W/M/X)
description:
Pioneer of online flash sales since 2001 and key player in European e-commerce, Veepee collaborates with over 7,000 brands to offer highly discounted products available for a limited time. Operating across various sectors, including fashion, home, wine, travel or beauty... Veepee achieved a turnover of 3.3 billion euros incl. VAT in 2024 and employs 5,000 staff members across 10 countries.

🎯 Level & Domain

Level:

Staff Engineer is IC4 on our engineering ladder:

  • Has worked as a Senior Developer in at least two product teams. 

  • Turns the tribe’s hardest, ill-framed problems into shipped business value. 

  • Lands in any product fast, de-risks the complex, and raises the bar across teams.

    • The Fastline:

    Each domain has its own Fastline: a small team of Staff Engineers working across all the products of the domain, in a highly agile, commando mode.

    The Fastline is transverse to the domain’s products: it is not attached to one product, but deployed wherever a domain needs senior engineering firepower the most.

    The Fastline takes on three kinds of work:

  • Complex features in existing products: deliver features too risky, cross-cutting or technically hard for a product team to absorb alongside its committed roadmap.

  • Legacy decommissioning: retire legacy systems safely, migrate their capabilities and data, and switch them off for good.

  • IS simplification: reduce the complexity of the tribe’s information system, remove duplication, and make the architecture easier to run and evolve.

    • Fastlines are attached to the Domain Lead, who sets their priorities based on business value, in coordination with the domains’ Lead ITs. Missions are short and outcome-driven: you join a topic, deliver, hand over to the owning product team, and move on to the next one. 


    🎯 TASK

    Strategic & Hard Problems

  • Take on the domain’s most difficult and strategic topics: legacy decommissioning, IS simplification, complex features in existing products.

  • Contribute, with the Architects, to the decommissioning of legacy systems end to end: map dependencies and data flows, design the migration path, run it without business disruption, and switch the legacy off.

  • Drive the simplification of the tribe’s information system: identify redundant components, unnecessary coupling and dead code, and remove them.

  • Deliver complex, cross-cutting features inside existing products, working hand in hand with their product teams.

    • Fast Onboarding & Delivery

  • Land in any product or codebase of the domain and become productive in days, not months.

  • Quickly understand the business context, the architecture, the constraints and the people involved in a topic.

  • Deliver early and often: integrate end to end first, sequence work from most unknown to least worrisome, and show tangible progress quickly.

  • Hand over cleanly to the owning product team: documentation, tests, runbooks and knowledge transfer, so that the team can run what you built.

    • Problem Framing & Business Partnership

  • Take ill-defined, poorly framed problems and turn them into clear, actionable plans.

  • Navigate between tech and business: understand the business stakes, challenge the need with a “how yes” mindset, and propose the simplest solution that delivers the value.

  • Partner with business teams, PMs/POs and Engineering Managers to shape the problem, identify rabbit holes, no-gos and hidden complexity, and agree on scope.

  • Think business value first: explain the value of every technical investment, legacy removal and simplification included.

  • Be the person the business can count on: reliable, transparent on risks, and committed to outcomes.

    • Engineering Excellence & Technical Leadership

  • Own the how end to end: architecture, libraries, data model, implementation, testing and deployment.

  • Write production code: you are hands-on and contribute heavily to the implementation.

  • Make sound technical trade-offs and document key decisions.

  • Raise the bar in the teams you work with: code quality, testing, operability, and AI-first practices.

  • Coach and mentor engineers along the way, and share knowledge across products.

  • Contribute to the domain’s technical vision and target architecture with the Lead IT and the domain’s Architects.

    • Run & Reliability

  • Live by “you build it, you run it”: ship stable, battle-tested software and take ownership of its run until it is handed over.

  • Make migrations and decommissioning safe: rollback plans, monitoring, data reconciliation, progressive switch-over.

  • Step in on critical incidents and complex production problems across the domain when your expertise is needed.

    • AI-First Ways of Working

  • Treat specifications and tests as IP: in an AI era where code is cheap, Veepee’s value moves from code to clear specifications and tests.

  • Use applied AI and prototyping to move faster: understand legacy codebases, generate migrations and tests, explore solutions.

  • Apply a “no roadmap without AI” mindset and spread AI-first practices across the products you work on.


    • 👉 What this role is not
  • Not a manager: you have no direct reports. You lead through expertise, influence and delivery, not hierarchy.

  • Not an ivory-tower architect: you do not draw diagrams and leave. You write code, ship to production and own the outcome.

  • Not attached to a single product: you go wherever the domain needs you most, and you move on once the job is done.

  • Not a spec coder: you do not need a detailed spec to start. A messy, poorly framed problem is your starting point.

  • Not a purely technical expert disconnected from the business: you understand the business, take initiative and drive every topic with a value-first mindset.


    • 👉 Requirements

  • Experience as a Senior Developer (IC3), or equivalent, in at least two product teams, with a strong track record of shipping working, tested software in production on complex systems.

  • Proven experience on hard, high-stakes topics: legacy migration and decommissioning, large refactorings, architecture simplification, or critical features in existing systems.

  • Deep technical expertise: architecture, system design, distributed systems, data modelling, and engineering best practices.

  • Hands-on and fast: able to dive into an unknown codebase and business context and deliver value quickly.

  • Strong business acumen: ability to understand a business domain, its stakes and KPIs, and to build trusted relationships with business teams.

  • Excellent problem-solving skills: comfortable with ambiguity, able to frame an ill-defined problem and find the simplest path to value.

  • High autonomy and ownership: you do not need to be told what to do, and you take full accountability for outcomes.

  • Hands-on with the “you build it, you run it” principle: operability, monitoring, on-call and SLAs.

  • Pragmatic understanding of applied AI and AI-first engineering (prototyping / vibe coding, AI-assisted legacy understanding, specifications and tests as IP).

  • Ability to influence without authority, and to coach and raise the level of the engineers around you.

  • Excellent communication and collaboration with PMs/POs, Engineering Managers, business teams, engineers, Architects, SREs, the Lead IT and the Domain Lead.

  • Open to internal Senior Developers (IC3) who meet these criteria, as well as external applications.

  • Master’s degree in Engineering / IT or equivalent.

  • Fluency in English, international environment.

Au sein de l'équipe Administration & Finance France, le/la Chargé(e) de facturation maintenance assure la gestion et le suivi de la facturation des contrats de maintenance et des prestations associées.

Il/Elle veille à la fiabilité des données contractuelles et tarifaires, au respect des échéances de facturation et à la bonne transmission des éléments nécessaires à la comptabilisation et au suivi du chiffre d'affaires.

  • Créer et mettre à jour les données de facturation dans les outils de gestion.
  • Établir les factures initiales, les renouvellements et les éventuelles factures complémentaires.
  • Gérer les avoirs et les régularisations nécessaires.
  • Veiller au respect des délais de paiement par les clients et participer à la relance en cas d’impayé en lien direct avec le client pour une transformation efficace de la facturation en trésorerie.

  • Identifier et régulariser les éventuelles anomalies ou incohérences.

4 stories par semaine et par client.

1 carrousel par semaine et par client.

Nous recherchons une personne ayant déjà une première expérience professionnelle en Social Media Management.

Un dernier échange pour approfondir votre candidature et vous permettre de découvrir la vision et les ambitions de l'agence.

POURQUOI REJOINDRE CULINARY AGENCY ?

Rejoindre Culinary Agency, c'est intégrer une agence en pleine croissance, spécialisée dans des univers passionnants, où l'image, la créativité et le sens du détail occupent une place centrale.

Vous travaillerez sur des projets variés, auprès de restaurants, chefs, hôtels et marques, avec la possibilité de développer votre expertise en Social Media Management dans l'univers de la gastronomie et de l'Hospitality.

title: GTM & Value Creation Lead
description:
About Hexa

Hexa builds and scales software companies alongside entrepreneurs. Since its launch as eFounders, Hexa has helped create companies including Aircall, Spendesk, Front, Swan and Yousign.

Hexa Scale is a small-cap software investment firm deploying a €100 million fund. We take majority stakes in established B2B software companies and work directly with their founders to unlock their next stage of growth. We bring capital, but first and formemost operators who get involved in the daily work to build the fundamentals required to ignite a real Sscaling story: go-to-market, product, hiring and the systems needed.

Hexa Scale

Many software companies have a strong product and loyal customers but have yet to build a repeatable growth engine. Their next phase calls for more than optimising today’s funnel: they need to rethink how they find, win, serve and grow customers as AI changes both customer workflows and commercial execution. They need people who can test what works with their teams and turn the learning into a way of operating.

That is what we do at Hexa Scale. We invest in software companies with roughly €2–10 million in ARR and work alongside their founders after the investment. Our approach is hands-on, with go-to-market at the centre of the acceleration plan?

Mission

We’re looking for a Value Creation Manager with a strong GTM background to join the Hexa Scale team. You will assess growth opportunities and feasibility before an investment decision, then work across our portfolio with founders and their teams to remove growth bottlenecks. Your judgement will help the investment team test whether a company has strong, executable growth potential; your operating work will help turn that potential into results.

This is a GTM-major role: your core craft is building a next-generation go-to-market engine, combining customer insight, commercial execution, data and AI-enabled workflows. You have built or improved commercial motions inside a fast-growing startup, and you are as comfortable with positioning and customer interviews as with sales execution, pricing & process optimization. The remit can become broader as the needs and maturity of each portfolio company change, particularly where product is the best route to more customer value and growth.

You will not be an external advisor producing slides for a management team. You will work with that team, from within the company, establish a useful operating cadence and leave behind a system they can run without you.

What you’ll do

As a preliminary note and as you’ll understand based on the 4 pillars below, the role is in close synch with the investment team. You’ll be a sparing partner, brining both your expert judgement as well as your field working competences to the table. While the role will enable lots of autonomy, you’ll be working in close synch with one or more investment partners, who’re experienced entrepreneurs you’ll learn from and who’ll have the final call on major decisions.

Participate in investment selection

  • Assess growth potential: Work with the deal team before an investment decision to test whether the growth opportunity is substantial, accessible and actionable, rather than relying on an optimistic management plan.

  • Support commercial diligence: support the investment team in interviews of customers and prospects; examine segmentation, win/loss, funnel conversion, sales cycles, retention and expansion, pricing, channels and the capacity of the current team to execute.

  • Underwrite the growth levers: Prioritize potential improvements in GTM, pricing, upmarket sales or distribution. Quantify the starting point, expected impact, costs, timing, dependencies and downside. Separate demonstrated opportunities from assumptions that still need testing.

  • Turn diligence into a plan: Present an evidence-based growth-engineering assessment to the investment team, including what could disprove the thesis and an initial post-close step-by-step execution roadmap. Final investment decisions remain with the partners.

Build a next-generation go-to-market engine

  • Find the constraint: Work with founders and commercial teams to understand where growth stalls, from targeting and lead generation to conversion, onboarding and expansion.

  • Get close to customers: Run interviews, listen to sales calls, examine lost deals and translate what you learn into sharper segmentation, messaging and offers.

  • Run experiments: Lead and co-run tests with teams across outbound, partnerships, demand generation, pricing, AI-assisted prospecting and sales processes. Set a baseline, define what success looks like, measure conversion and unit economics, and stop what doesn’t work, while bringing teams along so the new ways of working stick.

  • Build AI-enabled GTM workflows: Design and test practical workflows for research, targeting, qualification, sales preparation, customer success or expansion using AI tools and agents where appropriate. Measure quality, adoption, cost and human oversight, not just activity or demos.

  • Make the funnel usable: Improve CRM discipline, pipeline visibility, forecasting and the handoffs between marketing, sales and customer success. Automate repeatable work where it improves the customer experience and commercial outcomes.

Execute alongside portfolio teams

  • Connect product and growth: As portfolio needs and maturity vary, partner with product teams to increase customer value and create new growth paths. Explore features such as embedded finance or agentic execution where relevant; validate customer demand, adoption, willingness to pay, implementation costs and margins before treating them as growth levers.

  • Work with founders: Help turn priorities into a weekly cadence, clear owners and decisions grounded in customer and commercial evidence.

  • Build internal capability: Coach or assist in recruiting when needed the people who will own the work long term. Document the useful parts of a playbook without imposing the same answer on every company.

  • Own critical projects: Take responsibility for a defined growth or operating problem, from diagnosis through implementation, rather than handing over a recommendation.

Can include temporary embedding in the company on a full-time basis

Strengthen the Hexa Scale operating model

  • Make our work repeatable: Capture what works across portfolio companies and improve the tools and methods we use to diagnose and accelerate growth.

  • Take on adjacent problems: GTM remains your major, but the most valuable work may extend into product, customer operations, hiring or cross-functional execution depending on the company and its stage of maturity. Know when to take ownership and when to bring in a specialist.

  • Use technology pragmatically: Build and deploy AI-enabled workflows with portfolio teams when they improve GTM outcomes or customer value. Assess reliability, cost and operational fit; do not confuse a demo with an adopted process.

What we’re looking for

Experience

  • Five years or more: Substantial time in a fast-growing startup or scale-up in a hands-on GTM role.

  • Commercial execution: You have personally built, operated or significantly improved a B2B growth engine, ideally in a fast-growing startup. You can explain how you changed the GTM motion, what the numbers showed and what you would do differently.

  • B2B software: You understand sales cycles, conversion, retention, expansion, pricing and the trade-offs involved in scaling a team. Experience in high growth vertical SaaS is a plus.

  • Range: You can work across sales, marketing, customer success and operations without needing a large team or a perfectly defined brief.

  • Working with leaders: Experience alongside founders or senior commercial leaders is a strong plus. French and English fluency are required for this role.

Mindset

  • Autonomous: You can turn an ambiguous problem into a plan, make progress and know when a decision needs to be escalated.

  • Hands-on: You are willing to inspect the CRM, join customer calls, rewrite a sequence and run an experiment yourself.

  • AI-fluent: You already build with AI tools and use them in your daily work, not just in occasional demos. You can show workflows or products you have built, explain what worked and failed, and help teams adopt AI where it changes how they go to market.

  • Commercially sharp: You care about revenue outcomes, not activity for its own sake.

  • Versatile without being superficial: GTM is your major, but you can work on product and wider operating problems when they are the real constraint. You connect new customer value to adoption, pricing, retention and growth.

  • Low ego, high standards: You can challenge a founder’s assumption, listen when you are wrong and earn the trust of the team doing the work.

What we offer

  • Ownership: A role at the centre of Hexa Scale’s work with founders, with responsibility for real operating projects across B2B software companies.

  • Team: Direct collaboration with Hexa Scale partners and access to Hexa’s product, talent, brand and operational expertise.

  • Compensation: A competitive package, including carried interest

  • Benefits: Hexa employee benefits may include a Swile meal card, RTT, a green mobility budget and health insurance.

Recruitment process

Proposed process, to confirm with the Talent team:

  1. Introductory call with Hexa’s Talent team.

  2. Interview with the Hexa Scale team on your GTM experience and operating approach.

  3. Practical case on a real pre-investment growth diligence and portfolio execution problem, followed by a working session.

  4. Conversations with the people you would work with most closely.

  5. Reference checks and offer.

Confirm speakers early enough to include them in event promotions, landing pages, emails, and social campaigns, and manage briefing, preparation, logistics, approvals, and follow-up.

  • Analytical and operational skills, including the ability to connect customer behavior and program performance to business outcomes.

  • Ability to work effectively across EMEA markets and time zones. Additional language skills are a plus.

  • Review volume, ratings, sentiment, and progress against award criteria.

title: Junior Business Controller (Data specialist)
description:
Do you enjoy working with numbers, analysing data and finding out what is really happening behind the figures? As Junior Business Controller at HG, you will support our Controllers and Group Financial Controller with financial analyses, reporting and increasingly data-driven insights.

At HG, you will work in a compact organisation with an international reach. You will get the opportunity to learn from experienced colleagues, take responsibility early and turn financial and business data into insights that help us make better decisions. We value people who are curious, take initiative and have the energy to turn ideas into action.

About the role

As Junior Business Controller, you will support our Controllers and gradually build your own areas of responsibility. The role combines financial activities with a strong focus on data, analysis and improving management information.

You will:

  • support the Business Controllers with financial analyses, reporting and recurring control activities;

  • own and maintain the data model

  • analyse financial and business data and translate it into useful insights;

  • investigate differences, trends and developments and help explain what is happening behind the numbers;

  • build, review and improve data models used for reporting and analysis;

  • use various tools including Excel and Power BI to make information clearer and easier to use;

  • investigate how data flows from source to report and identify opportunities to improve data quality and reporting;

  • help reduce manual work by finding smarter and more reliable ways of working;

  • contribute to improvements in management information and financial processes;

  • translate questions from colleagues into practical analyses and insights.

An important part of the role is conceptual thinking about data. You understand how information should be structured, see connections between different data points and can think about how a data model can be improved to provide better business insights.

Your development in data

Next to your finance responsibilities, you will grow step by step into the data side of the role, coached by our current Data Specialist. You do not need to master these areas from day one: together we will set up a development path in which you learn to:

  • contribute to HG's Business Intelligence and data strategy, making sure data supports our company goals;

  • design and maintain data models (such as star schemas) and database/Lakehouse structures, so that data is accurate, reliable and accessible;

  • integrate data from different sources and systems in a medallion model (Bronze for raw data, Silver for engineering, Gold for consumption);

  • manage the HG Data Dictionary, data repositories and the underlying data architecture;

  • apply data governance and data quality practices, including audit trails, data privacy requirements and best-practice frameworks such as DAMA;

  • map business processes (BPMN 2.0) and translate business requirements into practical data solutions;

  • work with tools such as SQL, Python (pandas), Power Query, Power Automate and Microsoft Fabric, and over time explore AI techniques;

  • document data models and data processes, and monitor data systems for performance and reliability.

This gives you a strong combination of finance and data expertise, which is becoming increasingly valuable in modern Business Control.

Collaboration & positioning

You will be part of the Finance team and work closely with our Business Controllers. This gives you the opportunity to learn from experienced colleagues while contributing your own analytical and data-driven perspective.

Because HG is a relatively compact organisation, you will have direct contact with colleagues across different disciplines. This means you can quickly see how your analyses and improvements are being used in the business. At the same time, you will work within an international organisation, with colleagues and markets across Europe.

The role is based at our head office in Almere.

HG is a compact, fast-growing and international organization where you can directly see the impact of your work. This requires ownership, initiative and a pragmatic, results-oriented mindset. The team culture is open, pragmatic and focused on results, encouraging you to bring ideas forward, challenge constructively and take responsibility. Everything we do is guided by our three core values: Aim High, Be Brave, Be Connected.


What you bring

We are looking for someone who is analytical, energetic and curious. You enjoy getting to the bottom of a question rather than simply producing a report. You want to understand why the numbers look the way they do and how the underlying data can provide better insights.

You bring:

  • willingness to learn

  • around 3–5 years of relevant work experience, for example as a big 4 auditor, Finance Analyst, Data Analyst or Junior Business Controller;

  • solid knowledge of finance and accounting, preferably gained through an education in Accountancy, Finance & Control, Business Information Management, Data Analytics);

  • experience with or a strong interest in Power BI;

  • strong analytical skills;

  • the ability to think conceptually about data, reporting and data models;

  • a curious and proactive approach to solving problems;

  • the confidence to ask questions and challenge existing ways of working;

  • an energetic mindset and the drive to learn and improve;

  • a genuine eagerness to learn and to keep developing yourself, both in finance and in data;

  • fluent English; knowledge of Dutch is desirable.

  • experience with AI tools, such as Copilot.

    Please note that we do not offer visa or work permit sponsorship for this position. You must therefore hold a valid EU work permit

What we offer

This is a role where you can build a strong foundation in modern Business Control while developing further in data and analytics. You will not only work with existing reports and figures, but also have the opportunity to improve how information is structured, analysed and used.

You can expect:

  • a monthly salary between €4.000 and €5.200 (excluding holiday allowance), depending on your experience.

  • an annual on-target bonus of 10% of your gross annual salary; 

  • full-time employment with 30 days of annual leave; 

  • a pension scheme; 

  • a commuting allowance; 

  • a dynamic and ambitious working environment where initiative and ownership are valued;

  • the opportunity to grow towards a broader Business Controller role as your knowledge, experience and responsibilities develop;

  • structured coaching by our Data Specialist to develop your data skills alongside your finance role;

  • a friendly, welcoming team, with a free shared lunch every Monday and monthly social drinks.

We are HG

HG is a leading European brand in specialist cleaning and maintenance products.

We believe a home should be a place where people can live carefree, with confidence in the products they use to care for the spaces and belongings around them. Our products are developed to do exactly what they promise: deliver effective, reliable and specialist cleaning solutions that help consumers solve real household problems.

HG’s mission is to help people enjoy their homes without worrying about what might go wrong. We do this through high-quality products, specialist expertise, clear advice and a relentless focus on performance.

We are dedicated to delivering superiority, innovation, quality and customer satisfaction. With a strong presence across Europe and beyond, we are continuously investing to make an even bigger impact.

HG does what it promises.

Vanuit jouw rol houd je overzicht, coördineer je verbeteracties en steek je zelf de handen uit de mouwen. Je bent dus niet alleen adviserend bezig, maar zorgt er ook voor dat zaken daadwerkelijk worden uitgevoerd. Je bevordert het bewustzijn en de kennis van informatiebeveiliging en privacy binnen de organisatie en ondersteunt bij incidenten, risicoanalyses en assessments.

  • Het coördineren van verbeteracties en ondersteunen bij informatiebeveiligingsincidenten en datalekken.

  • Het vergroten van bewustzijn binnen de organisatie en collega’s praktisch adviseren over informatiebeveiliging en privacy.

  • De rol biedt nadrukkelijk ruimte om te groeien. Naarmate je de organisatie en het vakgebied beter leert kennen, pak je steeds meer regie en ontwikkel je je verder van een praktisch en coördinerende rol naar een meer tactische en strategische adviesrol.

Hier kom je terecht

Berenschot is een zelfstandig en onafhankelijk Nederlands organisatieadviesbureau in Utrecht, waar we met meer dan 500 gedreven collega’s werken aan duurzame oplossingen voor de vraagstukken van onze opdrachtgevers. Onze organisatie heeft een platte structuur zonder partners, waardoor je korte lijnen hebt met collega’s en de ruimte krijgt om verbeteringen voor te stellen en op te pakken.


Dit neem je mee

Je hebt een stevige basis in informatiebeveiliging en privacy en vindt het leuk om zaken daadwerkelijk voor elkaar te krijgen. Je kunt beleid en risico’s vertalen naar concrete oplossingen en voelt je prettig in een rol waarin nog niet alles vastligt. Tegelijkertijd heb je de ambitie om je verder te ontwikkelen en op termijn ook meer strategische verantwoordelijkheid te pakken.

Daarbij neem je mee:

  • Hbo-werk- en -denkniveau; bijvoorbeeld op het gebied van securitymanagement, bestuurskunde of bedrijfskunde.

  • Minimaal vijf jaar werkervaring en relevante ervaring op het gebied van informatiebeveiliging en/of privacy.

  • Het vermogen om risico’s en beleid te vertalen naar concrete, werkbare maatregelen en acties.

  • Een praktische en zelfstandige houding: je adviseert, organiseert én pakt zelf zaken op.

  • Sterk analytisch vermogen, goede communicatieve vaardigheden en organisatiesensitiviteit, waardoor je collega’s kunt meenemen en verschillende belangen bij elkaar kunt brengen.

Certificeringen als CISSP, CISM, CISA, CISM, CIPP/E, CIPM en CDPO zijn een pré, maar geen vereiste. Belangrijker vinden we dat je de inhoudelijke basis en motivatie hebt om je hierin verder te ontwikkelen.

Bij Berenschot bieden we een unieke commerciële omgeving zonder aandeelhouders of partners. Dit geeft ons veel ruimte en vrijheid om te ondernemen en de mogelijkheid om ons in te zetten voor belangrijke maatschappelijke thema’s. Kenmerkend is onze informele cultuur. Ons diverse en inclusieve personeelsbeleid omarmt diversiteit en biedt iedereen gelijke kansen.

In deze functie krijg je ruimte om samen met collega’s de het information- & securitybeleid verder vorm te geven en je inhoudelijk te ontwikkelen. Zo bouw je mee aan de informatiebeveiliging en privacy binnen Berenschot én aan je eigen volgende stap.

EU Remote (CET preferred) · German & English · Full-time
Competitive salary · Early equity

YOUR MISSION

A software engineer today works alongside Claude Code or Cursor. A mechanical engineer designing the next jet engine still clicks through CAD trees, searches Excel sheets and asks whoever has been around longest.

We are building the AI co-engineer for physical products: one that works natively in 3D and learns from real engineering decisions. We are in production with major European manufacturers.

The interaction model is still an open problem. How does an engineer give an agent context, steer its work and understand what changed? How much should the agent figure out itself? And how does all of this fit into existing CAD and engineering workflows?

You will work directly with founders, engineers and customers to figure that out and turn it into a product people can actually use.

You are our first full-time product designer. We want someone with a point of view who can help shape the direction, not someone waiting for a finished brief.

WHAT YOU'LL WORK ON

You will work across discovery, interaction design and shipped product. We cannot say exactly what that looks like in month three, but these are the kinds of problems in front of us:

  • How engineers work with AI agents in 3D. Briefing, steering, reviewing and understanding agent work without turning the product into another complex engineering tool.

  • Connecting AI into real engineering workflows. Spend time with customers, understand how they actually work, test ideas early and turn what you learn into better product decisions.

  • Prototyping new interaction models. Sometimes that means Figma, sometimes a rough prototype in code, sometimes pairing directly with an engineer. Use whatever gets us to an answer fastest.

  • Driving product initiatives with founders and engineers. Help frame the problem, facilitate decisions and turn a direction into projects and tasks the team can execute.

  • Making the product coherent as it grows. Own interaction and visual quality, including the design system, without slowing down experimentation.

WHAT WE CARE ABOUT

  • You have shipped complex software products for expert users and can point to the decisions you made, not just the final screens.

  • You are comfortable when the problem is not yet defined. You form your own opinion, push back and help create clarity.

  • You have strong product judgment. You know when to research, when to prototype, when to polish and when to ship.

  • You are comfortable working directly with customers and software engineers, and you learn unfamiliar domains quickly.

  • You have strong interaction and visual craft and are comfortable with Figma, prototyping in code and AI-assisted workflows.

  • You are fluent in German and English.

Bonus: CAD, 3D, PLM, industrial software, AI agents or other highly technical products. None required.

HOW TO APPLY

Via Ashby with:

  • Your CV

  • Your portfolio – at least two case studies of complex B2B or AI products, showing your process, not just final screens

  • A link to something you prototyped in code or with AI tools – rough is fine

  • A 2-min intro video (any format you like)

  • A short answer to: "What is the most complex workflow you have simplified – what made it hard, and what did you decide to leave out?"

No recruiters, no portals.

Du arbeitest an der Schnittstelle von Produktmanagement, Qualitätsmanagement und Behördenkommunikation. Eng zusammen arbeitest du mit Learning Content Engineers, Sales, Marketing, Legal und der Geschäftsführung. Du verstehst die Logik des Fördersystems und übersetzt sie in Programme, die didaktisch überzeugen und sich wirtschaftlich tragen.

  • Du leitest die Zulassung und Re-Zertifizierung unserer Maßnahmen nach AZAV, gemeinsam mit der fachkundigen Stelle.

  • Du entwickelst förderfähige KI- und Data-Programme, die zu Kostensätzen, Dauer und Arbeitsmarktbedarf passen.

  • Du baust und pflegst die Zusammenarbeit mit Agenturen für Arbeit, Jobcentern und weiteren Förderstellen, damit unsere Maßnahmen in der Beratung bekannt sind und passend empfohlen werden.

  • Du gestaltest den Weg der Teilnehmenden von der Beratung bei der Arbeitsagentur über die Gutscheineinlösung bis zum Start und Abschluss der Maßnahme.

  • Du sorgst für saubere Prozesse bei Teilnahmedokumentation, Abrechnung mit den Kostenträgern und Nachweisen.

  • Du arbeitest mit Learning Content Engineers daran, Curricula, Prüfungen und Zertifikate an den Anforderungen der Förderung auszurichten.

  • Du arbeitest mit Sales und Marketing an Ansprache und Information für Interessent:innen, die mit Bildungsgutschein starten wollen.

  • Du verfolgst Vermittlungs- und Verbleibsquoten, Abbruchquoten, Teilnehmerfeedback und Änderungen im Förderrecht und leitest daraus Verbesserungen ab.

  • Du führst ein kleines Team oder koordinierst Kolleg:innen und externe Partner fachlich.

Das bringst du mit

  • Ein abgeschlossenes Studium, bevorzugt mit Bezug zu Bildungsmanagement, Wirtschaft oder Informatik, oder eine vergleichbare Qualifikation

  • Mehrjährige Erfahrung im Bereich geförderte Weiterbildung, idealerweise mit Kenntnis von AZAV, SGB III und dem Bildungsgutschein

  • Erfahrung in der Zusammenarbeit mit Agenturen für Arbeit, Jobcentern oder anderen Kostenträgern

  • Gutes Verständnis für KI- und Data-Themen und die Bereitschaft, dich in aktuelle Entwicklungen einzuarbeiten (Tiefe Programmierkenntnisse sind kein Muss.)

  • Erfahrung in Produkt-, Projekt- oder Qualitätsmanagement und im Planen und Priorisieren

  • Erste Erfahrung in fachlicher Führung oder in der Koordination von Teams und Partnern

  • Strukturierte Arbeitsweise und ein sicherer Umgang mit Vorgaben, Nachweisen und Fristen

  • Verhandlungssichere Deutsch- und gute Englischkenntnisse

Das bieten wir Dir

 

Arbeitskultur
Dich erwartet eine lösungsorientierte und datengetriebene Arbeitsweise, eine offene Feedbackkultur sowie ein starker Teamspirit. Zwei vom gesamten StackFuel-Team gewählte Trustees unterstützen Dich bei Fragen und Anliegen als neutrale, vertrauliche Anlaufstelle.

Ownership
Übernehme ab dem ersten Tag Verantwortung, bringe Deine eigenen Ideen aktiv ein, gestalte Prozesse nachhaltig und präge unsere Abläufe maßgeblich mit.

Hybrides Arbeiten
Wir arbeiten in einem hybriden Modell und sind üblicherweise 3 Tage pro Woche vor Ort in unserem Office in Berlin.

Bis zu 10 Tage pro Jahr kannst Du von überall aus der EU, dem EWR und der Türkei arbeiten.

Regelmäßiger Austausch im Team, saisonale Feiern und eine immer gut gefüllte Küche sorgen für ein lebendiges Miteinander.

title: Enterprise Customer Success Manager
description:
At Semperis, our mission is to be a Force for Good. Starting with being a great place to work. We believe that when people feel valued, supported, and empowered, they do their best work. That’s why we focus on creating an employee experience rooted in purpose, growth, and balance. Semperis has been recognized as one of America’s Fastest-Growing Cybersecurity Companies by the Inc. 5000, a DUNS 100 Top Startup to Work For, and a multi-year Inc. Best Workplace awardee.

What we are looking for:

Semperis is looking for a passionate and results-driven Enterprise Customer Success Manager to join our EMEA team.

What you will be doing:

As an Enterprise Customer Success Manager at Semperis, you will ensure your customers' success and satisfaction with our products and support them every step of the way. You will be an essential member of our Customer Success team, collaborating closely with cross-functional teams including Technical Delivery and Sales teams to maximise opportunities for our Enterprise Business customers and Semperis.

Our Customer Success Managers are strategic and empathetic communicators who can convey complex concepts in a clear and concise manner. Our CSM will build and nurture long-lasting relationships across multiple client accounts. Our CSM’s strengths include the ability to identify gaps in the product and internal operations and build effective and scalable solutions to address them. Our CSM will also onboard new customers, ensuring a smooth and successful implementation of our solutions.

You will be responsible for:

  • Design a success plan for a Book of Business of strategic customers throughout their lifecycle. From onboarding and implementation through upsell, cross-sell, and renewal, you will guide your customer down the path of success every step of the way to reach their business objectives and operational goals

  • You will be empowered to achieve and report on customer health, satisfaction, retention, and growth targets

  • Act as the voice of the customer, gather insights to provide feedback to internal teams including our Product Development team. Collaborate on new developments to ensure the product suits our client’s needs

  • Lead training sessions to ensure that the product is meeting user needs and is being used widely enough to have concrete impact on our customers' operations

  • Monitor record-keeping to ensure that relevant customer information is captured to enable informed, personalised customer interactions with Semperis Support, Customer Success (CS), Sales, etc

  • Develop and execute programs for ongoing customer development (health checks, product upgrades, workshops, etc.)

  • Identify potential customer references and assist with development of customer case studies

  • Gain and maintain an understanding of Semperis technology, products, and services

  • In addition to managing an assigned customer segment, assist with development and enhancement of processes and systems for the overall Semperis CS program

What you will bring to the table:

Technical & Cyber Security Skills

  • Hands-on product enablement experience with a security product vendor, including running product health checks, articulating the output with expertise, configuring or tuning alert and response rules, remediating Active Directory and Entra security posture vulnerabilities

  • Understanding of security concepts (NIST IR process, MITRE Attack framework, APTs, etc.) and workflows, Active Directory and Entra ID vulnerabilities and attack patterns, IAM and Security team organisation structures

  • Strong foundational knowledge of cyber security domains:

  • Network security, endpoint protection (EDR/XDR), cloud security (CSPM/CWPP), identity (IAM/SSO/MFA), SIEM, zero-trust, threat intelligence, etc

  • Fundamental understanding of modern architectures: on-prem and cloud (AWS, Azure, GCP)

  • Familiarity with compliance frameworks (NIST CSF, CIS, ISO 27001, PCI-DSS, HIPAA, GDPR, SOC 2)

Customer-facing & Soft Skills -

  • 5+ years’ experience as a Customer Success Manager, technical account manager, or related customer-facing role in a Cybersecurity SaaS solutions company

  • Executive presence & communication: can explain complex threats or product value to CISOs, CIOs, architects, and analysts in their language

  • Storytelling with data: Turn telemetry, risk scores, and attack surface metrics into compelling business narratives

  • Project/program management: Be in tune with customer onboarding, health checks, maturity roadmaps, and expansion opportunities

  • Conflict resolution & expectation management during incidents or escalations.

  • Consultative selling & value realization: Identify use cases that justify expansion, upsell & cross-sell modules, or multi-year renewals

Business & Strategic Skills:

  • Renewal & expansion forecasting (understand ARR, NRR, consumption metrics)

  • Ability to build and Execute Customer Success Plans / Joint Success Plans with Account owners (sales reps)

  • Risk identification (technical debt, low adoption, competing solutions) and mitigation planning (QBRs, escalation paths)

  • Competitive intelligence: Know how your product differentiates from the competition

Preferences:

  • Experience with SFDC and Active Directory

  • Fluent German and English language skills are required

You’ll be part of a global team on the front lines of cybersecurity innovation. At Semperis, we celebrate curiosity, integrity, and people who take initiative. title: Finance Lead (f/m/d)
description:
Description

We are building a Finance function that enables our next phase of growth – and we're looking for someone who wants to build it with us.

As our Finance Lead, you will take end-to-end ownership of our financial operations, laying the financial foundation for a scaling deep-tech hardware company. From accounting, reporting, controlling and treasury to public funding and the financial infrastructure supporting global equipment deliveries, you will play a central role in how QuantumDiamonds grows.

Reporting directly to the CEO, you will work closely with our leadership team, investors and external partners, translating business priorities into sound financial decisions and scalable processes.

This is a hands-on build role, not a position where you simply oversee an established Finance department. You will work with a lean team, take ownership of operational and strategic topics, and actively leverage technology, AI and automation to build an efficient Finance function that scales alongside the business.

We're looking for someone who brings strong Finance foundations, sound judgment, and the ambition to take on broader responsibilities as the company grows. You don't need to have done everything before – but you should be excited to figure things out, take ownership, and make things happen.

 

Who we are

Founded in 2022 as a spin-off of TU Munich, QD leverages quantum sensors to rapidly capture three-dimensional current maps within multi-layer chips. Our strong, international team of over 70, including physicists, engineers, data scientists, and other experts, works side by side with major semiconductor manufacturers, supporting chip debugging and accelerating yield analysis. Backed by top-tier deep tech investors, semiconductor experts, and strategic public programs, we have ensured long-term stability, shifting from breakthrough to scale - and shaping the next chapter in chip testing.

 

Why join QuantumDiamonds?

Picture this:

  • Quantum sensors that see inside the most advanced chips on Earth, right where two frontier fields collide.

  • Nobel-Prize physics aimed at real customers with real problems, in production now, not someday.

  • Physicists, data scientists, and engineers building side by side, turning deep science into tools the industry actually runs on.

  • An international team that runs at hard problems for fun, where knowledge moves fast and so do you.

Still unsure about why joining us?

  • You'll get to build a company together with a brilliant and welcoming team on a product that has never been done before.

  • From Day 1, you'll own your own topics end to end and see the direct impact of your work on how the world sees QuantumDiamonds.

  • Our technology is the cutting edge of tomorrow, starting today and not in 10 years.

  • You’ll be part of a high-growth company backed by top-tier investors.

Let’s make the invisible visible!

 
 

What will you do

  • Own our day-to-day financial operations, including accounting, controlling, financial reporting and compliance, in collaboration with external partners.

  • Drive budgeting, forecasting, cash flow planning and liquidity management, providing actionable financial insights across the business.

  • Work closely with the CEO on financing opportunities, including debt financing, fundraising, investor and board reporting.

Dafür gibt es diese Rolle. Du holst Conversion Rate Optimization ins Haus und baust Testing-Prozess und Roadmap neu auf: Landingpages, Produktseiten, Homepage, Cart und Checkout. Das Ziel ist klar: den Umsatz pro Besucher in den ersten 6–12 Monaten um 40–50 % steigern. Du nimmst Tests selbst live und rollst Gewinner selbst aus, ein eigener Entwickler setzt um.

Und du baust nicht nur für eine Marke. Supplement Hub vereint sieben Marken mit über 500 Produkten und rund 50–60 Mio. € Umsatz. Was in unserem größten Shop funktioniert, wird zum Playbook für die ganze Gruppe — mit der Perspektive, CRO gruppenweit zu verantworten.

Warum es diese Rolle gibt

Supplement Hub ist über starke Produkte und Amazon groß geworden. Im Direktgeschäft wächst unsere größte Marke schnell — mit über 200.000 Kund:innen. CRO lief bisher über eine Agentur. Das reicht für das, was jetzt kommt, nicht mehr: Mit jedem Euro mehr im Performance Marketing wird jeder Prozentpunkt Conversion wertvoller.

Deshalb holen wir das Thema ins Haus. Das DTC-Team wird gerade neu aufgebaut. Wir suchen niemanden, der Agentur-Ergebnisse durchwinkt, sondern jemanden, der die Zielgruppe so gut versteht, dass daraus Tests mit echtem Umsatzhebel entstehen.

Was du bewegen wirst

Nicht als Aufgabenliste, sondern als das, was in zwölf Monaten anders sein soll:

  • Du kennst die Zielgruppe besser als jeder Report. Bedürfnisse, Einwände und Kaufängste sind erforscht — mit Microsoft Clarity, Shop-Daten, Reviews und Umfragen — und fließen direkt in deine Hypothesen.

  • Die Shops verkaufen besser. Landingpages, Produktseiten, Cart und Checkout sind getestet und optimiert — Copy, Layout, Bundles und Angebote eingeschlossen.

  • Gewinner sind ausgerollt, Learnings dokumentiert. Jeder Test ist sauber ausgewertet und so festgehalten, dass er für die nächste Marke der Gruppe nutzbar ist.

  • Der Umsatz pro Besucher ist spürbar gestiegen — und du kannst genau zeigen, welche Tests dazu beigetragen haben.

Wie hier gearbeitet wird

Supplement Hub ist effizienzgetrieben: Calls gibt es, wenn sie nötig sind, Entscheidungen fallen in Tagen.

  • Ein Entwickler baut deine Tests technisch und pflegt sie in Intelligems ein. Du konzipierst, er setzt um.

Wen wir suchen

Wir suchen keinen perfekten Lebenslauf, sondern einen Nachweis: Du hast die Conversion eines Onlineshops schon einmal messbar gesteigert — mit eigenen Tests.

  • Mindestens zwei bis drei Jahre operative CRO- oder E-Commerce-Verantwortung bei einer D2C-Marke im Konsumgüterbereich — etwa Supplements, Health, Beauty, Food oder Fashion.

Die Vorteile für dich

This is account-led selling rather than opportunity-led. You run each account like a business, over years rather than quarters.

We are early. The strategic motion is new, and you will shape it alongside a small group of senior sellers and n8n leadership. If you are looking for a fully built territory and a playbook to follow, this is not it. If you want to be one of the people who builds it, read on:

OWN A NAMED PORTFOLIO

BUILD THE STRATEGIC MOTION

  • Shoot. Assist on every shoot: podcast recordings, product videos, webinars, livestreams and full conference days. Rig cameras, lights and audio, operate a camera, and manage media on set.

  • Cut the podcast. Deliver first-pass edits of AI Native Dev episodes, ready for review.

  • Make social cuts. Turn long edits into short clips built for YouTube, LinkedIn and other social channels.

  • Finish the picture and sound. Edit, color correct and grade, edit and mix audio, pick music and create captions.

  • Publish. Schedule finished episodes and videos to podcast platforms, YouTube and our social channels.

  • Automate the boring parts. Use and extend our AI-assisted post-production pipeline (transcripts, captions, clip finding, publishing assets), and build your own automations wherever you spot repetitive work.

  • Proof you can shoot and cut. A short reel, a few clips, a YouTube channel or a uni project that shows basic competence behind the camera and in the edit.

  • Camera range. You're comfortable shooting on a wide range of cameras, and you know your way around lighting and sound on set.

  • The software stack. You're comfortable in Adobe Premiere Pro, After Effects, Photoshop and Audition, DaVinci Resolve and Figma.

  • A pro-AI attitude. You already use AI tools in your work, and you're comfortable building and running AI automations to speed up your own workflow.

  • Curiosity and drive. You ask good questions, pick things up fast and pitch in wherever you're needed, from carrying flight cases to cutting a trailer.

  • Some experience. Around 1 to 2 years in production or editing (in a job, freelance or self-taught) is typical for this role, but it isn't a hard requirement.

Nice to have

  • The Blackmagic ecosystem, in depth. Cinema cameras, ATEM switchers, HyperDeck recorders and Blackmagic RAW workflows through to Resolve.

  • Live production. Vision mixing, multicam recording or running a livestream.

  • Motion graphics. Titles, lower thirds and simple animation in After Effects.

  • Curiosity about software and AI. You'll be filming developers talking about AI coding agents every week, so it helps if you want to understand what they're saying.

Send us three things. A polished portfolio isn't required.

  1. Your CV.

  2. A link to 2 to 5 minutes of your work (a reel, YouTube, Vimeo or a Drive folder), with a line on what you shot and what you edited.

  3. A few sentences on one AI tool or automation you use in your video work, and what it saves you.

Life at Tessl

We want Tessl to be a place where you can do meaningful work, keep learning and enjoy being part of the team. Alongside competitive compensation, we offer benefits designed to support you both inside and outside work.

 

What we offer

  • Competitive compensation and equity: Market-benchmarked salaries and EMI share options.

  • Time off: 25 days of annual leave, plus UK public holidays, and two paid volunteering days each year.

  • Private healthcare: Vitality medical insurance, including dental, optical and mental health support, with cover included for partners and dependants.

  • Pension: A 5% employer pension matched contribution through Smart Pension.

  • Life assurance: Company-paid life insurance with MetLife providing cover of four times your annual salary.

  • Family Leave: We offer enhanced Maternity, Parental and Adoption Leave from day one to support you and your growing family.

  • Learning and development: We support opportunities to continue developing your skills with a £1,000 per year to spend.

  • Commuting benefits: Financial support for eligible team members commuting from outside Greater London, plus a Cycle to Work scheme.

  • Summer & winter offsites: Twice a year, we bring the whole Tessl team together for a week-long offsite. It's a chance to step away from our usual routines, collaborate on big ideas, build stronger relationships and enjoy shared experiences together. And of course, we have a lot of fun along the way!

     

Our London HQ

Our office is in the heart of King's Cross, surrounded by London's growing AI and technology community.

We work together in person on Mondays, Tuesdays and Thursdays, giving us time to collaborate, exchange ideas and build relationships. You'll also enjoy catered lunches (Tuesday & Thursday), plenty of office snacks, regular team lunches and socials, plus a pet-friendly workplace.

How we work

Our operating principles shape how we collaborate and make decisions. We move quickly and learn by doing, build on ideas before challenging them, get stuck in wherever we can help, and give people real ownership. We encourage thoughtful debate, curiosity and a willingness to try things that haven't been done before. Read our five operating principles.

We're AI native

AI isn't just what we're building - it's central to how we work every day, across every function. We actively use AI to improve how we work, solve problems and challenge traditional ways of doing things.

You don't need to be an AI expert to thrive at Tessl, but you do need curiosity, an appetite for experimentation and a willingness to embrace new ways of working. We expect everyone to use AI regularly, invest time in learning how to get the most from it and keep experimenting when something doesn't work the first time, rather than defaulting to manual approaches.

We're also big believers in sharing what we learn. We encourage transparency about how we're using AI, what's working, what isn't and how we can help each other improve. Being AI native doesn't mean removing human judgement, it means using AI thoughtfully, while taking ownership of the quality and outcomes of our work.

Everyone is welcome at Tessl

We're committed to building an inclusive environment where people from different backgrounds, experiences and perspectives can thrive.

We particularly welcome applications from people who are underrepresented in technology. If you're excited about the opportunity but don't meet every requirement, we'd still encourage you to apply.

If you need any adjustments or additional support during the recruitment process, please let us know. We're happy to work with you to make the process accessible and comfortable.

Come build with us

We're moving fast, experimenting boldly and figuring things out as we go. There's plenty to build, lots to learn and real opportunities to make your mark.

If you're excited by big ideas, enjoy getting stuck in and want to be part of something from the ground up, we'd love to hear from you!
