title: Senior AI Architect & Consultant (m/w/d)
description:
Wer wir sind

Die Mayflower GmbH baut Individualsoftware mit Fokus auf Generative AI – seit 1998 inhabergeführt.

Wir bringen komplette AI-Infrastrukturen in Produktion: Model-Serving, Agent-Gateways, Chat und Voice – direkt in der Umgebung des Kunden. Dich erwartet ein agiles Arbeitsumfeld mit echter Verantwortung und flachen Strukturen – Entscheidungen triffst Du selbst, statt sie durch Freigabeschleifen zu schieben.

Wir suchen Dich – jemanden, der AI-Systeme nicht nur konzipiert, sondern ihren Weg in die Produktion aktiv mitverantwortet. Von der Architekturberatung auf C-Level bis zum Produktivbetrieb: Du entwirfst die Lösung und bringst sie mit dem Team in den echten Einsatz.

Was dich erwartet

  • Anspruchsvolle Projekte mit LLMs, Agentic RAG und AI-Agent-Frameworks (z. B. LangGraph, PydanticAI, Mastra oder OpenAI Agents SDK) – inklusive Deep-Agent-Architekturen. Du baust Evaluation-Pipelines und Observability (Logging/Tracing mit LangSmith, Langfuse o. Ä.) auf und arbeitest mit modernem MLOps-Stack sowie Vector Databases.
  • Du entwirfst Lösungsarchitekturen für komplexe Kundenvorhaben – mit Security, Compliance, Skalierbarkeit und Datenschutz im Hinterkopf – von der ersten Skizze im Gespräch bis zur konkreten Roadmap.
  • Gemeinsam im Team führst Du Deep-Dive-Calls und Workshops mit Kunden durch und bringst sie in die nächste Projektphase.
  • Du begleitest die Anbahnung neuer Projekte und unterstützt unser Team im Pre-Sales mit technischer Glaubwürdigkeit.
  • Du kommunizierst souverän auf C-Level – Du verstehst ökonomische Ziele, sprichst die Sprache von Entscheider:innen und verbindest technische Exzellenz mit Business-Impact.
  • Der Schwerpunkt Deiner Rolle liegt mit etwa 50 % in Kundenprojekten, in intensiven Phasen auch darüber. Den übrigen Teil Deiner Zeit investierst Du in Pre-Sales-Gespräche und Workshops, die Du vorbereitest und durchführst, sowie in die strategische Unterstützung von Geschäftsführung und Sales.
  • Konferenzen, Community-Events, Fachbeiträge: Präsenz ist ein Plus, keine Bedingung. Wichtig ist uns nur, dass Du bereit bist, Dich fachlich zu zeigen.
  • Du reist 4–8 Tage im Monat zu Kunden und Kolleg:innen – Reisebereitschaft innerhalb Deutschlands, bei Bedarf auch in Österreich und der Schweiz, ist Teil der Rolle.

Das solltest du mitbringen

  • Langjährige Erfahrung als Architekt:in oder Senior Engineer, idealerweise bei einem Dienstleister oder in der IT-Beratung.
  • Projekterfahrung mit Agentic-AI-Implementierungen, die über Prototypen hinausgeht: LangChain, LangGraph und Deep Agents im echten Einsatz – oder vergleichbare Tiefe im TypeScript-Umfeld (Mastra) bzw. im Microsoft-Ökosystem (Semantic Kernel / Microsoft Agent Framework, Azure AI Foundry). Vector Databases und MLOps sind ein Plus.
  • Die Kompetenz, Kunden AI-Konzepte und Architekturen anschaulich und praxisnah zu vermitteln.
  • Du kannst Lösungen im Kundengespräch skizzieren und überzeugend vertreten – Storytelling und Präsenz sind Deine Stärken.

Die Mayflower GmbH baut Individualsoftware mit Fokus auf Generative AI – seit 1998 inhabergeführt.

  • Kompetitive Vergütung: Je nach Erfahrung und Kompetenz vergüten wir die Stelle mit einem Bruttojahresgehalt von 80.000 € bis 90.000 € bei 40 Wochenstunden.

  • Kundenbeziehung auf Augenhöhe: Wir pflegen eine ehrliche und vertrauensvolle Zusammenarbeit mit unseren Kunden.
  • Mache einen Unterschied: Viel Verantwortung, großer Gestaltungsspielraum - in einem Mittelständler, in dem dein Beitrag den wirtschaftlichen Erfolg direkt beeinflusst.
  • Lerne immer dazu: Weiterbildung (intern und extern), Training-on-the-job und regelmäßige Weiterentwicklungs- und Gehaltsgespräche.
  • Wie arbeiten selbstorganisiert: Wir geben dir den Freiraum, den Rahmen für gute Arbeit selbst mitzugestalten – im Team wie beim Kunden.

At Zego, we're on a mission to do the good thing, not the insurance thing.

Insurance hasn't changed much in over a century. The way we live, work and travel has. We're building the real-time, AI-driven infrastructure that powers innovative insurance, so good drivers get cover that works the way they actually drive.

We're not just updating insurance; We're leading the AI evolution in insurance 🤖

We don't do things slowly, and we don't do bureaucracy. We back high-performance builders who want ownership, early responsibility and the chance to do the most career-defining work of their lives. You'll get the space to try things, the tools to move fast, and the room to see your ideas reach millions of drivers.

Do not take our word for it. Read what Zegons say about us on Glassdoor.

If you're ready to build the future of insurance, we're hiring.

About the team

Zego’s Data team delivers high-impact projects across the whole business - from AI tools that let anyone query data and publish dashboards in Zego Lens, to the customer insights that shape our growth strategy.

We already have established data science teams in Pricing and Telematics. This is the first data science role in our central Data team, focused on the huge untapped potential across the rest of the business - from experimentation to churn, marketing and fraud. We’re a fast-moving disruptor in insurance, driven by great tech products and data. We adopt new technology quickly - we’re AI-first, so most of our code is now written by AI and reviewed by people.

About the role

As our first Lead Product Data Scientist, you’ll shape how Zego makes its biggest product and commercial decisions. You’ll work directly with senior leaders across Product, Growth and Operations to decide where to focus, which bets to back and how we’ll know they’ve worked.

You’ll start by building the foundations - a trusted experimentation framework and customer models that tell us who to acquire, how to engage them and where to invest. As teams learn to run routine experiments themselves, your focus will shift to guiding product investment and making sure evidence, rather than intuition, drives our roadmap.

This is a senior, hands-on role with real scope to shape a new capability - and the chance to use AI to scale data science across a growing business.

What you will be doing

  • Work with senior leaders to embed data science in strategy and decision making. Create and own a prioritised roadmap for where data science can have the biggest impact.

  • Own Zego’s experimentation framework - design standards, power, guardrail metrics and decision rules. Coach teams to run routine experiments themselves.

  • Partner with Product teams before anything is built, shaping ideas into evidence-based hypotheses and well-designed experiments. Apply causal inference where randomised tests aren’t possible.

  • Build models of customer behaviour across the lifecycle - acquisition, conversion, retention, churn and lifetime value - with teams such as Marketing and Fraud.

  • Use AI to scale data science across Zego, automating experiment analysis and readouts. Build self-serve tools that help teams sharpen their hypotheses.

  • Take the most impactful models into production with our ML Platform team.

  • Set technical direction and mentor analysts and data scientists as the capability grows.

What you’ll need

  • Significant data science experience in a product-led business, with a track record of work that changed product or commercial decisions.

  • Strong executive presence - you influence senior leaders, challenge decisions with evidence and explain results clearly to any audience.

  • Expertise in experimentation and causal inference, with many online experiments designed and analysed.

  • Experience building customer models such as churn, propensity, LTV or segmentation - and getting them used in real decisions.

  • Strong Python and SQL, with confidence working AI-first (and the judgement to spot when AI output is wrong).

  • Experience taking models into production on AWS SageMaker or a similar ML platform.

Nice to have

  • Familiarity with experimentation or product analytics platforms such as Statsig or Amplitude.

  • Experience with Snowflake, dbt and Looker or a similar modern data stack.

  • Experience of marketing measurement such as media mix modelling or incrementality testing.

  • A background in insurance, fintech or another regulated or subscription business.

Teams work better with time to collaborate and space to get things done. We call it Zego Hybrid: some of us are in our office (central London, Gibraltar or Halifax) weekly, others monthly or quarterly. It's about finding the balance between face time and focus that produces great work and a healthy life around it.

Investa is building the UK’s first zero-commission Options and Stocks trading platform. Legacy platforms typically feature high fees and complex interfaces that cut out the majority of retail investors. We are building a streamlined alternative to fix that. Investa is the first FCA-regulated platform to offer completely free US share trading with no FX, no commission, and no other fees.

Our Traction So Far:

  • £3.5M+ raised in funding with 1,000+ shareholders backing our vision

  • FCA-regulated and multi-award winning in 2026: Best Options Trading App (Good Money Guide) & Best App for Options Trading (ADVFN)

  • Available on iOS and Android, scaling rapidly toward our next milestones of 10,000 and 100,000 active users

  • 8,000+ trades processed, 2,500+ early supporters rewarded, and 150+ 5-star reviews

Our Mission: To democratise options trading for UK investors

Our Vision: Think Options, Think Investa

We are a lean, agile team where every employee directly shapes the business. We don't have a corporate way of working. Instead, we look for people who want high autonomy, care about making a visible impact, and align with our core values of being Collaborative, Curious, and Creative.

We are growing and looking for ambitious talent to help us democratise retail investing across the UK.

The Role

As our Risk & Controls Operations Associate, you will serve as the first line of regulatory and operational control for Investa’s platform. Working together with our Head of Risk & Compliance and Co-Founders, you will help own the day-to-day execution of our key operational controls spanning CASS oversight, onboarding operations, financial crime monitoring, and execution control.

This is a critical, high-visibility role within a fast-scaling financial trading environment. You will bridge regulatory oversight with practical execution: verifying client money flows, resolving dealing and onboarding exceptions, and ensuring our operations adhere strictly to FCA standards as our operating model expands from sub-account clearing into in-house custody and scales UK retail options trading. Rather than running a static checklist, you'll help build and refine our operational controls and CASS processes as we launch new products.

What the role involves

1. Risk & Control Operations

  • CASS Reconciliations: Perform daily internal & external CASS reconciliations across Investa’s client base to prevent breaches and ensure compliance with day-to-day CASS obligations.

  • CASS Reporting & Audits: Maintain audit-ready compliance records, log breaks and CASS breaches, and assist in preparing regulatory returns and notifications when needed.

  • KYC & Onboarding Operations: Own the day-to-day onboarding queue, performing KYC/AML document reviews, appropriateness assessments, and managing PEPs, sanctions, and high-risk escalations.

  • Financial Crime Monitoring: Organise high-risk client reviews assisting with enhanced due diligence, source of funds/wealth checks, and periodic and event driven reviews.

  • Vulnerable Customer Framework: Manage sensitive customer cases as identified in the vulnerable clients policy, ensure good outcomes for clients with support needs, manage key performance indicators for clients in this segment in strict compliance with Consumer Duty standards and internal policies.

2. Business Oversight & Governance Support

  • Management Information: Own and gather key performance indicators covering all aspects of the business for committee reporting and oversight.

  • Financial Promotions: Review and approve marketing campaigns, product copy, and social media promotions to ensure strict alignment with FCA Financial Promotion and Consumer Duty rules.

  • Regulatory Change: Assist in implementation of regulatory change in the UK or elsewhere to ensure compliance with new rules that apply to the Firm.

  • Third Party Risk Management: Point of contact for vendors and outsourcing partners to oversee and coordinate information sharing for incident closure & customer support.

  • Trade surveillance: Provide first line review of alerts generated through trade surveillance for signs of market abuse. Oversee the closure of alerts and applicable audit trail.

Your Background

  • 2+ years of hands-on experience covering trade operations or controls support at a regulated firm, FinTech, investment platform, or broker.

  • Understanding of the regulatory framework surrounding CASS, Consumer Duty, Systems & Controls, and Anti-Money Laundering.

  • Direct experience executing CASS reconciliation workflows, client adoption, and trade surveillance.

  • Strong analytical mindset with high attention to detail and sound, practical judgement.

  • Technical proficiency in Office and Google-based software including excel, Google Sheets, Google Docs.

Desirable

  • Prior exposure to retail investment platforms, derivatives markets.

  • Experience using workflow tools like Jira or case management software.

  • Familiarity with third-party clearing integrations (e.g., Interactive Brokers) or regulatory reporting tools.

  • CISI or equivalent qualification regarding financial services, client assets, or regulatory modules.

  • Understanding of EU regulation.

  • Career Ownership & Impact: You have autonomy over your execution and your career trajectory. Your work impacts the business immediately without corporate red tape.   • Annual Leave: 30 days (including bank holidays) + your birthday off.

  • Premium Coverage: Private medical and dental insurance via Bupa.

  • The Office: Work from a vibrant, spacious office featuring a private gym and a rooftop terrace for fresh-air breaks.

  • Fuel & Socials: Enjoy tea, coffee and snacks daily. Every last Wednesday of the month, we host a Team Lunch where the menu is chosen by the staff. We also run regular team socials, alongside company and individual milestone celebrations.

Tech 💻

Who are Veezu?

Veezu is the UK's fastest growing taxi and private hire technology business operating across hundreds of UK towns and cities. We are a tech-driven on-demand mobility service that supports our hyper-local communities, helping them thrive and so much more!

  • Support recruitment, onboarding and training of new team members.

  • Ensure processes, guidance and knowledge resources remain up to date.

Skills & Experience Required

  • Proven experience in complaints handling, passenger resolution or passenger service management.

  • Experience managing complex or escalated complaints.

  • Experience leading or managing teams.

  • Strong passenger focus with the ability to balance empathy and commercial decision-making.

  • Excellent investigation, analytical and problem-solving skills.

  • Strong written and verbal communication skills.

title: Assistant Controller
description:
About MUBI

MUBI is a global streaming service, production company and film distributor dedicated to elevating great cinema. To make this possible, we create, curate, acquire and champion visionary films, bringing them to audiences all over the world. We have a team of brilliant, dedicated and passionate people to help bring our mission to life. From London to New York, Istanbul to Paris, and Berlin to Mexico - we work together to realize MUBI’s vision.

That’s where you come in! Join our global team and help us make great cinema accessible to everyone, everywhere.

About the Role

MUBI is looking for an Assistant Controller to lead our group accounting and financial reporting function from London. Reporting to the Global Controller, you will own the US GAAP close and consolidation, lead group financial reporting and the day-to-day delivery of our Big Four group audit, and oversee statutory accounting across our international entities.

You will directly manage our senior statutory accounting leads. This is a hands-on leadership role: you will stay close enough to the detail to resolve issues and set a high bar for accuracy, while also developing the team, strengthening controls and improving how we close, report and operate.

Your initial mandate is focused on group and statutory accounting. Cash and treasury operations and payroll will initially remain outside your remit. Once the core accounting mandate is firmly established, we expect the role to broaden over time to include greater oversight of cash and treasury. We are therefore looking for someone who already brings meaningful experience in these areas.

You will work closely with the Global Controller on complex accounting matters, systems and automation, controls and the continued development of the function. MUBI's accounting environment spans subscription streaming, film distribution and production across multiple entities, countries and currencies. We are looking for someone who learned the fundamentals in Big Four audit and has since applied them in-house, with the judgement and experience to operate effectively across this complexity as the business continues to grow.

We work hybrid-remote where we require 3 office days in London. Our core days are Tuesday, Wednesday & Thursday, with the flexibility to use our offices on the remaining two days if you wish.

Where you’ll have impact:

  • Own the close and consolidation. Lead the month-, quarter- and year-end close and consolidation process across all entities, including review of journal entries, accruals, reconciliations, eliminations and other key close outputs.

  • Lead financial reporting. Prepare and review consolidated US GAAP financial statements, management reporting packs and supporting schedules, ensuring group reporting is accurate, timely and well supported.

  • Own key accounting areas. Oversee accounting for content assets, subscription and distribution revenue, deferred revenue, partner and app-store settlements, intercompany balances and foreign currency. Work with FP&A, content and other teams where accounting depends on operational data or business context.

  • Oversee global statutory accounting. Directly manage our senior statutory accounting leads and coordinate statutory reporting across the group, working with local teams and external advisers to ensure statutory accounts and filings are complete, accurate and delivered on time.

  • Lead the audit. Manage the day-to-day delivery of the Big Four group audit and coordinate statutory audits across our entities. Build an effective relationship with our auditors and advisers and ensure requests and deliverables are well supported and resolved promptly.

  • Strengthen controls and processes. Document and improve accounting processes and SOPs, strengthen key close and reporting controls, and help develop the control environment toward public-company and SOX standards.

  • Partner on technical accounting. Work with the Global Controller and external advisers on new or complex accounting matters, helping translate technical conclusions into clear accounting policies and treatment.

  • Improve systems and automation. Lead improvements to our accounting systems, close and reporting workflows. Use automation and AI where they can materially improve accuracy, speed and efficiency.

What you’ll bring:

  • Active US CPA licence. You hold an active US CPA licence and bring strong practical knowledge of US GAAP.

  • Big Four and in-house experience. You have at least eight years of accounting experience, including meaningful Big Four audit experience and at least two years in an in-house accounting role, ideally within a complex, multi-entity international business.

  • Close and consolidation expertise. You have owned or played a senior role in month-, quarter- and year-end close and group consolidation, including the preparation or review of financial statements, with a strong understanding of the GL and end-to-end financial reporting process.

  • Strong people leadership. You have at least three years of experience managing and developing accounting professionals and are comfortable leading experienced team members across different countries and areas of responsibility.

  • Audit and controls experience. You have acted as a senior company-side contact for external auditors and have experience documenting, operating and improving internal financial controls.

  • International statutory experience. You have overseen statutory accounting and reporting across multiple jurisdictions and know how to work effectively with local finance teams, advisers and auditors without needing to be the technical expert in every market.

  • Meaningful cash and treasury experience. You have practical experience with the core disciplines of cash and treasury in a multi-entity business, including cash reporting or forecasting, banking operations, payment controls and bank reconciliations.

  • Strong systems and process capability. You have experience with NetSuite, Ramp and other finance and accounting systems, plus advanced Excel skills.

  • Clear judgement and communication. You have strong attention to detail, can move comfortably between accounting detail and the wider business context, communicate clearly with senior stakeholders, and manage competing priorities under tight deadlines.

  • You have the right to work in the UK and are able to work in person from our London office.

title: Senior Manager, Product Partnerships
description:
About Us

Perk (formerly TravelPerk) is the intelligent platform for travel and spend management. Built to tackle the time-consuming, manual work that gets in the way of real work, our tools automate everything from travel bookings to expenses, invoice processing, and more. By eliminating this shadow work that wastes hours, erodes morale, and saps innovation, we're on a mission to power real work, with real impact.

We're trusted by more than 12,000 companies worldwide, including Bolt, GoCardless, and Fabletics, and we're tackling the 7 hours of lost productivity per employee each week, a $1.7 trillion problem.

Founded in 2015, Perk has grown into a global company of more than 1,800 people across 12 offices globally, with headquarters in London and Boston. We combine innovation, control, and simplicity to transform how businesses work and how people feel at work.

At Perk, we're driven by our values, like being an owner, delivering a 7-star experience, and working as one team. We value curiosity, purpose, and mindset, not just knowledge, to unlock the power in your potential. Our talent team brings together leading minds from the travel, fintech, and SaaS industries, representing over 70 countries. If you're excited about having a real impact and shaping how millions of people experience work, we'd love you on the team.

Visit www.perk.com to learn more.

About the Role

Perk works best when it connects seamlessly with the tools and platforms our customers

already rely on. From ERP and accounting systems to workplace software, mobility providers,

technology platforms, and emerging AI ecosystems, these third-party relationships can directly

shape the value customers get from Perk.

We’re looking for a Senior Manager, Product Partnerships to own and build those relationships.

Unlike our Growth Partnerships and Supplier Partnerships teams, this role isn’t responsible for

generating sales pipeline or supplier commission revenue. Its goal is to make Perk’s product

and customer experience stronger through the third parties we depend on and integrate with.

You’ll determine where strategic relationships can unlock the most customer value, build and

manage those partnerships, secure the access and agreements our teams need, and work

closely with Product and Engineering to turn them into successful customer-facing experiences.

This is a new role at Perk with significant opportunity to define how Product Partnerships should

work as we scale.

What You’ll Do

  • Build our product partnership strategy: Translate Perk’s product and company priorities into a clear roadmap of third-party relationships across areas such as ERP and accounting, business software, mobility, integration platforms, and AI.

  • Own strategic partner relationships: Serve as Perk’s primary relationship owner for the external platforms and technology companies that enable or enhance customer-facing product experiences.

  • Unlock Product and Engineering: Secure the developer access, API licences, programme memberships, certifications, marketplace approvals, and other partner support our teams need to build and maintain integrations.

  • Structure and negotiate partnerships: Lead commercial and strategic discussions around API access, data, licensing, marketplace participation, co-marketing, and other partnership terms, working closely with Legal, Security, Finance, Product, and Engineering.

  • Partner with Product on priorities: Bring the partner and market perspective into roadmap discussions while Product Managers own product requirements and delivery. Help determine which external relationships and integration models create the greatest customer value.

  • Own the partner lifecycle: Manage relationships from initial engagement through integration, certification, launch, ongoing roadmap alignment, escalations, programme changes, and renewals.

  • Drive adoption and customer value: Work with Product, Marketing, Customer Success, Sales, and Support to ensure partnerships aren’t simply launched—they are discoverable, useful, reliable, and adopted by customers.

  • Build the Product Partnerships playbook: Establish how Perk evaluates, prioritises, launches, measures, and manages product partnerships as this function grows.

What We’re Looking For

  • Proven experience in strategic partnerships, ecosystem partnerships, business development, or a product-adjacent role within SaaS, fintech, or B2B technology.

  • Experience building and managing complex relationships with technology or platform companies, ideally including developer, API, certification, or marketplace programmes.

  • Comfortable working with Product and Engineering and understanding technical concepts such as APIs, OAuth, data models, sandboxes, and integration dependencies without needing to be an engineer.

  • Ability to distinguish between an interesting partnership and one that will meaningfully improve Perk’s product or customer experience.

  • Strong relationship-building, negotiation, and communication skills across both external partners and senior internal stakeholders.

  • Able to move complex initiatives forward across Product, Engineering, Legal, Security, Finance, Marketing, Customer Success, Support, and Sales without relying on direct authority.

  • Comfortable defining the strategy, operating model, priorities, and processes for a new function rather than inheriting an established playbook.

  • Able to build the case for a partnership and measure its impact through adoption, customer experience, integration quality, and other relevant outcomes.

  • Based within commuting distance of our London or Barcelona hub.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with ERP, accounting, spend management, payments, travel, or fintech ecosystems.

  • Experience managing relationships with major business software, technology, mobility, or AI platforms.

  • Familiarity with unified API or integration-platform models.

  • Experience with European ERP and accounting ecosystems across markets such as DACH, Benelux, France, the Nordics, or the UK.

  • Additional European languages.

 

What We Offer

  • Receive competitive compensation and equity ownership in Perk

  • Rest and recharge with 25 days of annual leave plus bank holidays

  • Take control of your physical health with private medical cover and voluntary dental insurance from Bupa, and discounted gym memberships with GymFlex

  • Plan for your future with our qualifying earnings company pension plan with Aviva

  • Know that your loved ones are protected financially through your Life Insurance if the worst were to happen

  • Rest assured that you’re covered by income protection in case you experience a long-term sickness or absence

  • Leverage tax-efficient cycle and electric car schemes with Cycle2Work & Octopus

  • Join our unforgettable Perk events, including our spectacular annual summer party

  • Always feel supported with Spring Health, our market-leading wellbeing partner, providing fast, comprehensive access to 12x therapy and 12x coaching sessions for you and your loved ones

  • Focus on your family with 12-16 weeks’ paid parental leave

  • Contribute to your community with 16 paid hours per year to spend volunteering for your dearest charitable causes

  • Broaden your horizons with up to 20 "Work from Anywhere" days per year

  • Stay savvy with access to a wide variety of discounts and rewards

  • Follow your passions and take a four-week, fully paid sabbatical once you reach 5 years

  • Let us help you move to one of our hubs with relocation support

The Process

  • Hiring Manager Interview - 30 mins - Virtual

  • Values interview - 30 mins - Virtual

AI at Perk
AI is embedded in how we work across every function. The tools you'll use day-to-day are AI-enabled so you can move faster and spend more time on the work that matters. In practice, that means using AI to research and prioritise accounts, draft and refine outreach, handle customer interactions more effectively, synthesise information, and cut through shadow work - the invisible tasks that pull people away from the work only they can do - so you can focus on relationships and outcomes.

How We Work

At Perk, we take an IRL-first approach to work, where our team works together in-person 3 days a week. As such, this role requires you to be based within commuting distance of our hubs. We fundamentally believe in the value of meeting in real life to improve connectivity, productivity, creativity and ultimately making us a great place to work.

Perk is a global company with a diverse customer base, and we want to make sure the people behind our product reflect that. We’re an equal opportunity employer, which means you’re welcome at Perk regardless of how you look, where you’re from, or anything else that makes you, well, you.

Protect Yourself from Recruitment Scams

About the Venture:

Complaints are changing faster than the teams that handle them. Generative AI makes complaints longer and easier to file: the Financial Ombudsman says up to a third of responses to its initial assessments now look AI-generated, and it has seen 200-page submissions in reply to an eight-page decision. Soon personal agents will file and chase complaints for people, so one event becomes several. UK financial services firms received 1.85 million complaints in the first half of 2026, up 6.3%, and a human still has to read and check every one. Every ombudsman referral can cost a firm £680.

It isn't only financial complaints. New kinds of regulated requests are arriving that no off-the-shelf tool handles well, such as waves of GDPR data requests from job candidates a company never hired. Each one raises the same questions: why is this happening, do we have to respond, and how do we respond fairly and on time?

We are building the AI desk that handles them. It splits a long complaint or request into its separate claims, checks each one against the policy, the customer's records and the rules, and drafts a fair, cited response within the deadline, with a handler always making the decision. We are building the layer that lets agents buy together. title: Tritium Process Engineers
description:
About Tritium Fuel Cycle (TFC)

GFG is designing a first-of-a-kind (FOAK) fusion power plant (FPP) to deliver 1 GW of electrical power in the 2040s. The “GIGA” plant will be based on a stellarator magnetic confinement fusion device, operating continuously on a deuterium-tritium (D-T) fuel cycle.  Prior to this, the smaller “Gauss Industrial Demonstrator (GID-170)” will be deployed in the mid-2030s.

While deuterium can be extracted from seawater, tritium is a tightly controlled radioactive isotope with an extremely limited global supply. Therefore, both GID-170 and GIGA must utilise closed tritium fuel cycle infrastructure, to ensure that unburnt tritium is fully recycled back to the stellarator and not released to the environment. Meanwhile, the tritium consumed by the fusion reaction must be replenished using tritium breeding blankets (TBB).

A first-of-a-kind dedicated tritium fuel cycle (TFC) facility, suitable for continuously supporting a stellarator device, must be designed, built and commissioned. It will adopt a multi-loop process architecture, each loop comprising many deeply integrated subsystems. Developing such a facility presents unique engineering challenges: the supply chain is still emerging, commercial process simulation tools lack dedicated TFC libraries, suitable off-the-shelf equipment is not always available, and some technologies have relatively low technology readiness levels (TRLs). 

A conceptual design is currently under development, with the project then progressing into pre-front-end engineering design (pre-FEED) in 2028, followed by front-end engineering design (FEED) and design for manufacturing phases. Completion of the overall design phase (for GID-170) must be achieved by 2032.


About the role

GFG is looking for several Tritium Process Engineers to join the TFC department and develop the GID-170 and GIGA TFC facilities. The roles will contribute to the continued development and optimisation of the overall fuel cycle architecture and its subsystems. Activities will include managing design requirements; developing process flow diagrams (PFDs), piping and instrumentation diagrams (P&IDs), heat and mass balances (HMBs) and the Basis of Design (BoD); selecting technologies; sizing and arranging equipment; and contributing to safety-related design. The roles may also involve supporting equipment prototype development and testing with technology developers and research partners.
We welcome candidates with complementary strengths in process design and process modelling and simulation, with systems engineering experience also desirable. These specialisations sit within the same engineering function, and candidates are not expected to have equal expertise across all areas. The number of appointments and balance of responsibilities will reflect the successful candidates’ experience and technical strengths. Drawing on their specialist expertise, successful candidates will work collaboratively on design development, modelling, analysis and optimisation to assess design alternatives and inform robust, well-documented design decisions.
The TFC comprises a wide range of technologies and subsystems, requiring the department to manage multiple sub-projects and work packages in parallel. Each engineer will contribute across several activities and will be expected to take ownership of specific tasks or subsystems, or lead work packages, depending on their experience. The roles will involve close collaboration with engineers from the same and other disciplines at national and international partner organisations, research institutions and suppliers, as well as with colleagues across disciplines and departments within GFG. Given the specific challenges associated with tritium, close collaboration with Nuclear Safety and Export Control specialists will also be essential.
During conceptual design, successful candidates will work closely with the Head of Tritium Fuel Cycle to address the strong interdependencies between subsystems and develop a coherent, integrated design. As the project moves into pre-FEED, they will be expected to take greater day-to-day ownership of their assigned areas and drive design development through pre-FEED and FEED, while maintaining close coordination across subsystem interfaces. As the project progresses, the roles will evolve to support design for manufacture, procurement and commissioning of the GID-170 TFC systems, followed by further development and refinement of the TFC design for GIGA.


Main responsibilities

  • Process definition and systems engineering
    1. Identify, define and manage system requirements and interfaces across TFC subsystems and the overall plant architecture.
    2. Develop and optimise the fuel cycle architecture, assessing alternative subsystem technologies, their respective advantages and disadvantages, technology readiness levels (TRLs), and potential system configurations.
    3. Develop process flow diagrams (PFDs) for individual TFC subsystem blocks and the overall plant architecture.
    4. Participate in the development of piping and instrumentation diagrams (P&IDs), identification and sizing of key components, and equipment layout.
    5. Develop and maintain representative heat and mass balances to support process definition, system integration and design decisions.
  • Process modelling and simulation
    1. Develop, apply and improve process simulation models for individual TFC subsystem blocks and the overall plant architecture, using tools such as Aspen Plus, Aspen Custom Modeler, Python and dedicated proprietary software, as appropriate.
    2. Support the development and integration of custom models and, where appropriate, contribute to the development of dedicated simulation tools.
    3. Use modelling and simulation to assess system performance, compare technology options and operating configurations, support component sizing, and inform process optimisation and design decisions.
    4. Documentation of assumptions, uncertainty and applicability limits, and perform model validation when suitable data becomes available.

As a Defense Success Manager, you own what happens to our most strategic defense and sovereign accounts after the build: you make deployed AI stick in real workflows — often in restricted or disconnected environments — keep production commitments healthy, defend renewals, and source the expansion signals that Sales closes.

Mistral's Solutions teams (Deployment Strategists and Forward Deployed Engineers) co-create high-value AI use cases with customers in these environments. Your job is to make those investments successful beyond delivery — adopting what has been built, operating it with confidence, demonstrating its impact, and scaling value across the institution. You will work with mission owners, program stakeholders, end users, security and IT teams, and across Mistral with Solutions, Product, Engineering and Support.

This is not a high-volume, ticket-queue customer success role. Portfolios are small and deep — typically one or two flagship accounts plus a small number of adjacent programs. It calls for a strategic account mindset, the technical judgment to navigate complex and constrained deployment environments, and the energy to build the customer success function as Mistral grows. Travel to customer sites, including secure facilities, is a regular part of the job.

You will join on one of two tracks (and can move between them):

  • Adoption track — embedded in flagship programs while Solutions is still delivering. You own the adoption and change-management motion around the build: user waves, enablement, champions, training programs, and the evidence that proves value is landing.

  • Operational track — you take accounts through a structured handover once Solutions completes delivery, and own the run phase end-to-end: operational health, value realization, renewals, and expansion signals.

In both tracks you operate in close partnership with Solutions: they deliver and hand over; you own post-handover; they re-engage on expansion signals. Occasionally, account teams will also pull you into late-stage pre-sales — authoring the customer training and scale-up plan that gives a buyer confidence in the rollout.


What You Will Do


Own the customer success and value plan

  • Build a clear view of each account's objectives, stakeholders, deployed use cases, commitments and risks. Translate it into a shared success plan with owners, milestones and measurable outcomes.

  • Establish a practical operating cadence with customer sponsors, business owners, IT and delivery teams. Lead success reviews that make progress, risks, decisions and next steps clear.

  • Define a baseline and track the outcomes that matter for each use case: adoption and usage against entitled seats, customer satisfaction, operational health and business impact. Turn the evidence into a clear value narrative.

Make deployment realities part of the success plan

  • Understand how each customer's deployment model — on-premises, VPC or serverless — affects the products and use cases they can access, operate and scale. Validate the specifics with the technical teams rather than assuming feature parity or identical operating models.

  • Identify the practical implications of deployment choices: security and data requirements, access and integrations, release and upgrade cadence, available features, capacity, observability and support processes. Explain the trade-offs clearly to customer and Mistral stakeholders.

  • Translate those constraints into an actionable adoption plan: align enablement and release communications with the version the customer actually runs, account for security approvals and upgrade windows, and agree how to measure usage when telemetry is limited.

  • Spot risks early, qualify their impact on adoption, renewal or value, and coordinate the right Solutions, Product, Engineering or Support owners to resolve them. Set clear expectations without making unvalidated technical or roadmap commitments.

Drive adoption, autonomy and sustained value

  • Help customer teams move from a delivered use case to regular, effective use. Identify the users, workflows and change-management needs that determine whether it sticks.

  • Coordinate onboarding, training, product updates and hands-on enablement with the right Mistral and customer teams. Develop customer champions and train-the-trainer motions so adoption scales beyond direct Mistral involvement.

  • Prepare the transition from delivery to run: clarify operational ownership, support and escalation paths, and the resources users need to succeed independently.

  • Monitor adoption and customer health, investigate where usage or value is falling short, and lead a coordinated plan to address the causes.

Defend and grow the commercial relationship

  • Own the renewal motion for your accounts: know every renewal date, the auto vs non-auto renewal terms, and the risk story behind each one. Run the renewal play early — no surprises at renewal time.

  • Track and improve account NRR. Identify new use cases, teams and expansion opportunities, and share them with the account team grounded in demonstrated value.

  • Lead business reviews with the account team: value delivered, risks owned, decisions needed, roadmap asks.

Bring the customer voice into Mistral

  • Gather and qualify feedback from users, technical teams and sponsors. Distinguish enablement needs from product gaps, deployment constraints and support issues, and route each to the right owner.

  • Track important requests and communicate progress and limitations back to the customer, while Product and Engineering retain ownership of product and technical decisions.

Build the company as well as the account

  • Create the playbooks, success plans, handover practices and measurement approaches that are missing. Test them with customers, improve them, and make them reusable across accounts.

  • Bring structure to ambiguity: identify what needs to happen, make a plan, mobilize the right people and follow through — without waiting for a perfect process or detailed instructions.

Instead of handing your designs over for someone else to build, you take them all the way: you calculate them, build and assemble the prototypes yourself in our workshop, and take the design from first prototype to a product ready for series production.

This role is for you if…

you've designed the mechanical integration of power electronics or other electronic systems and know your way around creepage, clearance and insulating plastics. You back your designs with solid calculations, and you're as comfortable with a screwdriver in the workshop as with CAD at your desk.

This role isn't for you if…

your experience is in classic mechanical design only, such as gears, gearboxes or pumps, or you prefer to stay at your desk while someone else builds your prototypes. It's also not a fit if you need technicians for assembly or established processes before you can start.

Robot Heart is building the AI-native software and financial infrastructure for the global robotics economy.

As millions of autonomous mobile robots, drones and humanoids enter the workforce, a massive new asset class is emerging. Yet the infrastructure to monitor, evaluate, finance and insure these machines remains fragmented.

Our ambition is to build the leading cross-OEM intelligence platform for Physical AI, transforming real-world robot telemetry into actionable insights on asset health, reliability, performance and financial risk.

Your mission is to turn heterogeneous robot data into a proprietary intelligence engine capable of predicting asset performance, failures, remaining useful life and financial risk.

We are assembling our founding team in Zurich and engaging with robotics manufacturers, financial institutions and potential strategic partners.

title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer, FeedForward 3D/4D Reconstruction
description:
At Parallel Domain, we believe that autonomous systems – from self-driving cars to contactless delivery drones – have the opportunity to drastically improve the quality of life for billions of people. That is why we love what we do: enabling our customers to develop their technology safely using the Parallel Domain data generation platform. Our platform revolutionizes the way our customers generate sensor data for AI development. We're looking for people like you to join us in pushing the boundaries of artificial intelligence and synthetic data.

About the role 

Before any physical AI system is trusted in the real world, it has to prove itself in ours. Parallel Domain turns real captured drives into faithful digital replicas — geometry, appearance and motion that perception stacks are trained and validated against.
 
We are hiring a Senior Machine Learning Engineer to push our feed-forward reconstruction stack forward — from static 3D toward full 4D scenes over time. You will join a small, deep team where your technical judgment carries real weight from day one, and your work will ship in a pipeline customers depend on.

What You'll Do
  • Advance our feed-forward reconstruction models. Improve how we predict geometry, camera pose and appearance from real capture with transformer-based models, and extend it from static scenes to dynamic 4D.
  • Train at scale. Run multi-node GPU training on large multi-view and video datasets, and decide what to scale, what to ablate and when a result is real.
  • Define what "good" means. Build evaluation the team trusts for reconstruction quality, temporal consistency and geometric accuracy.
  • Explore stronger priors. Investigate where generative models, such as pre-trained video diffusion, can help fill gaps the capture did not see.
  • Land research in the product. Work with the pipeline engineers to get results into production, and care whether they hold up there.
  • Track the field. This area moves monthly; form a view on where it is heading and argue for it.

    • What we're looking for
  • Hands-on feed-forward reconstruction experience. You have built or trained feedforward 3D reconstruction models (for example in the lineage of DUSt3R, VGGT, π³ or D4RT), and you know where they work and where they break.
  • A track record of models others relied on. We weight demonstrated depth over years served : a recent PhD with the right focus and an experienced research engineer are both credible here.
  • Large-scale training. Practical experience with multi-node, multi-GPU training and telling a promising run from a stalled one early.
  • Strong PyTorch skills in a large shared codebase with real build and CI.
  • Research judgment. You turn an ambiguous direction into experiments that resolve something, and change your mind when the numbers say so.
  • Clear communication with researchers, pipeline engineers and leadership alike.

    • Strong pluses
    These are listed in order of how much they matter to us.
     
    1. Feed-forward Gaussian prediction. Experience predicting 3D Gaussians directly from images in a single pass, rather than fitting them per scene. 
    2. Top-tier publications in feed-forward reconstruction. First-author or significant work at CVPR, ICCV, ECCV, NeurIPS, ICLR or SIGGRAPH in this area. 
    3. Video diffusion models. Familiarity with diffusion or flow-matching video models, especially camera-conditioned generation. 
    4. Dynamic scenes. Work on dynamic reconstruction, scene flow or temporal consistency. 
    5. Real-world capture. Experience with automotive, robotics or drone data and its mess: imperfect calibration, motion blur, poses you cannot trust. 
    6. Making big models fast, or open-source contributions to widely used reconstruction libraries.
    Why join Parallel Domain?

    We are assembling a team of creative, talented visionaries seeking to build a new technology that will change the world. You will be able to learn, build, and scale our team and technology in a collaborative, creative culture that values every team member.

    •  Flexible paid vacation, sick time, winter shutdown, and 11+ holidays per year

title: AI & Data Platform Engineer (GCP) (all levels)
description:
Über KnowWay

KnowWay entwickelt KI-Agenten für kritische Infrastruktur: Energie, Telekommunikation und öffentlicher Sektor. Wir automatisieren Geschäftsprozesse mit autonomen Agenten, und zwar für Kunden, bei denen Compliance, Nachvollziehbarkeit und Datensouveränität Pflicht sind.

Das Projekt

Für einen führenden Telekommunikationskonzern in Deutschland setzen wir Daten- und KI-Projekte auf der Google Cloud um. Wir kennen die gesamte Prozess- und Systemlandschaft des Kunden, arbeiten darin und bauen mehrere Plattformen, auf denen die Fachbereiche ihre Anwendungsfälle betreiben. Mehrere Anwendungsfälle laufen parallel und stehen an unterschiedlichen Punkten zwischen Discovery und Live-Betrieb.

Unser Delivery-Team deckt dabei ungewöhnlich viel ab: Business-Analyse und die Definition der eigentlichen Anforderungen, Solution Design, schnelle PoCs und die Produktivsetzung. Wo es passt, verwenden wir vorhandene Plattform-Capabilities wieder, und wo etwas fehlt, entwickeln wir es neu.

Der Stack läuft bereits produktiv. Dazu gehören LLM-Extraktionspipelines über einen gemanagten AI-Service mit vorgeschaltetem Compliance-Proxy, agentische Systeme mit Vector Search, Batch-Verarbeitung und Orchestrierung, ein zentrales Data Warehouse und containerisierte Services. Die Infrastruktur ist komplett als Code beschrieben und läuft in einer streng abgeschotteten Umgebung mit mehreren Freigabestufen. Auf der Roadmap stehen unter anderem der Umbau des Query-Layers, die Anbindung von On-Premise-Systemen an Cloud-Worker und die Integration weiterer Quellsysteme.

Die Rolle

Du arbeitest mit uns dort, wo Datenpipelines, KI-Modelle und Cloud-Infrastruktur zusammenkommen. Gemeinsam mit dem Team sorgst Du dafür, dass das Ergebnis im Produktivbetrieb zuverlässig läuft, und übernimmst dabei nach und nach mehr Verantwortung. Jeder Schritt soll nachvollziehbar, überwacht und wartbar bleiben, auch wenn sich Datenmengen, Dokumentqualität oder Anforderungen ändern.

Zwei Wege in diese Rolle

Der Stack reicht von der Infrastruktur über Datenpipelines bis zu LLM- und Agentensystemen. Niemand bringt das alles auf Expertenniveau mit, deshalb beschreiben wir zwei Profile mit jeweils anderen Entwicklungsperspektiven. Wenn Du einen Schwerpunkt und die Bereitschaft hast, auch in die andere Richtung mitzudenken, dann ist die Rolle die Richtige für Dich.

Profil A - Platform-Schwerpunkt: Deine Erfahrung liegt vor allem in GCP/Cloud-Infrastruktur, Infrastructure as Code und Deployment. Daten- und AI-Pipelines willst Du so weit verstehen, dass Du sie betreiben und debuggen kannst.

Profil B - AI & Data-Schwerpunkt: Deine Erfahrung liegt vor allem in AI Engineering, LLM- und Datenpipelines und in Datenmodellierung. Die Infrastruktur darunter willst Du so weit verstehen, dass Du selbst deployen und Probleme bis in die Plattform verfolgen kannst.

In der Rolle entwickelst Du Dich jeweils in die andere Richtung: Mit Profil A arbeitest Du Dich zunehmend in AI- und Datenthemen ein, mit Profil B in Infrastruktur und Plattform. Wir planen das bewusst ein, und Du übernimmst auf der anderen Seite nach und nach mehr Aufgaben.

Die Rolle passt auch für Junior- und Mid-Level-Engineers. Wichtiger als viele Jahre Erfahrung ist uns, dass Du in einem der beiden Bereiche schon praktisch gearbeitet hast und Lust hast, Dich in den anderen einzuarbeiten. Die Anforderungen unten "für beide Profile“ + das A oder B-Profil sind das Minimum, mit dem Du einsteigen kannst. Wer mehr mitbringt, steigt entsprechend höher ein.

Deine Aufgaben

Die Listen beschreiben das Spektrum des Teams. Wie viel davon Du am Anfang übernimmst, hängt von Deiner Erfahrung ab.

Gemeinsamer Kern:

Entwicklung und Betrieb von Datenpipelines auf GCP: Batch-Verarbeitung, Orchestrierung, Beladung der Datenplattform

Anbindung neuer Datenquellen. Jede Quelle hat ihre eigenen Eigenheiten, deshalb lässt sich eine Anbindung selten einfach auf die nächste übertragen.

Fehlersuche über die gesamte Kette, von der Quelldatei über Pipeline und Modell bis in die Anwendung

CI/CD-Pipelines, Deployment-Automatisierung, Container-Builds und Vulnerability-Gates

Netzwerk, IAM, Secret-Management, Verschlüsselung und Zugriffskonzepte

Logging, Monitoring und Alerting für Pipelines und Anwendungen

Kostenkontrolle und Ressourcendimensionierung

Schwerpunkt AI & Data:

Entwicklung von LLM-Extraktionspipelines: Segmentierung und Klassifikation von Dokumenten, prompt-basierte Extraktion, Schema-Validierung, Upsert in die Datenplattform

Extraktionsgenauigkeit bewerten und verbessern, auf Basis belastbarer Messungen

Datenqualität als eigenes Arbeitsfeld

Was Du mitbringst

Für beide Profile:

Mindestens etwa ein Jahr Berufserfahrung mit Datenpipelines, Cloud-Infrastruktur oder KI-Systemen. Eine längere Werkstudententätigkeit in einem Engineering-Team zählt auch. Idealerweise lief davon schon etwas in Produktion und nicht nur in Notebooks oder Proof-of-Concepts.

Du bleibst an einem Problem dran, bis Du verstehst, was passiert, auch wenn die Ursache drei Systemgrenzen weiter liegt.

Wie wir Dich einarbeiten

Du bekommst eine feste Ansprechperson im Team und startest mit einem abgegrenzten Teil, zum Beispiel einer Pipeline oder einem Modul. Code Reviews und Pairing mit erfahrenen Kolleginnen und Kollegen sind dabei Dein wichtigster Lernweg.

title: Research Scientist Intern (PhD) - Cohort '27
description:
Who we are

Foundation models transformed text and images. Structured data - the largest and most consequential data format in the world - stayed untouched, until now. What LLMs did for language, we're doing for tables.

We pioneered tabular foundation models: TabPFN v2 was a Nature cover story, has passed 3.5M+ downloads and 7,500+ GitHub stars, and runs in production from detecting lung disease with Oxford Cancer Analytics to preventing train failures with Hitachi. The hardest problems - millions of rows, real-time inference, entirely new modalities - are still open, and no one else is working on them at this level.

We're a small, highly selective team of 40+ with backgrounds from Google, DeepMind, Meta, Apple, Amazon, Jane Street, and CERN, led by Frank Hutter, Noah Hollmann, and Sauraj Gambhir, and advised by Bernhard Schölkopf and Turing Award winner Yann LeCun.

In July 2026, less than 18 months after our €9M pre-seed, we joined SAP as an independent frontier AI lab - same team, mission, and open-weights models, now backed by more than €1 billion over four years.

About the role

You’ll join our research team for a 4 to 6 month internship, in the cohort that starts in May 2027. The work is hands-on, with tabular foundation models, a new class of AI model, and how they’re applied. We have more open research problems than people to work on them, and you’ll get a project matched to your interests and expertise, with the chance to publish the results. Some of the problems we’re working on:

  • Scaling model architectures and training

  • Models that read text and tables together

  • Architectures for time series, forecasting and anomaly detection

  • Faster training and inference

  • Causal reasoning in foundation models

  • Learning across multiple related tables

  • Benchmarks that show where tabular foundation models work and where they break, in science and in industry

What we’re looking for

  • You’re doing a PhD in computer science, applied maths, statistics, electrical engineering or a related field.

  • You have at least one first-author or shared-first-author paper at a top venue such as NeurIPS, ICML or ICLR.

  • You've turned your own research ideas into working experiments, for example in PyTorch, and you can tell when code is quietly wrong, whether you or a coding agent wrote it.

  • You can join us in Freiburg or Berlin from May 2027 for 4 to 6 months.

  • Experience with data science for tabular data or time series data is a plus

Mentorship at Prior Labs

Your mentor will be one of the researchers building TabPFN, who’ll help you with the technical side of your project and with your development as a researcher. Before you accept, we agree on a project area and a mentor with you, so you know what you’re working on and who you’re working with from day one. During the internship you’ll also work alongside the rest of our research and data science teams.

Benefits

  • A cohort of PhD interns who start with you, and a week-long workshop in Freiburg with the whole cohort in summer 2027

You'll work alongside researchers and builders who hold themselves to a very high bar - in the quality of their work and in how they work with each other. We move fast and still take the time to do things right.

Our teams are based in Berlin, Freiburg, and New York - when you're working on something as hard as TabPFN, being in the same room matters. title: Produktionsmitarbeiter  (m/w/d)
description:
Bei GALVANY ist es unser Ziel, klimaneutrales Wohnen für alle zur Realität zu machen. Wir setzen auf Umsetzung und entwickeln konkrete, smarte Lösungen, indem wir Wärmepumpen, Batteriespeicher und Smart Metering einfach zugänglich, zuverlässig und bezahlbar machen.

Wir sind ein profitables Greentech-Startup und glauben, dass nachhaltiger Impact und langfristiges Wachstum nur auf Basis eines gesunden Geschäftsmodells möglich sind. Um unsere ambitionierte Tech Roadmap umzusetzen haben wir im Frühjahr 2026 eine Seed-Finanzierung in Höhe von 10 Millionen Euro mit Set Ventures und AENU abgeschlossen. Getrieben von Kundennutzen, Klarheit und Verantwortung stehen wir für hochwertige Heizlösungen und ein Arbeitsumfeld, in dem Menschen Verantwortung übernehmen und nachhaltigen Mehrwert schaffen.

Die Rolle

In unserer Eigenproduktion bauen wir die Komponenten vor, die unsere Installationsteams beim Kunden direkt einsetzen: hydraulische Cubes und elektrische Unterverteilungen für die Wärmepumpe. Je besser sie vorgefertigt sind, desto schneller und sauberer läuft die Installation vor Ort.

Cubes sind unsere vormontierten Hydraulikmodule, die alle wesentlichen Komponenten für den Heizkreis kompakt in einem Gehäuse bündeln. Wir fertigen sie in mehreren Varianten für unterschiedliche Wärmepumpen und Einbausituationen.

Unterverteilungen sind die elektrischen Verteiler, über die die Wärmepumpe abgesichert und angeschlossen wird. Sie werden nach Plan in Standardvarianten je Geräteserie und Leistungsklasse aufgebaut.

Du arbeitest in einem kleinen Produktionsteam innerhalb von Supply Chain, eng verzahnt mit Lager, Kommissionierung und Einkauf. Die Produktion wächst mit unseren Installationszahlen und zieht 2027 in unser neues Hauptlager in Ludwigsfelde.

Deine Aufgaben

  • Montage von Cubes: Rahmen aus Aluprofilen aufbauen, Komponenten einsetzen, Verrohrung in Edelstahl-Pressfitting und Gewinde herstellen, Verkleidung montieren.

  • Aufbau und Verdrahtung von Unterverteilungen nach Bestückungsplan, Stückliste und Stromlaufplan, inklusive Beschriftung der Betriebsmittel.

  • Qualitätsprüfung vor Auslieferung: Dichtheitsprüfung der Cubes, Sicht- und Funktionsprüfung der Unterverteilungen, Dokumentation der Prüfergebnisse.

  • Vorbereitung von Material für die Produktion, z. B. Kabel ablängen, Anschlusssets zusammenstellen, Rohre zuschneiden.

  • Übergabe fertiger Cubes und Unterverteilungen in die Projektkommissionierung, termingerecht zur geplanten Installation.

  • Pflege der Materialbestände am Arbeitsplatz und frühzeitige Meldung von Fehlmengen an Lager und Einkauf.

  • Mitarbeit an der Weiterentwicklung unserer Varianten und Arbeitsabläufe: Rückmeldung aus der Montage zu Stücklisten, Bauteilen und Prozessen.

  • Ordnung, Sauberkeit und Arbeitssicherheit in deinem Produktionsbereich.

Dein Profil

Location: London

About Founders Factory:

Founders Factory builds and funds startups together with exceptional entrepreneurs and the world's leading companies. Created by IPO-exited founders, we offer founders capital, operational support from a team of hands-on experts, and unrivalled access to a coalition of industry-leading corporate partners. Since 2015, Founders Factory's 450+ portfolio companies have secured 500+ pilots and commercial contracts with our partners.

Our Studio partners with entrepreneurs at day one, developing new ideas, technologies and business models into high-growth companies. In partnership with Aviva, one of the UK's leading insurers, we are building a new portfolio of ventures out of London.

About the Venture:

Complaints are changing faster than the teams that handle them. Generative AI makes complaints longer and easier to file: the Financial Ombudsman says up to a third of responses to its initial assessments now look AI-generated, and it has seen 200-page submissions in reply to an eight-page decision. Soon personal agents will file and chase complaints for people, so one event becomes several. UK financial services firms received 1.85 million complaints in the first half of 2026, up 6.3%, and a human still has to read and check every one. Every ombudsman referral can cost a firm £680.

It isn't only financial complaints. New kinds of regulated requests are arriving that no off-the-shelf tool handles well, such as waves of GDPR data requests from job candidates a company never hired. Each one raises the same questions: why is this happening, do we have to respond, and how do we respond fairly and on time?

We are building the AI desk that handles them. It splits a long complaint or request into its separate claims, checks each one against the policy, the customer's records and the rules, and drafts a fair, cited response within the deadline, with a handler always making the decision. Every outcome and published ombudsman decision feeds back in, so the drafts get better case by case. We start with insurers, banks and lenders, then move to utilities, telecoms and any regulated business.

Jobs to be Done:

As Founder & CEO, you will be responsible for turning a strong thesis into a scaled, defensible business.

  • Find the sharpest pain. Decide which workflow to own first, whether AI-written financial complaints, data requests or another emerging regulated workflow, and who feels it most.

  • Build a product handlers trust. Take the AI desk from concept to something complaint handlers rely on to save real time, and that regulators accept as fair handling.

  • Pilot with Aviva. Prove it on real (anonymised) complaint files across motor, home and pet, and show fewer ombudsman referrals and faster, more consistent decisions.

  • Plug into how firms work. Integrate with the case-management systems firms already use, rather than asking them to switch.

  • Build the company. Hire the initial team, raise capital, and establish the venture as the standard for complaint and regulated-request handling across sectors and countries.

Your Ideal Experience:

The ideal candidate gets excited by messy workflows and knows first-hand why complaints matter in a regulated business.

  • Experience in or alongside a regulated business: financial services, insurance, utilities, telecoms, legal or compliance. Direct experience in complaints or customer operations is a strong plus.

  • A builder's instinct for workflow: you see a manual, painful process and know how AI and good product design can fix it.

  • Comfortable building with AI: you can shape agentic products and work closely with engineers, even if you're not writing the code yourself.

  • B2B commercial instinct: you can sell to heads of complaints, operations and compliance in large organisations.

  • Comfortable operating in ambiguity: making irreversible calls with incomplete data.

  • Credibility with a large corporate partner and with forward-looking venture investors.

Most importantly, you want to make complaint handling faster and fairer for both the business and the customer.

This is your company. We're here to help.

We're looking for an experienced and proactive Senior Product Designer to join our Product Design team at Zable. You'll join a team of 5 product designers and report to the VP of Product & Design.

You'll work mainly on the Zable app, our financial SuperApp with 2M+ monthly active users. It brings together credit cards, loans, memberships, mobile and more in one place. You'll own complex product areas end-to-end, from discovery and research through to polished, production-ready design. You'll set design direction alongside PMs and Engineering, mentor other designers, and help raise the bar for craft and outcomes across the team.

  • 5+ years of product design experience, ideally in fintech or a fast-paced startup

About the Role

Zable is a high-growth FinTech building its security operations capability deliberately. As a Senior Security Operations Analyst, you will triage and respond to security alerts, help improve the quality of the detections behind them, and lead the response when a security event becomes an incident.

You will investigate alerts and escalations from our MSSP, tune our monitoring so that it finds more of what matters and less of what doesn’t, and act as a trusted Incident Commander for security incidents, from declaration through to post-incident review. You will work with Engineering, IT, Legal, Risk and senior stakeholders, and you will be credible with all of them.

AI is used widely across the business, in how we build software, run operations and serve customers, and that changes both what security incidents look like and how quickly we can respond to them. You will use AI and automation as a normal part of your work, and you will be able to investigate and respond to incidents where AI tooling is the cause, the target or the route in.

  • Triage and investigate alerts across our SIEM, EDR, identity and cloud tooling, taking escalations from our MSSP’s first-line team.

  • Utilise AI and automation to speed up triage, enrichment and response, and to remove repetitive manual work from the analyst workflow.

  • Run blameless post-incident reviews, track actions to closure, and feed lessons back into detection, playbooks and controls.

  • Take part in the out-of-hours on-call rota.

title: Customer Support Specialist
description:
About us

Owkin is an agentic AI company pioneering Biological Artificial Superintelligence to solve problems in biology where human researchers alone have failed.
Owkin builds K Pro - an AI scientist for pharmaceutical research and strategic decision-making. K Pro orchestrates a suite of AI skills and tools to decode complex biology, accelerate research, and dramatically increase productivity.
K Pro is built on Owkin’s unrivalled multimodal patient data network, state-of-the-art AI for biology and a decade of experience working with pharmaceutical partners.

Position is based in our Paris office or remotely in France, UK or Germany.

Please submit your CV in English

About the role:

Owkin is looking for a Customer Support Specialist to own first-level support for K-Pro, Owkin's AI research platform for biopharma R&D, used by AstraZeneca, Sanofi, Servier and Boehringer Ingelheim.

Our clients have made major investments to access K-Pro, and their contracts come with strict response and resolution SLAs. You will be their first point of contact during business hours: the person who understands their problem quickly, keeps them informed, and gets the right engineering, product or customer success people moving. You will also help shape how support works at Owkin, including where AI and agentisation make it better.

 

In particular, you will:

Own the support flow

  • Own incoming tickets during business hours as the first line of support for all K-Pro clients

  • Triage every ticket: set priority (P1 to P4) and the impacted service, and route it to the right team

  • Keep SLAs on track: follow up on open tickets, escalate early when a deadline is at risk

  • Communicate clear, timely updates to users and CSMs throughout the ticket lifecycled 

 Go deep on the product

  • Diagnose issues directly with users: reproduce bugs, check data and configurations, and give engineers a clean, actionable report

  • Learn K-Pro in depth (its features, the datasets clients use, how login, API access, exports and permissions work, and the research questions clients bring to it) so you can resolve most issues without escalating

  • Recognise when a result looks scientifically wrong and when it's a usage question

Turn support into insight

  • Act as the Customer Success team's eyes on support: flag critical tickets, recurring issues, and signs that a client is becoming dissatisfied, so CSMs can act early

  • Spot patterns across tickets and turn them into product feedback, doc updates or process fixes

  • Track and report on support metrics (response time, SLA compliance, first contact resolution, volume) and give actionable insights to the team.

Own the knowledge base

  • Own the K-Pro help center: write, update and remove articles as new issues are resolved

  • Turn one-off fixes into reusable answers for clients and for the support team

Improve support with AI

  • Identify where automation and AI tools (triage, routing, response drafting, knowledge retrieval) would save time or improve quality

  • Work with R&Tech Operations to build, test and improve these workflows

 

About you

Required qualifications / experience:

  • Proven technical support or customer support for B2B software, ideally SaaS, with enterprise clients

  • A track record handling SLA-bound support with demanding customers, and staying calm under pressure

  • Strong technical curiosity: comfortable with APIs, logs, data and configurations; basic SQL or scripting is a plus

  • Hands-on experience with AI tooling and building or improving agentic support workflows (AI-assisted triage, automated routing, LLM-powered drafting), and the judgment to know when automation fits

  • Excellent written and verbal communication, able to explain technical issues to scientists and to engineers alike

  • Experience with support tooling such as Zendesk, Linear and PagerDuty, or equivalent

  • Able to follow runbooks and escalation paths, and to know when to deviate from them

  • A habit of turning fixes into documentation and patterns into insights

Preferred qualifications/bonus:

  • Experience in life sciences, biopharma or another regulated industry is a strong plus

What success looks like in your first 6 months

  • You handle the full ticket flow for all K-Pro clients with SLAs met

  • CSMs rely on your signals to anticipate account risks

  • The help center covers the most frequent ticket types

  • You have shipped at least one automation that measurably improves support 

#LI-HB1

  • Flexible work organization

  • Friendly and informal working environment

  • Opportunity to work with an international team with high technical and scientific backgrounds

description:
About Orakl Oncology

At Orakl Oncology, we are accelerating the development of oncology treatments. Today, fewer than 5% of new cancer drugs succeed in clinical trials. Clearly, new methods are needed. We combine cutting-edge biology and AI to build the next generation of insight platforms with the world's largest cohort of patient tumor avatars. These avatars fuel our AI-powered predictive engine, helping to anticipate clinical trial outcomes, validate therapies, and uncover new drug candidates. By generating multimodal, real-world data, we deliver insights that consistently outperform existing solutions.

Our mission is simple yet ambitious: to bring more effective treatments to patients who need them - and to make drug development smarter, faster, and more personalized. We collaborate with top hospitals, research institutes, and pharmaceutical companies worldwide. Backed by leading investors, we are a fast-growing, mission-driven startup at the intersection of science and technology.

The company is growing fast, and we are now seeking the best talents to come and join our exciting and ambitious team in the fight against cancer - join us!

Position overview

Orakl runs its data and AI platform on AWS: Dagster pipelines, a versioned PostgreSQL warehouse, ephemeral Fargate and EC2 compute, eight microservices.

Unique in-house and hospital-provided biological, clinical and omics data flow through it every day. We continuously train our proprietary AI models on this every day to create new scientific insights that will benefit patients.

We are hiring a Platform Engineer across three missions: infrastructure, security and scalability. You will be our first dedicated platform hire, and you will decide what this platform looks like for the next years. This is a high-stakes, high-ownership position.

Our stack

  • Cloud: AWS (Paris region), cross-cloud backup to a second European provider

  • Compute: ECS and Fargate, EC2, ephemeral provisioning per job

  • Data: PostgreSQL, S3, versioned transformations

  • Code: Python everywhere, Docker, Terraform, GitHub, GitHub Actions, Dagster orchestration, Nextflow

What you will be doing

1. Security: Codebase, incident management, AI guardrails, fleet management.

These are the main things that you will be focusing during your first months with us:

  • Secure the codebase: workflow permissions, pinned actions, dependency and secret scanning, package security.

  • Run vulnerability watch and build our incident response tooling: establish the blast radius, write the fix, deploy it company-wide, run the postmortem.

  • Define our AI guardrails: we use AI tools heavily and we are embedding them in the product, so we need clear rules on which data those tools may reach and how their output is reviewed before it ships.

  • Develop our fleet management tools to **keep our laptops up-to-date and secure, define and enforce security practices, deploy and maintain management and security tooling to our fleet.

2. Infrastructure management: Compute, data access, observability.

  • Own our AWS compute: VPC and network segmentation, EC2 allocation.

  • Support data storage. As the team and our partner base grow, access to sensitive data has to stay compartmented and auditable. You will be consulted on where data belongs, across RDS, Redshift, PostgreSQL and the rest, and on keeping access to it properly controlled.

  • Build the observability layer: metrics, logs and traces in one place, alerting that fires on real failures.

  • Own secure access to our infrastructure: secure networks, access control and policies, observability.

3. Scalability: Improve the tools we have, choose the ones we will need.

  • Our product is being built and the volume of data coming in keeps growing, which will call for architecture and resources we do not use today. You will be expected to anticipate failures and future needs, and bring your expert knowledge and experience to our systems & designs.

Who you are

Minimum qualifications

  • 5+ years in platform, infrastructure or site reliability engineering, with security a real part of the job rather than an occasional task.

  • Deep hands-on AWS: IAM and identity management, VPC design, RDS, container orchestration, secrets management, federated authentication for CI.

  • Terraform in production with a real review workflow behind it, and containers you have operated rather than only deployed to.

  • Ownership of CI/CD security, ideally GitHub Actions: supply chain integrity, dependency management, build provenance.

  • Incident response as a practitioner. You have been the person on the hook, not the person who read the report afterwards.

  • Fluent in English.

Preferred qualifications

  • Highly sensitive data in a high-stakes regulated sector: health, finance or defence.

  • Working knowledge of French health data regulation (HDS, CNIL, GDPR), or another regulated environment and the appetite to learn this one quickly.

  • Device management at scale (Jamf, Kandji, Fleet or equivalent) and automated joiner, mover and leaver processes.

  • Dagster or a comparable orchestration framework, and PostgreSQL in production.

What we offer

  • Mission: work in a cutting-edge environment, on the forefront of cancer research.

  • Impact: take ownership of a critical piece of an early-stage, fast-moving company, with the opportunity to shape it; your engineering decisions will carry through to our science and, ultimately, to patient outcomes.

  • Team: join a collaborative, multidisciplinary team where you’ll work alongside stellar clinicians, biologists, and engineers towards a common mission.
