title: Lab Automation Lead
description:
About us, and our mission

At Orakl Oncology, we are accelerating the development of oncology treatments. Today, fewer than 5% of new cancer drugs succeed in clinical trials. Clearly, new methods are needed. We combine cutting-edge biology and AI to build the next generation of insight platforms with a large cohort of patient-derived tumor avatars. These avatars fuel our predictive engine, helping to anticipate clinical outcomes, validate therapies and uncover new drug candidates. By generating multimodal, real-world data, we aim to make drug development smarter, faster and more personalized. We collaborate with leading hospitals, research institutes and pharmaceutical companies. Backed by leading investors, Orakl is a fast-growing, mission-driven startup at the intersection of biology, automation and AI.

Position overview

Orakl runs a high-throughput 3D cell‑culture platform to culture patient-derived organoids (PDOs). These patient-derived specimens reveal critical information into the patient disease, but require heavy maintenance work. Automating these workflows will be critical to improve the reliability and traceability of experimental work. We are hiring our first automation lead to build the Automation function from scratch. This is a high ownership and high autonomy job. You will map our processes, decide what to automate and what to leave alone, specify and source the equipment, negotiate with vendors and integrators, commission the machines, run them with the lab team, and hire the people the function needs. As the ideal candidate, you have already put automated lines or special machines into service, and you know what typically breaks between commissioning and the first experimental runs. While previous experience in biology is a plus, it is not a strict requirement: you will be taught all you need to know. However, you do need a proven experience in working deeply embedded in interdisciplinary teams.

Key responsibilities

  • Map cell culture workflows end to end and identify key process automation and optimisation opportunities.

  • Own the automation roadmap. Present and lead the implementation of the major decisions to Orakl’s leadership.

  • In line with the automation strategy you will have identified, evaluate vendors and integrators. Write user requirement specifications, acceptance criteria and interface requirements for each project.

  • Negotiate price, scope, delivery, acceptance, support and consumables terms autonomously within agreed thresholds.

  • Lead design reviews and factory and site acceptance tests.

  • Translate our proprietary cell culture protocols into automated machine execution with our team of cell biologists and scientists.

  • Track machine availability, hands-on time per line, interventions, failures and recovery time. Use the data to decide the next step.

  • Coordinate with Orakl’s management to anticipate future automation needs on the platform and adjust the roadmap accordingly.

  • Hire and develop the automation technicians and engineers the roadmap needs.

  • Set the standards for the automated platform: documentation, quality control, safety, qualification, change control, vendor management.

In this role you will collaborate closely with our cell culture, cell biology and data science teams. You will be at the heart of Orakl Oncology’s capabilities roadmap and help generate unprecedented amounts of biological data to power scientific discovery in cancer.

Key qualifications

Must-have

  • Engineering degree (generalist, robotics, industrial, mechanical or process engineering) or equivalent, and at least eight years of experience.

  • Exceptional process thinking skills: you map flows, time operations, find bottlenecks and question the processes.

  • Experience in supplier negotiation and budget ownership on your own projects.

  • Experience in PLC and robot programming concepts, scheduling software, instrument interfaces, basic scripting.

  • You enjoy and are comfortable spending time on the floor with operators. You have experience in communicating and operating with engineers, technicians and workers at the heart of production processes.

  • Autonomy: you tell your manager what you decided and why, not what you need decided.

  • Fluency in English is required.

Nice-to-have

  • You have put automated lines, cells or special machines into service end to end: requirements, vendor selection, negotiation, integration, factory and site acceptance, ramp-up, budget. This doesn’t have to be in a lab environment : plant, food and fermentation, pharma or cosmetics are other examples of relevant experience.

  • Automation in life-science or regulated environments: cell culture, biotech, food and fermentation, pharma, cleanroom or BSL-2 work.

  • A working understanding of cell culture and what it demands: sterility, contamination risk, variability between samples, and steps governed by the biological pace.

  • Liquid handling, plate-based workflows, incubators and imagers; laboratory scheduling software.

  • Experience hiring and leading an automation team.

What we offer

  • Short decision lines and fast execution.

description:
Ready to make connectivity from space universally accessible, secure and actionable? Then you’ve come to the right place!

E-Space is bridging Earth and space to enable hyper-scaled deployments of Internet of Things (IoT) solutions and services. We are building a highly-advanced low Earth orbit (LEO) space system that will fundamentally change the design, economics, manufacturing and service delivery associated with traditional satellite and terrestrial IoT systems.

We’re intentional, we’re unapologetically curious and we’re 100% committed to innovate space-based communications and deliver actionable intelligence that will expand global economies, protect space and our planet and enhance our overall quality of life.


What is the role: 

We are seeking a Thermal Engineer to own the thermal analysis and testing of our space products, such as sensors and actuators. The role centers on building thermal models and correlating them with test data, and on planning and running thermal test campaigns in house. It is a hands-on position: you will instrument and run tests yourself and use the results to improve both the design and our test infrastructure. This position is based in our Toulouse office. 


What you will do:

  • Develop and maintain thermal models (analytical and numerical) of units such as sensors and actuators, from early design trades to flight predictions. 

  • Perform thermal analyses (steady-state, transient, worst-case hot and cold) to support design reviews and recommend design changes. 

  • Define thermal test campaigns: test plans, predictions, temperature profiles, instrumentation, and pass/fail criteria from requirements and qualification margins. 

  • Operate our in-house thermal test facility: run thermal cycling tests, coordinate thermal vacuum (TVAC) campaigns, and own the test reports. 

  • Correlate models with test data to refine predictions and margins and feed the results back into the design. 

  • Improve our test infrastructure: identify capability gaps, specify and procure equipment, design fixtures and thermal interfaces, and commission new setups. 

  • Act as the thermal point of contact for our units toward the spacecraft team: unit thermal budgets, interface boundary conditions, and unit models for the spacecraft thermal model. 

  • Support spacecraft Assembly, Integration, and Test (AIT) through system-level thermal balance testing.


    • What you bring to this role:

  • BS + 8 years / MS + 5 years in Mechanical, Aerospace, or Thermal Engineering, or equivalent, with professional experience in thermal engineering of space or electronic hardware. 

  • Solid grounding in space heat transfer: radiation in vacuum, conduction and contact conductance across bolted interfaces, and multi-layer insulation (MLI). 

  • Hands-on experience building thermal models with standard thermal analysis tools, running worst-case analyses, and correlating models with test data. 

  • Hands-on experience planning and running thermal tests (thermal cycling or TVAC) on space or electronic hardware, from test plan to test report. 

  • Ability to instrument a test article: thermocouple selection and bonding, heater sizing and placement, thermal interface materials, and data acquisition and real-time monitoring, with ESD-safe, clean handling of sensitive hardware. 

  • Excellent teamwork, communication, and documentation skills, with professional proficiency in English; comfortable in a hands-on, fast-paced startup environment.


    • Bonus points:

  • Experience with Python to post-process test data and automate model correlation. 

  • Experience designing or specifying thermal test equipment such as TVAC chambers, thermal plates, or shrouds. 

  • Knowledge of spacecraft thermal control hardware: heat pipes, radiators, coatings, and heater circuits. 

  • Experience using AI/LLM tools to accelerate development, analysis, and documentation, with sound judgment about their limits.

title: Edge & Machine Integration Engineer (PLC to Cloud), Freelance, m/f/d
description:
FALU AG in Rüti (ZH) builds and sells swab production machines that run in plants around the world. With FALU PMAS, our cloud based production monitoring and assistance system, every machine reports its state every five seconds. Customers get live dashboards, shift KPIs, downtime analytics and automatic alerts in the browser. The first customer went live in September 2026 with eight machines, and more plants are lined up.

The cloud side of PMAS is built and running in production: broker, ingestion service, databases, web app. The path from the PLC inside the machine to the MQTT broker is covered by one engineer who designed and built it. With more machines and more plants coming, that one person is no longer enough. We are looking for a freelancer who adds capacity on exactly this path: PLC software, Raspberry Pi edge devices, site gateway, broker connection.

This is a permanent role that we staff on a freelance basis: no project end date, a long term engagement with about 1 week of work per month, with more when a rollout is on. You will work directly with our existing integration engineer, our inhouse engineering team and the CEO.

Tasks

You work on everything between the machine PLC and the MQTT broker, alongside the engineer who built the current setup. Which parts you take over completely and which you share depends on your strengths. Concretely:

PLC and machine side

  • Bring the PMAS message format into the CB1 machine software (Siemens S7, TIA Portal V18 with HMI) and keep it in sync with the payload contract: cumulative counters, machine status, error codes, timestamps from the PLC clock.
  • Decide and implement how data leaves the PLC: MQTT publishing from the PLC itself, or a read on the edge device (S7 protocol or OPC UA) that publishes on its behalf. Pick one, justify it, standardise it.
  • Manage PLC software versions across the fleet, including safe update and rollback procedures for machines already running at customers.
  • Ensure clock discipline on the PLCs (NTP, local time zone per plant), since every duration KPI is computed from PLC timestamps.

Edge devices and site gateway

  • Develop and maintain the software on the Raspberry Pi based edge devices next to each machine: MQTT client, buffering and store and forward during uplink outages, unique client IDs, credential handling, health reporting.
  • Develop and maintain the site gateway: isolated machine network, routing and firewall, outbound only TLS and NTP, remote maintenance access, watchdogs, recovery from a spare device.
  • Help turn the current setup into a provisioning process: golden image, per machine configuration, fleet wide updates without a site visit. A new machine goes from unboxing to "visible in the dashboard" in under an hour.
  • Monitor the edge layer so that we know about a degraded device before the customer does.

Broker and data contract

  • Administer the HiveMQ Cloud clusters per customer: credentials, topic ACLs, client ID scheme, certificates.
  • Maintain the payload contract together with the existing integration engineer. Changes are versioned and documented.

Commissioning and support

  • Onboard new customers and new machines end to end, remotely where possible and on site where needed (primarily Europe and the United States).
  • Act as second line when "the dashboard shows nothing" or "the numbers look wrong" and the cause sits between PLC and broker.
  • Write the documentation you would have wanted on day one: onboarding sheets, runbooks, wiring notes.

Requirements

Must have

  • Siemens PLC programming in TIA Portal (SCL and LAD, S7-1200/1500 family). You can open an existing machine project, understand it and change it without breaking the machine.
  • Industrial networking: PROFINET, VLANs, static and DHCP setups, firewalls, TLS basics. You have connected a machine to a network that was not built for it.
  • Linux on Raspberry Pi or comparable single board computers: systemd, networking, images, headless operation, remote administration.
  • Solid programming skills in Python or Node.js for edge software, and Git as a daily tool.
  • MQTT in depth: versions 3.1.1 and 5.0, QoS levels, retained messages, last will, TLS, broker ACLs.
  • Proficiency with AI coding tools is a hard requirement. You use Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot or comparable tools every day, you write and maintain project instructions for them, you review their output critically, and you are measurably faster with them than without. Our code and documentation are written with and for these tools. If you see AI tools as optional, this role is not for you.
  • Working proficiency in English (all code, commits and documentation are in English). German is a plus for the machine side.
  • Willingness to travel to customer plants, typically a few days per quarter.
  • Availability of at least two days per week on a permanent basis, with the option to scale up during rollouts.
  • You work as a freelancer (own company or registered self employed) and can invoice FALU AG.

Nice to have

  • OPC UA, Snap7 or the Siemens open communication libraries.
  • Node-RED, Docker on ARM, Ansible or similar fleet tooling.
  • Machine building or commissioning experience: reading electrical schematics, 24 V control cabinet basics, HMI (WinCC).
  • Administration of HiveMQ, Mosquitto or EMQX.
  • A basic understanding of what happens after the broker (Node.js services, PostgreSQL, ClickHouse), so that you can talk to the cloud side at eye level.

Benefits

  • A clearly bounded, business critical scope with a colleague who knows the system and hands over properly. No cold start.
  • A running production system with a real customer, not a greenfield slide deck.
  • AI assisted development is how we work, not an experiment. You get the tools and the budget for them.
  • Machines you can touch: a test bench at FALU in Rüti with real PLCs and edge hardware.
  • Remote by default, on site in Rüti when hardware is involved. Travel to customer plants is paid on top of the rate.
  • A permanent role, not a project with an end date: growing volume as more plants go live, on a freelance basis for as long as it works for both sides.
  • Fast, uncomplicated invoicing and decisions from a small team.

If you have ever made a stubborn PLC talk to the cloud and have capacity to do it again with us, we would like to hear from you.

Please send us your CV or LinkedIn profile, your daily rate and availability, one paragraph about a PLC to cloud integration you built or fixed and what went wrong on the way, and one concrete example of how you use AI tools in your daily engineering work.

What to expect: a short call with Marc Wyss (CEO) within a week of your application, then a small practical task with a simulated PLC data source, a Raspberry Pi image and a broker endpoint. We look at how you work, not just at the result. After that, one conversation with our integration engineer and the team, then a decision and a contract.

Gebäude verursachen bis zu 40 % der weltweiten CO2-Emissionen, meist durch ineffizienten Betrieb. Unsere Antwort? Eine KI-gestützte Plug-and-Play-Optimierungslösung, die den Energieverbrauch massiv senkt, Betriebskosten um bis zu 35 % reduziert und sich oft in weniger als einem Jahr amortisiert. Namen wie die SBB, der Flughafen Zürich oder Mobimo vertrauen bereits auf uns.

Unsere Software wertet Gebäude aus und steuert sie auch direkt vor Ort. Wir wachsen schnell, und der Betrieb muss mitwachsen. Genau hier kommst du ins Spiel: Wir suchen dich als Infrastructure & Operations Engineer, um aus bestehenden Grundlagen einen Betrieb zu machen, der auch bei einem Vielfachen der heutigen Grösse trägt — und um ihn danach zu verantworten!

Aufgaben

Deine Aufgaben als Infrastructure & Operations Engineer

  • Betrieb und Automatisierung: Du führst unsere bestehenden Werkzeuge zu einem durchgängigen System zusammen und entwickelst es weiter.
  • Flottenbetrieb skalieren: Du machst den Betrieb bereit für eine stark wachsende Geräteflotte in Kundengebäuden — mit verlässlichen, automatisierten Rollouts.
  • Gebäudeanlagen absichern: Du verantwortest Netzwerksegmentierung, Zugriffskontrolle und sichere Fernzugänge zu unseren Geräten und den Anlagen dahinter.
  • Plattform betreiben und härten: Du betreibst unsere eigene Infrastruktur und machst sie fit für die nächsten Jahre — von Storage über Kapazitätsplanung bis zu Runbooks.
  • Zugänge und Nachweise: Du gestaltest den Lebenszyklus von Zertifikaten, Dienstkonten und Zugriffsrechten und sorgst dafür, dass Audit-Nachweise im Alltag automatisch entstehen.
  • Präsenz: Du bist dort, wo die Anlagen stehen — bei Kundenstandorten, im Rechenzentrum, im Office in Baden oder flexibel aus dem Homeoffice.

Qualifikation

Das bringst du mit

  • Betriebs-DNA: Du bringst Systeme zum Laufen und hältst sie am Laufen. Du bringst zu Ende, was du anfängst, und übernimmst Verantwortung für das, was danach im Betrieb ist.
  • Technisches Fundament: Linux im Betrieb, nicht nur in der Anwendung — Systemd, Netzwerkstack, Fehlersuche an laufenden Systemen. Dazu Netzwerk mit Substanz: Routing, NAT, Firewalling, VPN, Segmentierung.
  • Automatisierung: Infrastruktur als Code ist für dich Alltag. Git ist deine Arbeitsweise, nicht dein Ablageort.
  • Skripting: Python und Bash, um Werkzeuge zu bauen und Daten auszuwerten. Dazu SQL, um Betriebsdaten selbst abzufragen, statt auf ein Dashboard zu warten.
  • Agentic Coding: Du arbeitest selbstverständlich mit KI-Agenten wie Claude Code, Codex oder Cursor. Du weisst, wie man eine Aufgabe so zuschneidet, dass ein Agent sie zuverlässig löst, und erkennst, wann du besser nicht delegierst.
  • Urteilsvermögen: Du kannst Code lesen und beurteilen, auch in Sprachen, in denen du nicht selbst entwickelst. Bei uns entsteht viel mit Agenten — das Prüfen und Entscheiden ist die eigentliche Arbeit, besonders wenn eine Änderung die ganze Flotte erreicht.
  • Feld- oder Flottenerfahrung: Du hast mit verteilten Geräteflotten gearbeitet oder kommst aus der Anlagentechnik und weisst, was es bedeutet, wenn ein Update ein Gebäude erwischt.
  • Sprachen: Deutsch und Englisch.

Wertvoll, aber keine Voraussetzung: Erfahrung mit Virtualisierung und verteiltem Storage, Datenbanken, Gebäudeautomations-Protokollen, Kubernetes sowie IEC 62443 oder ISO 27001 aus der Praxis. Zertifikate ohne Praxis brauchen wir nicht.

Benefits

Das bieten wir dir

  • Entscheidungsspielraum statt Zuarbeit: Du baust die Infrastruktur, die du danach betreibst. Architektur und Betriebsmodell liegen bei dir, nicht bei einem Gremium.
  • Eine Strategie statt eines Blankoblatts: Die Grundlagen sind erarbeitet. Du fängst nicht bei null an — und auch nicht in einem fertigen System, in dem nichts mehr zu entscheiden ist.
  • Ein Problem, das es so selten gibt: Eine Geräteflotte, die stark wächst, und Infrastruktur, deren Fehler nicht in einem Ticket enden, sondern in einem Gebäude. Wer Gebäudetechnik und IT-Betrieb verbinden will, findet das nicht an vielen Orten.
  • Kurze Wege: Ein kleines Team, keine Zwischenebenen, kein Konzernprozess. Was am Montag entschieden wird, läuft am Mittwoch.
  • Agentic Coding als Standard: Wir arbeiten konsequent mit KI-Agenten, finanzieren die Werkzeuge dafür und entwickeln die Arbeitsweise gemeinsam weiter. Wer das schon kann, wird hier nicht ausgebremst.

Ehrlich vorab: Wir sind ein kleines Team, und diese Rolle ist neu. Vieles wirst du selbst gestalten, statt es vorzufinden — von Runbooks bis zu Bereitschaftsregeln. Wenn dich genau das reizt, passt es gut. Wer eine eingespielte Betriebsorganisation sucht, wird bei uns nicht glücklich.

Dafür arbeitest du an etwas, das messbar wirkt: Jedes Gebäude, das effizienter läuft, zählt doppelt — für unsere Kunden und für die CO2-Bilanz.

Kein klassisches Motivationsschreiben nötig. Beschreib uns im Anschreiben stattdessen in ein paar Sätzen, woran du zuletzt gearbeitet hast und was dabei schiefgegangen ist — das sagt uns mehr als jede Floskel.

Qualifikation

Benefits

  • Exklusives Gebiet: Ihr Gebiet ist Ihnen exklusiv zugeordnet; Sie bauen darin Ihren eigenen Mandantenstamm und Ihr eigenes Netzwerk auf. Aktiv akquirieren Sie in Ihrem Gebiet; Mandanten von außerhalb, die von sich aus auf Sie zukommen, dürfen Sie ebenfalls betreuen.

SANOVIO is the collaborative AI platform for healthcare procurement. Every euro a hospital loses in purchasing is missing in patient care. We help hospitals get good products at fair prices, with far less manual work.

We build the software. And we move the goods. SANOVIO aOS, our agentic operating system for procurement, handles master data management, portfolio management and digital procurement processing. SANOVIO Fulfillment covers global direct sourcing, quality control, warehousing and logistics.

Founded in 2024 in Munich by Noel Nosswitz, Alexander Hüttner and Yong Wang, we work with hospitals in Germany and Switzerland, purchasing groups and international suppliers. We are customer-funded: our customers are our only investors.

As Technical Product Manager, you turn real procurement problems into working software. You sit between our hospital and supplier users, our engineering team and the founders. You decide what we build next, shape how it works, and often build the first version yourself.

You work on SANOVIO aOS and the internal tools behind our fulfillment operations: AI agents that clean item master data, workflows that move an order from request to ward, and integrations with hospital and supplier systems.

A large part of the role is talking to customers. You join calls and on-site visits with hospital purchasing teams, purchasing groups and suppliers, show them what we build, take their feedback and turn it into product decisions. You are a trusted contact for our customers on everything technical.

Location: Munich (on-site, with flexibility).

  • Own the product roadmap for selected areas of SANOVIO aOS, from problem discovery to release.

  • Write clear product specifications and translate them into tasks engineering can ship.

  • Understand and map user flows end to end, and find where users lose time or get stuck.

  • Iterate fast: ship a first version, learn from real users and improve it within days, not months.

  • Design and prototype AI agents and LLM-based features, for example matching products across supplier catalogues or checking certificates.

  • Automate internal workflows across procurement, quality, warehousing and finance, and connect the systems behind them.

  • Familiarity with information security, access management and the responsible handling of confidential data.

What else you bring

  • A degree in computer science, engineering, business informatics or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

  • Experience in product development: you have taken a product or internal tool from first idea to something people use every day.

That's what Tanso is building. And it's one of the reasons people join us.

Your role

Each industrial company we work with sets things up differently. As a Forward Deployed Engineer (f/m/x), you own that part. You'll work directly with our customers' sustainability, finance and IT teams, connect their systems to Tanso, and build the integrations, data pipelines and workflows that make the platform work for them.

description:
Getting homes off fossil fuels means fitting millions of heat pumps, solar panels and batteries, and every one has to be designed, sold and fitted by an installer. The assets themselves already work brilliantly, but getting them into homes is still slow, complex and painful. Our mission is to change that: to make it wildly easier and more profitable to run a renewables installation business, and get homes off fossil fuels way faster.

In just a few years we've become the leading platform for heat pump installers in the UK and Ireland, with around half of all heat pump installations now being managed on Spruce. We've just launched our solar and battery product, and we're building on that to go after even bigger opportunities: every other type of job these installers do, the rest of how they run their business, and a bunch of new countries.

We're now on the hunt for someone truly brilliant to own our socials: making content installers look forward to watching, and turning that attention into customers.

 

🌲 About Spruce

  • Almost 20% of the UK's carbon emissions comes from heating homes – there's simply no way to reach net zero without phasing out gas and oil boilers. Right now the only serious alternative is heat pumps, with their almost-magical ability to turn 1 kW of electricity into 3-5 kW of heat (🤯). But the heat pump installation journey is slow, inefficient, and just so painful. This makes it hard for existing installers to grow their businesses and puts off gas engineers from starting to do heat pumps. Perhaps most critically, it means you can't currently offer a heat pump when someone's boiler breaks and they urgently need heating.

  • We're fixing this. We've built a platform for heat pump installers to manage the whole installation journey from initial enquiry through to final compliance paperwork, freeing up their time to focus on what really matters: doing high-quality installations, providing great customer service, and scaling their business. Despite only getting started at the beginning of 2024, we're having a massive impact on installation businesses, suppliers, and manufacturers across the UK: halving the time they spend on each job and doubling their sales conversion rates.

  • We raised a chunky Seed round last year from top-tier investors and this year have doubled the team and grown revenue 4x. We've expanded into Ireland, have just launched an end-to-end solar and battery product, and are increasingly becoming the operating system for the whole home renewables supply chain. If you can picture a combination of ServiceTitan, Procore, and AutoCAD, you might get a sense of where we're headed…

 

🥖 The role

You'll work closely with Hector and the wider growth team. You'll be our first dedicated social hire. Almost nobody is making great content for installers, so the field is wide open and it's yours to build. Your goal is to make Spruce the account every installer follows. Day-to-day you'll be:

  • Making the content yourself – You'll take each piece from idea to script, shoot, edit and post: installer stories, site visits, founder clips, and new out-of-the-box ideas with a real shot at going viral. You'll have the freedom to try anything, and to bring in freelance editors or videographers when that gets better content out sooner.

  • Getting people on camera – You'll spend time on site with our customers and make installers look brilliant on camera. You'll get our own team on camera too, from sales to the devs who build the product.

  • Getting the mix right – You'll balance videos that entertain (skits, challenges, series), teach installers something useful, build trust through real installer stories, and show what Spruce does, so the account never feels like an advert. You'll keep testing new formats, trends and collabs with installer creators.

  • Owning our socials – You'll run Instagram, TikTok, YouTube, LinkedIn and Facebook: the voice, what we make, and what goes out and when. You'll do more of what works and drop what doesn't.

  • Building a community – You'll reply to comments and DMs yourself, and build a community of installers who want to be featured: an audience that becomes our customers.

 

🫵 About you

We look for the same five things in everyone at Spruce: curiosity; intense drive, ambition and work ethic; a high degree of personal agency and ownership; deep humility and a growth mindset; and excellent craft.

You don't need a particular job title or a set number of years, but you do need to show us something you grew: an account, a channel, a series or a brand. You'll ideally be:

  • A proven creator – you've grown an account, you've had videos that travelled well beyond your normal reach, and you can tell us why they worked;

  • Obsessed with what works – you study what's working on TikTok, Reels and Shorts this week (not last year), you have strong opinions about hooks, and you're always learning what's taking off and what's dying;

  • Properly hands-on – you do most of the shooting and editing yourself and you're quick, and you use AI tools to go faster;

  • Comfortable on camera – you're happy being the talking head yourself, and even happier getting a great take out of an installer who's never been filmed;

  • Curious about the numbers – you check how every post did because you want the next one to be better, not because you love a dashboard;

  • Interested in installers – you see small business owners doing technically complex, physically demanding work, with a brilliant story in every one, and you want to understand their world, not just film it.

… and you'll hopefully also love heat pumps! 🤓

You may have seen us advertising several roles across Legal, Risk and Compliance. That is deliberate, not random. We've moved from 5 million customers to 7 million, and we are now building beyond 10 million. The legal, risk and privacy foundations have to be laid ahead of that growth, not scrambled together after it. New markets, new products and new partners all arrive with new data questions. Joining now means shaping the privacy programme while its biggest chapters are still ahead of it.

What makes this different

In many organisations, the data protection officer reviews things at the end of the process. Here, the role reaches the whole group. Your current role: one jurisdiction, one regime. This role: six markets, one customer promise.

The AI Whistleblower Initiative (https://aiwi.org) is an independent non-profit supporting frontier AI insiders who want to raise concerns. We do this through outreach and education of insiders, access to vetted legal and financial resources, and policy work. Our insights help strengthen internal and government reporting channels, advocate for better legislation, and promote the conditions under which concerns can reach the people best placed to act on them, with source protection at their core. Find a selection of our work here (https://aiwi.org/our-work).

Most high-stakes moments in AI over the coming years will involve frontier company insiders having and raising concerns: within companies, to regulators, or through other pathways.

Those insiders tell us they face enormous uncertainty along the “concern raising” path -- from detecting concerns to whether and how to voice concerns with maximum impact and minimal risk, which even legally protected whistleblowing can carry. To date, no organization has dedicated itself deeply to delivering the best strategic, frontier-AI-specific guidance to these individuals, their supporters, and their attorneys (our partners). You will update, design and implement AIWI’s internal security posture, and provide external guidance to AI insiders, whistleblowers and partners. You will also design and deliver training and guidance to would-be whistleblowers and AIWI’s partners.

In other words, you are as comfortable drafting an internal security policy or building an onboarding and device-provisioning plan as you are training whistleblowers on how to evade insider-threat-management (ITM) systems, or explaining natural language watermarking. The role

As our MI Analyst, you will tell our Contact Centre leaders what the data means and what to do about it, then build the tools that deliver it at scale. You will sit in the Workforce Planning team, working across all teams who deal with customer contacts and report to the Head of Workforce Planning. Each day, week and month we publish reporting on agent productivity, operational performance and business review data across multiple teams and two sites. The job is to go beyond filling in the numbers and answer the "so what":

  • What are our most immediate opportunities?

  • What do we do about them with operational leaders?

  • Where are we losing efficiency?

  • Where could the same hours deliver more?

You will also use AI to do this faster than any manual process could. We run Claude connected to our BI data lake, so the right person can pull data, build reports and automate repeatable work themselves, without waiting in a queue. We want someone who sees that and immediately starts asking what they can automate.

What you will do

Find the insight

  • Turn Contact Centre data into clear findings and recommendations, and tell leaders what to do, not just what happened.

  • Spot where we are losing efficiency or capacity, size each opportunity, and prioritise the ones worth acting on.

  • Add commentary to the reports you publish, so readers see the story behind the numbers.

  • Own our understanding of contact drivers: explain why customers contact us, how that is changing, and what we could do to reduce it or handle it better.

Build with AI, at scale

  • Use Claude and our BI data lake to pull data, build reports and automate manual collation.

  • Replace repeatable, manual reporting with automated, reliable processes, so your time goes on analysis.

  • Bring us ideas for what to automate next, and show the time and capacity you save.

  • Document what you build so others in the team can run and maintain it when required.

Run the reporting cadence

  • Deliver daily, weekly and monthly reporting on agent productivity, utilisation and key service metrics across phone, email, chat and messaging.

  • Prepare the data for our daily, weekly and monthly business reviews (WBR and MBR).

  • Keep stakeholders updated on what you are working on and when it will land, without being asked.

Own accuracy

  • Validate every output before you share it. You are the last line of quality control on your own work.

  • Check sources and definitions rather than trusting historical reports, and flag anything that looks wrong before others find it.

  • Cross check your reports against the WBR and other sources, so mismatches show up before stakeholders spot them.

Be our Contact Centre data partner to BI

  • Act as the Contact Centre data partner to our BI teams, and the link between them and our operational leaders.

  • Help validate data models, dashboards and metrics against what is really happening on the floor.

  • Spot data issues early, raise them with BI with clear examples, and see them through to a fix.

  • Turn operational questions into clear requirements for BI, and help test what they build before it goes live.

  • Keep metric definitions consistent across Zendesk, Talkdesk, Calabrio and Looker.

  • Help define and evolve Contact Centre KPIs as the business grows.

  • Support ad hoc analysis and reporting on test and learn initiatives, and on BPO partner performance.

We want someone who has already worked with data in a busy operation and wants to do much more with it. If you are curious, thorough and keen to build, we want to hear from you.

You will need

  • Real curiosity about data. You ask why a number moved, not just what it is.

  • The ability to turn analysis into a clear recommendation that a non-technical leader can act on.

  • Strong attention to detail, and the habit of sense checking your own work before anyone else sees it.

  • Experience as an analyst, with a real understanding of the data you work with: where it comes from, how it is built, and what it can and cannot tell you.

  • Hands on experience using AI tools such as Claude to analyse data or build things, or a strong track record of picking up new tools fast.

  • A drive to take ownership, without being prompted, of the reports and processes you run.

  • The ability to manage daily and weekly deadlines in a fast moving operation.

  • Experience in a Contact Centre or operations environment, and working knowledge of how AHT, occupancy, SLA and productivity are measured and what moves them.

  • Experience with BigQuery, dbt, Looker Studio or similar BI tools.

  • Experience with Zendesk, Talkdesk or Calabrio data.

  • Examples of something you automated or built that saved real time.

Why join us

  • Claude connected to our BI data lake, so you can build with real, live data from day one.

  • Your work is used every morning by operational leaders to run the day and directly impacts business performance.

  • Room to move from running reports to owning our Ops reporting automation.

About Abound

We’re redefining consumer lending in the UK, and beyond. Using advanced AI and Open Banking data, we make fair, affordable personal finance available to more people. While traditional lenders rely almost entirely on credit scores, we look at the full financial picture - how much you spend, and what you can afford to repay to build a deeper, more accurate understanding of each customer's unique financial situation.


And we've shown it works at scale. We’ve issued over £1.3bn in loans directly to customers while delivering market-leading credit performance - for every 10 defaults the industry expects, we see only 3. We also reached profitability just 2.5 years after launch.


Backed by £2bn+ of funding from top-tier investors including Citi, GSR Ventures, and Deutsche Bank, we’re recognised as one of Europe’s fastest-growing fintechs (Sifted, CNBC). Now, we’re expanding into new markets and product lines - and we’re looking for ambitious people who want to learn fast, take ownership, and grow with us.

About the role

We’re looking for a Junior Software Engineer to join our New Products & Geographies Engineering team in London. This team launches and scales new lending propositions in two directions: bringing Abound’s lending to customers in new countries and expanding our B2B offering for partners. We move quickly, exploring ideas through production-ready MVPs and iterating as products mature.

This is a hybrid role, with at least three days a week in our London office. It’s a great opportunity for someone early in their career who wants to grow quickly, work on real production systems, and learn how a high-growth fintech operates from the inside.

You’ll work alongside experienced engineers who will support you through code reviews, pairing, and mentorship. We value engineers who are curious about the business and are keen to work with stakeholders to improve processes and customer experience.

Our technology stack

Python (including FastAPI, OpenTelemetry, procrastinate, SQLAlchemy and Uvicorn), Postgres, MySQL, Liquibase, Retool, Docker and AWS.

What you’ll be doing:

  • Build and maintain features in our backend services, which can span any part of the lending lifecycle – from finding and onboarding new customers, to helping underwriters assess affordability, through to paying out and collecting loans

  • Take part in the full software development lifecycle: contributing to designs, writing tests, reviewing code and helping with deployments

  • Write clean, well-tested Python, with guidance and feedback from senior engineers

  • Work with colleagues in Product and Design, as well as internal users, to understand requirements and turn them into working software

  • Work closely with our React frontend developers to build the APIs and backend logic their features rely on

  • Write and improve SQL queries against our Postgres databases

  • Help troubleshoot and resolve system issues that affect our customers

  • Gradually take ownership of parts of the platform as your experience grows

Who you are:

You’ll need:

  • 0–2 years of professional software engineering experience, or equivalent experience from a degree, bootcamp, internships or personal projects

  • Working knowledge of Python – you don’t need to be an expert, but you’re comfortable writing, testing and debugging code

  • An understanding of core programming concepts such as data structures, object-oriented design and unit testing

  • Familiarity with SQL, relational databases and Git

  • To be able to work from our London office at least three days a week

You’ll do well here if you:

  • Have a sharp eye for detail – in lending, small mistakes can have a real impact on customers

  • Learn quickly, take initiative and work methodically through problems, even in a large, evolving codebase

  • Communicate clearly, ask questions, take on feedback and work well in a team

  • Have a genuine interest in fintech and how financial products work

Ideally you'll also have:

  • Experience with async Python or frameworks such as FastAPI

  • Basic familiarity with cloud platforms (AWS, GCP or Azure) or Docker

  • Knowledge of lending products or open banking

How we work:

To be successful here, our culture needs to energies you. Here’s how we operate:

  • High bar and real ownership: We’re a high-performing team, and we hire people who raise the bar and take pride in great work. We own outcomes, not tasks.

  • Focus on impact: We measure success by what we deliver to customers. We prioritise carefully so our energy goes where it makes the biggest difference.

MSF International

Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) is an international, independent, medical humanitarian organisation that delivers emergency aid to people affected by armed conflict, epidemics, healthcare exclusion and natural disasters. MSF offers assistance to people based only on need and irrespective of race, religion, gender or political affiliation. MSF International is the legal entity that binds MSF’s 26 sections, 28 associations and 16 branch offices together. Registered in Switzerland, MSF International provides coordination, information and support to the MSF Movement, as well as implements international projects and initiatives as requested.

I. CONTEXT

MSF consists of 6 Operational Centres (OCs) and 3 European Supply Centres (ESCs). In the supply domain there is a joint Supply Tansformational Topics Roadmap composed by several inter-OC and inter-ESC projects, and their number is growing due to the need to increase cooperation between MSF entities while improving the quality of MSF's supply chain. The capacity to measure performance and analyse data across different entities is therefore essential and is contributing to MSF ambitions on interoperability and climate.

The role of the International Office is to foster cooperation and coordination between MSF entities. The Supply Data Analyst will therefore act as a facilitator between the OCs and ESCs: bringing their representatives together, helping them build shared approaches on supply data and performance, and turning these agreements into concrete deliverables.

The Global Supply Data & Analytics (GSDA) team (previously SCPM) has been actively working to build the analytical and data foundations needed to support a global approach to supply chain performance management, and to contribute to the governance of supply data across entities. The team is led by the Supply Chain Analytics Manager and includes one Data Analysts and one data governance specialist; the Supply Data Analyst will join it as an additional analyst.

Reporting hierarchically and functionally to the Supply Chain Analytics Manager, the Supply Data Analyst will: collaborate closely with the supply chain professionals responsible for BI and performance management within the 6 OCs and 3 ESCs; work in close link with the ShARP (Shared Analytics and Reporting Project) team in SITS (Shared IT Services); on the existing UniField intersection reports; work alongside the GSDA team and the IO Supply team on projects related to supply chain data analytics; and interact with stakeholders across MSF, including finance, IT, medical, pharmacy, logistics and operations teams.

II. PURPOSE OF THE JOB

The Supply Data Analyst supports supply chain performance analysis and decision making across MSF by delivering reliable data, KPIs, reports and actionable recommendations. The position also fosters cooperation between the OCs and ESCs around shared supply data, turning agreements into concrete deliverables.

Within GSDA, the Supply Data Analyst will support the growing need for data management, reporting and analytics from the supply chain teams, including the monitoring of KPIs and the analysis of data coming from MSF information systems (such as UniField, Isystock or Akiba).

III. ACCOUNTABILITIES

The Supply Data Analyst is accountable for the following expected results and the activities deployed to achieve them.

1. UniField intersection reports are reliable, relevant and meet the needs of the OCs

a. Take over the existing UniField intersection reports in close link with the ShARP team and improve them (reliability, relevance, usability) based on users' feedback and identified gaps

b. Collect the reporting needs of each OC and consolidate them into a clear, prioritised set of requirements

c. Design and deliver new intersection reports in coordination with the ShARP team, with validation from the OC representatives

2. Supply data is available and of reliable quality for analysis

a. Extract, clean and consolidate supply data from UniField and other information systems

b. Check data consistency and quality, and report anomalies to the relevant teams

c. Document data sources, definitions and calculation methods

title: Offre de stage de recherche Master 2 ou dernière année d’école d’ingénieur
description:
Dates : 6 mois à partir de février ou mars 2027

Contexte du projet :

L’allègement des structures automobiles reste un levier majeur pour réduire la consommation et les émissions des véhicules, tout en répondant à des exigences croissantes de rigidité et de tenue au crash. Les pièces de caisse en blanc sont en grande majorité réalisées à partir de tôles d’acier mises en forme, dont la conception repose encore largement sur l’expertise et sur des itérations successives entre calcul et dessin.

L’optimisation topologique permet de déterminer la meilleure répartition de matière dans un domaine de conception donné. Appliquée à un domaine volumique 3D, elle conduit cependant à des structures massives ou de type treillis, difficilement transposables en pièces embouties d’épaisseur quasi constante. Le défi scientifique consiste à formuler une méthode capable de faire émerger, à partir d’un domaine volumique, des géométries représentatives de tôles (structures à parois minces), en maîtrisant l’épaisseur et la fabricabilité, sous chargements statiques puis dynamiques.

Ce stage s’inscrit dans le cadre d’une collaboration de recherche entre le LTDS et ArcelorMittal Global R&D. Il a vocation à se poursuivre par une thèse CIFRE en cas de résultats concluants.

L’objectif du stage sera de développer et d’évaluer une première méthodologie d’optimisation topologique 3D aboutissant à une solution en tôle d’acier, en s’appuyant sur une structure automobile.

Les missions pourront comprendre :

•Un état de l’art des méthodes d’optimisation topologique conduisant à des structures minces de type coque (contrôle d’épaisseur par filtrage et projection, contraintes de longueur caractéristique, approches par composants explicites ou level-set).

•Le développement d’un algorithme d’optimisation 3D appliqué à une pièce automobile soumise à des chargements statiques.

•L’extension de la méthode à des solutions plus avancées proposées par ArcelorMittal.

Les missions pourront être adaptées en fonction du profil du candidat et de l’avancement du projet.


Profil recherché : étudiant(e) en Master 2 ou équivalent (stage ingénieur) dans le domaine de la mécanique numérique, du calcul des structures ou des mathématiques appliquées.

Compétences souhaitées : méthode des éléments finis, optimisation numérique, programmation scientifique (Python, MATLAB ou C++). Des connaissances en optimisation topologique ou en dynamique rapide (LS-DYNA, Radioss) seront appréciées.

Encadrement : Frédéric Gillot (LTDS, École Centrale de Lyon) ; Daoming Yu, Alexandre Blaise et Cristian Alvarez (ArcelorMittal Global R&D).

L’accueil au laboratoire est soumis à une autorisation préalable (procédure FSD, 2 à 3 mois de délai) : les candidatures (CV, lettre de motivation, relevés de notes) sont à adresser dès que possible.

description:
Are you looking to have an impact on the daily life of millions of entrepreneurs in France (and tomorrow in Europe)?

Are you looking for a work environment that values trust, proactivity, and autonomy?

Then Pennylane is the right place for you !

 

Our vision

We aim to become the most beloved financial Operating System of French SMEs and Accounting Firms (and soon, European ones).

We help entrepreneurs rid themselves of time-consuming tasks related to accounting and finance while providing them with access to key financial information to assist in making the best decisions for their business.

 

About us

Pennylane is one of the fastest growing Fintechs in France (and soon to be in Europe!)

 

In 5 years of existence, we’ve managed to :

💻 Make ourselves known as a groundbreaking accounting and financial software for small businesses and their accountants

💰 Raise a total of €400 millions, including from Sequoia, the famous fund from the Silicon Valley who invested early in companies like Google, Facebook, Airbnb, Stripe, Paypal and much more...

👨‍👩‍👧‍👦 Grow from 7 cofounders to 1000 happy Pennylaners : we’re now recognized as one of the greatest places to work in France (and also remotely), with a 4.6/5 rating on Glassdoor.

🌍 Build an international environment with more than 25 nationalities, with a strong remote-friendly culture, where 30% of the employees are already working from all parts of Europe

🤝 Earn the trust of thousands of customers and accounting firms and obtain outstanding ratings

🚀 Already more than 900,000 small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and over 6000 accounting firms use Pennylane in France!

 

In 2024, we implemented an organizational structure built around business 'tracks'. This approach integrates key stakeholders across marketing, sales, product, and customer care into unified teams focused on specific product lines or client segments. Each track operates as a mini-business, empowered with dedicated resources (e.g., product marketing, data analytics, and operational support) and direct accountability for performance.

 
 

Why this role matters at Pennylane

 

As Chief of Staff to the CTO, you operate as a senior leader in the Tech organisation. Your leverage does not come from managing teams but from owning the hardest problems that sit between them, and from being technical enough to earn the trust of the other engineering leaders.

You are the person the CTO trusts with ambiguous, org-wide problems. You turn that ambiguity into a clear framing, a decision, an owner and a measurable outcome.

This is not a coordination role. You are expected to have opinions on engineering strategy, staffing choices and technical trade-offs, and to defend them in front of the Tech leadership team.

 

Team and Context

Pennylane's Tech organisation is 70+ squads, each led by an Engineering Manager working with a PM and a Product Designer. We serve 1.5m+ customers and we want to scale in Europe. At that size, the hard problems are no longer inside a squad: how the organisation plans, how it decides, how it measures itself, how it invests in foundations without stalling product delivery. That is your perimeter.

You report directly to Quentin, Co-founder & CTO. Your influence comes from the scope of what you own and from credibility with senior engineering leaders, which is why we ask for a technical background. As the organisation grows, this role can evolve towards a management position.

Key missions

Engineering strategy and transversal initiatives

  • Own the strategic, cross-organization initiatives that no single squad can carry: platform or architecture programmes, reliability and quality step-changes, engineering productivity, technical debt paydown

  • Frame the problem, build the technical and business case, secure alignment across Engineering, Product and Security to drive execution

  • Lead the Tech side of company-level programmes (e.g. European expansion, major compliance or infrastructure shifts) alongside the rest of the Tech leadership

Planning & Performance tracking

  • Own the Tech planning cycle: collect the inputs, surface the trade-offs (capacity vs. platform, run vs. new bets), and drive the arbitration with Tech leadership

  • Drive the definition and calibration of Tech OKRs, and hold the organisation accountable

  • Define what "good" looks like for a 70+ squad engineering organization and build the metrics that measure it (delivery cadence, reliability, quality, staffing and attrition, engineering satisfaction)

Decision-making and leadership cadence

  • Own the Tech leadership operating system: staff meetings, QBRs, roadmap and architecture reviews. You design them, set the agenda, write or commission the pre-reads, frame the decisions to be made, and make sure decisions land

  • Maintain the CTO's decision log: what was decided, by whom, with what trade-off, and what happened next

  • Raise the quality of decision-making across the Tech leadership team

Communication

  • Lead internal and operational communications across the engineering organization, building clear messaging systems from board decks down to team-wide updates

Who you’ll work with?

  • CTO and Tech leadership (Head of Engineering / Head of Data / Senior Engineering Managers)

  • Rest of the leadership (CPO, VP Strategic Initiatives)

  • Other relevant teams (e.g. Security, Finance, People)

Who we’re looking for

Must-have

  • An engineering degree (engineering, computer science or equivalent scientific curriculum)

  • Technical fluency: you can read a design doc, follow an architecture discussion, challenge an estimate or a trade-off, and be taken seriously by senior engineers

  • 7-10 years of experience, including significant time inside a tech organisation at scale (multiple squads, platform teams), where you have lived the problems of scaling engineering

  • A track record of owning complex, cross-organisational initiatives from framing to measurable outcome with senior stakeholders

  • Outstanding written communication: this role produces documents that senior people act on

  • Fluency in English

Nice-to-have

  • A hands-on engineering past: software engineer, engineering manager, Technical Program Manager, architect or equivalent

  • Experience as a Chief of Staff, VP/Director of Engineering Operations, or in a strategy & operations function inside a product-led tech company

What you can expect?

Within one month

  • You'll complete the company and Tech onboarding, including our application, accounting domain and engineering practices

  • You'll have met the Tech leadership team and formed your own view of where the organisation loses time, quality or alignment

  • You'll have taken ownership of the leadership cadence and the next planning milestone

Within 3-6 months

  • You'll be leading selected org-wide strategic initiatives end-to-end, with a measurable target

  • The Tech organisation will have a metrics picture it trusts and uses to make decisions

  • You'll be a recognised voice in the senior tech community at Pennylane, consulted on decisions rather than just informed of them

  • You'll be shaping the engineering narrative that the rest of the company and the board hear

Recruitment Process

- Screening interview with Barbara - Senior Recruiter (30 mins)

- An interview with Eric - VP Strategic Initiatives (45 mins)

- An interview with Quentin - CTO (1h)

- A Business Case to prepare at home and to present (1h)

- A final interview with Nathan - Head of Product Strat&Ops (45 mins)

What do we do to make your work life easier

 

🌴 Wherever you are based, you will get 25 vacations days paid by Pennylane

💵 You’ll have a competitive compensation package

📈 You'll get company shares to enjoy a piece of the success story you're building with us

🏡 You’ll have a budget to turn your home into a more comfortable workspace, as well as a monthly allowance to work from a coworking space whenever you feel like it

⛹️ Through our partner Gymlib, you’ll have access to 8000 fitness spaces in Europe and more than 300 activities related to wellness

🇬🇧 You’ll have access to Busuu to perfect your English or your French

💻 You’ll get the latest Apple equipment

🏢 Depending on the teams and the requirements of the position - you'll be able to work remotely from your country of residence, as long as it is in Europe and within a maximum time difference of two hours from the CET time zone

🎉 We are committed to regularly coming together for company events such as Tech Days (which bring remote Pennylaners together every 3 months) or our annual company seminar, fostering significant moments of cohesion for everyone.

 

If you are based in France, you will have a French contract following French regulation on top of the additional perks : 6 to 12 RTT, 5 weeks PTOs, lunch credits (Swile), Alan Blue healthcare cover and regular events in cities where Pennylaners are mostly presents (Lyon, Bordeaux, Nantes…)

We're working on providing those last advantages to our people based outside of France as well, but it can be quite more complex depending on different countries.

 

Who are we looking for ?

To thrive at Pennylane, you need :

-To speak English (level is assessed and appreciated according to the department you’re applying to)

-To be energized by an ever-shifting work environment

-To be highly collaborative (within your team or other stakeholders)

-Sufficiently experienced to prioritize business-led actions on your day to day activity

 

We know that some people are less likely to apply than others, if they don’t feel like they meet the full list of criteria.

If you’re hesitating, we encourage you to apply : who knows, it might be the start of a meaningful and long-lasting collaboration.

Harmattan AI is a next-generation defense prime building autonomous and scalable defense systems. Following the close of a $200M Series B, valuing the company at $1.4 billion, we are expanding our teams and capabilities to deliver mission-critical systems to allied forces.

Our work is guided by clear values: building technologies with real-world impact, pursuing excellence in everything we do, setting ambitious goals, and taking on the hardest technical challenges. We operate in a demanding environment where rigor, ownership, and execution are expected.

About the Role

As a Hardware (Electronics) Engineer within our Electronic Warfare team, you will design and develop the RF hardware and electronic front-ends at the core of our electronic warfare and signal intelligence systems – from concept to field deployment. You will work hand-in-hand with system, software and mechanical teams to turn architecture needs into robust, high-performance hardware, and to ensure overall performance, robustness and reliability.

 

Responsibilities

  • RF Front-End Design: Design and develop radio and radar RF front-ends, from specification through to validation.

  • Hardware Architecture: Drive the hardware architecture of EW/SIGINT systems, ensuring performance, robustness and manufacturability.

  • High-Power & High-Voltage Electronics: Design high-power switching supplies (including narrow pulse generation) and high-voltage PCBs, supplies and shielding.

  • Integration & Validation: Lead board bring-up, RF integration, prototyping and validation against performance targets.

  • Technical Coordination: Collaborate across software, mechanical, GNC and ML teams on system integration and technical interfaces.

  • System Reviews & Documentation: Contribute to design and architecture reviews, maintaining consistency between requirements, design and testing.

Candidate Requirements

  • Strong background in RF hardware design is mandatory, including radio or radar front-end design.

  • No prior Electronic Warfare experience required.

  • Experience in RF integration is a plus.

  • Experience with high-power switching supplies (narrow pulse generation) is a definite plus.

  • Experience with high-voltage PCB / supply design and shielding.

  • MSc in Electrical / Electronics Engineering; PhD is a plus.

  • Broad engineering culture with understanding of mechanical, software and embedded systems.

  • Rigorous, structured and mission-driven mindset with strong analytical skills.

  • Excellent communication and documentation abilities.

 

We look forward to hearing how you can help shape the future of autonomous defense systems at Harmattan AI.

description:
About Odys

At Odys, we’re mobilizing power, with Hybrid Power Systems developed for aerospace and in-demand everywhere. It’s the kind of mission diversity that demands a fresh way of thinking.

We began with an early bet on hybrid, when the mobility industry was focused on batteries. We designed, tested, and validated our first 1 MW high-speed generator in 12 months. And then we pushed further, developing systems with greater power density in less time. Today, our Hybrid Power Systems offer outputs ranging from 20 kW to 4 MW, with applications in the air or on the ground.

One of those applications is Laila, an unmanned drone designed for critical logistics and defense missions. With its 100 kW-class onboard Hybrid Power System, Laila can support medical cold-chain transport or serve as an aerial platform for counter-UAS measures.

The market interest has been overwhelming: Over 30 inbound requests from leading US and global manufacturers, and 14+ DoD contracts.

Our team comes from deep tech and aerospace, with backgrounds spanning drone and aircraft development, high-volume production, and electrified mobility.

We operate with urgency and ownership at every level. We validated high-speed generator technology faster than our peers, not because we skipped steps, but because we've been doing this long enough to know which ones matter most.

Creating the future of power, in the air and on the ground, is a challenge we’ve been training our entire lives for. If that sounds like you, this is the opportunity you’ve been waiting for.

 

About The Role

Odys Aviation is seeking a senior business development manager for Europe. Your role is to turn European interest in Odys into signed contracts across aircraft, certification services, and power systems. The role sits with Odys Aviation GmbH in Munich, our European entity, reports to the GmbH Managing Director, and works integrated with our business development team in the US.

The targets are set: first revenues by mid-2027, and 25% of the GmbH cost covered from its own revenues by the end of 2027. Your pipeline secures our growth beyond 2028: Growth of the GmbH, and growth of the Odys group. Every Euro you bring in builds the GmbH: site, test facility, Design Organisation Approval, and jobs.

This is a hands-on role in a lean environment. You directly own your numbers, not a team, and no layers. There is no established European sales organization to inherit. You start from our current leads to get first tangible projects, you open new doors, and you run each deal yourself: From the first call, through technical alignment involving our experts, to negotiation, to the contract ready to sign, to continuing key account support of the customer.

You bridge two worlds: US startup speed and the way European customers decide and buy. You are Odys' boots on the ground in Europe. You balance quick wins with deals of real impact, and you secure the group resources your contracts need.

Don't meet all desired requirements? Studies have shown that some people are less likely to apply to jobs unless they meet every single desired qualification. At Odys, we are dedicated to building an authentic workplace, so if you're excited about this role but your experience doesn't align perfectly with every desired qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway.

What You'll Do

  • Convert our current European leads into signed contracts for aircraft, certification services, and power systems

  • Open doors with UAS and aircraft OEMs, starting with battery-electric players moving to hybrid

  • Run deals end to end: qualification, offer, pricing, negotiation, and a contract ready to sign

  • Integrate our product leads in Munich and the US to complement your efforts in the most efficient way for certification services, power systems, and aircraft expertise

  • Balance quick wins with deals of real impact

  • Secure the group resources that your contracts need, from proposal to delivery

  • Keep Odys high up on the European public funding radar, from Bavaria to Brussels, and land funding programs that make a difference for Odys

  • Keep your pipeline up to date and in weekly synch with the broader commercial team

What We're Looking For

  • Degree in engineering, business, or a related discipline, or equivalent experience

  • Substantial experience (typically 8+ years) in B2B sales or business development, with a proven trail of signed and relevant deals in aviation, UAS, propulsion, or power systems

  • An established network among European aviation OEMs, operators, and suppliers that you can call tomorrow

  • Proven startup or early-stage experience: shifting priorities, short resources, and delivery anyway

  • Hands-on contract skills: You draft, negotiate, and close the commercial terms

  • Technical depth to discuss power, mass, and integration with engineers, and the judgment to know when to bring in the experts

  • Persistence across sales cycles measured in quarters

  • Comfortable working across two entities and two continents, with one manager and close deal partners

  • Business-fluent English and German

Nice to Have

  • Experience working in export-controlled environments (e.g. EU Dual-Use Regulation, German AWG/AWV, U.S. EAR/ITAR) and with export compliance processes.

  • Further major EU or Middle-East languages

  • Access to European defense customers and programs, such as ASAP & EDIRPA / SAFE / AGILE, EDF, NATO DIANA, or national procurement programs

  • Experience with EU and national public funding programs

  • Freude an Konzeption & Kundenkontakt: Spaß an konzeptionellen Tätigkeiten und der Interaktion mit Kunden.

  • Abwechslungsreicher Arbeitsalltag in einem dynamischen Team mit flachen Hierarchien.

title: Senior CRM Manager (m/w/d)
description:
Du baust als erste CRM-Person das Retention-Ressort einer Supplement-Marke mit über 200.000 Kund:innen auf — von null, mit eigenem Budget und Tool-Stack.

Über 200.000 Menschen haben bei Wehle Sports, eine Marke der Supplement Hub Gruppe, schon bestellt. Die Marke wächst im Direktgeschäft um rund 60 % pro Jahr — getragen vor allem von der Neukundengewinnung. Was nach dem ersten Kauf passiert, wurde bisher über Agenturen gesteuert. Genau dort liegt der nächste große Hebel: Die ersten 90 Tage nach dem Erstkauf entscheiden, ob aus Kund:innen Stammkund:innen werden.

Dafür gibt es diese Rolle. Du bist die erste CRM-Person im Haus und baust das Ressort von null auf: Lifecycle-Flows, E-Mail, SMS und WhatsApp, ein Loyalty-Programm, das bestehende Abo. Wehle Sports soll im DTC wachsen — CRM ist dafür neben der Neukundengewinnung der zweite große Hebel.

Und du baust nicht nur für eine Marke. Die Supplement Hub Gruppe vereint sieben Marken mit über 500 Produkten und rund 50–60 Mio. € Umsatz. Was bei Wehle funktioniert, wird zum Playbook für die ganze Gruppe — und aus der ersten CRM-Rolle wird in zwei bis drei Jahren die Leitung eines gruppenweiten CRM-Teams.

Warum es diese Rolle gibt

Wehle Sports ist über starke Produkte und Neukundengewinnung groß geworden. E-Mail, SMS und ein Abo-Programm gibt es — aber es gibt kein CRM-Team, keinen eigenen Tool-Stack über Klaviyo hinaus und keine durchgängige Logik, die Erstkäufer:innen systematisch zum zweiten und dritten Kauf führt. Bisher lag das bei Agenturen.

Das ändert sich jetzt. Das DTC-Team wird gerade neu aufgebaut. Retention soll so schnell wie sinnvoll ins Haus, eine Agentur bleibt nur dort, wo sie nachweislich mehr bringt. Dafür braucht es jemanden, der kein fertiges System verwaltet, sondern das erste baut.

Was du bewegen wirst

Nicht als Aufgabenliste, sondern als das, was in zwölf Monaten anders sein soll:

  • Die ersten 90 Tage sind gebaut. Welcome, Post-Purchase, Replenishment, Cross-Sell, Winback und Abandonment-Flows laufen, sind getestet und führen Neukund:innen gezielt zum Wiederkauf und zu passenden Produkten rund um Gelenkgesundheit.

  • Die Kanäle spielen zusammen. E-Mail, SMS und WhatsApp sind ein Lifecycle statt drei Silos — und WhatsApp ist ein eigener Retention-Kanal mit eigener Liste.

  • Loyalty ist live, das Abo wächst. Du hast ein Loyalty-Programm ausgewählt, gebaut und gelauncht und das Abo-Programm bei Quote, Churn und Kündigungsstrecken weiterentwickelt.

  • Die Zahlen sind deine. Segmentierung und Kohorten-Reporting zu Retention, CLV und CLV:CAC stehen — und du steuerst das Ressort danach, nicht nach Öffnungsraten.

  • Das Ressort steht. Tool-Stack, CRM-Budget und Insourcing-Plan sind entschieden — von dir, mit Business Case. Die Prozesse sind so dokumentiert, dass sie auf die nächste Marke übertragbar sind.

Wie hier gearbeitet wird

Supplement Hub ist effizienzgetrieben: Calls gibt es, wenn sie nötig sind, Entscheidungen fallen in Tagen. Neue Produkte sind in zwei bis drei Wochen von der Idee im Lager — wenn dein Cross-Sell ein Produkt braucht, ist das kein Jahresprojekt.

  • Du entscheidest über Tools und Budget. Freigaben brauchst du nur, wenn du über das gemeinsam vereinbarte Budget hinausgehst.

  • Am Anfang baust und verschickst du selbst — es gibt noch kein Team, das umsetzt. Das Team entsteht mit dir.

  • Testen ist ausdrücklich gewollt: neue Kanäle, Angebote und Mechaniken ausprobieren, messen, skalieren oder stoppen. Fehler sind erlaubt, wenn sie gemessen werden.

  • Das Team arbeitet remote im DACH-Raum und trifft sich regelmäßig zu Team-Events und Workations in Berlin.

Wen wir suchen

Wir suchen keinen perfekten Lebenslauf, sondern einen Nachweis: Du hast Kund:innen einer Consumer-Marke schon einmal messbar zum Wiederkauf gebracht.

Das brauchst du auf jeden Fall

  • Rund fünf Jahre CRM- oder Retention-Erfahrung bei einer B2C-Marke im Consumer-Goods- oder D2C-E-Commerce-Umfeld — etwa Supplements, Food, Beauty oder Skincare.

  • Du kannst an Zahlen zeigen, dass du Wiederkaufrate oder CLV gesteigert hast — idealerweise auf Kohortenebene.

  • Ein B2C-CRM-Tool beherrschst du auf Expertenniveau: Flows, Segmente und Reporting hast du selbst gebaut, nicht nur gebrieft.

  • Du setzt selbst um. Konzepte schreiben reicht hier am Anfang nicht — du baust und verschickst, bis es ein Team gibt.

  • Kohortenanalysen in Sheets, Excel oder einem BI-Tool sind für dich Alltag.

  • Fließendes Deutsch in Wort und Schrift, weil du für deutschsprachige Kund:innen schreibst.

Das ist ein Plus, aber kein Muss

  • Erfahrung mit Nahrungsergänzungsmitteln und Health Claims

  • Klaviyo und Shopify Plus im Tagesgeschäft

  • Abo-Modelle: Churn, Pausen- und Kündigungsstrecken gesteuert

  • Ein Loyalty-Programm oder einen WhatsApp-Kanal aufgebaut

  • Schon einmal einen CRM-Bereich von null aufgebaut oder Agenturthemen ins Haus geholt

Du erfüllst nicht jeden Punkt, bist aber sicher, die Lücke schnell zu schließen? Dann melde dich.

Die Vorteile für dich

  • Ein weißes Blatt mit voller Hoheit. Tool-Stack (außer Klaviyo und Shopify Plus), CRM-Budget und Struktur entscheidest du.

  • Ein Mentor als Chef. Du berichtest an einen Head of DTC, der eine D2C-Marke vom sieben- in den achtstelligen Bereich mitskaliert hat.

  • Ein Weg nach oben, der real ist. Funktioniert der Aufbau, führst du in zwei bis drei Jahren ein eigenes CRM-Team für die ganze Gruppe.

  • Ein Bonus, der an deiner Wirkung hängt — gemessen an der CLV-Entwicklung deiner Kundenkohorten.

  • Rückenwind statt Rechtfertigungsdruck. Eine finanzstarke Gruppe mit sieben Marken, über 200.000 Kund:innen bei Wehle und ein DTC-Geschäft, das um rund 60 % pro Jahr wächst.

  • Tempo bis ins Lager. Neue Produkte in zwei bis drei Wochen — deine Cross-Sell-Ideen werden zu echten Produkten.

  • 100 % Remote in der DACH-Zeitzone, mit regelmäßigen Team-Events und Workations in Berlin.

Warum du dich jetzt melden solltest

Selten findest du eine Marke, bei der Produkt, Nachfrage und 200.000 Kund:innen schon da sind — und nur die Retention fehlt. Genau da steht Wehle Sports heute. Wenn du CRM nicht verwalten, sondern einmal richtig aufbauen willst, ist das dein Zeitpunkt.

Kontakt

Diese Position wird über A-Level besetzt. Fragen zur Rolle, zur Vergütung oder zum Prozess gehen direkt an Sören Gerdes.

Du bringst Tracking-Praxis mit, lernst bei uns Privacy Tech und betreust eigene Enterprise-Kunden wie Commerzbank, FedEx oder On.

Ohne Einwilligung keine Daten, ohne saubere Daten kein Marketing. Die Regeln dafür werden in Europa wie in den USA jedes Jahr strenger — und die meisten Unternehmen merken erst spät, dass ein Cookie-Banner keine Strategie ist. Genau an dieser Stelle arbeiten wir: Seit 2018 setzen wir Datenschutz technisch um, seit 2020 auch US-Privacy-Regulierung, in über 400 Projekten für mehr als 80 Kunden in 15 Ländern.

Du kannst Tracking? Dann lernst du bei uns, was in Deutschland kaum jemand kann. Spezialisten für Privacy Tech gibt es am Markt praktisch nicht — deshalb suchen wir niemanden, der es schon kann, sondern jemanden mit echter Measurement-Erfahrung, dem wir Consent und Privacy selbst beibringen. Ab Tag 1 betreust du eigene Kunden, baust Setups mit GA4, Google Tag Manager und Server-Side selbst und sprichst mit Anwält:innen genauso wie mit Entwickler:innen.

Wir sind neun Leute, wachsen seit Jahren organisch und bauen gerade unser Team in Hamburg auf. Wer hier überzeugt, übernimmt in ein bis zwei Jahren Verantwortung für das Consulting-Team.

Warum es diese Rolle gibt

Wir wachsen in beiden Bereichen — im Measurement und noch stärker in Privacy Tech. Im Measurement sind wir die unabhängige Messinstanz neben den Kampagnen-Agenturen unserer Kunden: Wer die Kampagne verkauft, sollte nicht auch das Reporting dazu liefern. In Privacy Tech gibt es kaum spezialisierte Agenturen; Aufträge landen sonst bei großen IT-Häusern, die das Thema nebenbei mitmachen.

Bisher hat unser Geschäftsführer das Consulting-Team allein geführt. Das stößt an Grenzen. Deshalb suchen wir eine Person, die heute als Senior Consultant einsteigt und morgen mitführen will — und die bewusst in Hamburg sitzt, damit wir hier mehr Team werden.

Was du bewegen wirst

Nicht als Aufgabenliste, sondern als das, was in zwölf Monaten anders sein soll:

  • Deine Kunden laufen ohne Umweg. Du bist feste Ansprechperson für eigene Enterprise-Kunden und führst nach einem Jahr auch große Projekte mit mehreren Kolleg:innen.

  • Die Daten stimmen. Tracking mit GA4, Google Tag Manager und Server-Side GTM ist sauber aufgesetzt, und Fehler im Website-Code findest und behebst du selbst.

  • Consent ist kein Banner mehr. Du richtest Consent-Management (vor allem Usercentrics) und Consent Mode ein und erklärst Kunden, welche Chancen und Risiken darin stecken.

  • Die Daten fließen weiter. Je nach Interesse baust du Datenflüsse nach BigQuery bis hin zu Pipelines und Dashboards.

  • Das Team wird stärker. Du gibst Wissen weiter, gestaltest Standards mit und wächst in Richtung Teamlead.

Wie bei uns gearbeitet wird

  • Eine Person entscheidet. Kein Gremium, keine Freigabeschleifen — mit dem Geschäftsführer klärst du Dinge direkt.

  • Eigene Projekte, eigene Entscheidungen. Es gibt keine Projektmanager, die dir Arbeit zuteilen. Du organisierst deine Projekte selbst.

  • Wir erklären das Warum. Kunden bekommen nicht nur ein Setup, sondern verstehen, warum es so gebaut ist.

  • International. Rund die Hälfte unserer Privacy-Kunden sitzt in den USA, dazu Middle East, Südamerika und Asien.

  • Direkter Draht zu Usercentrics. Als engster Partner weltweit sehen wir neue Funktionen, bevor sie live gehen.

Wen wir suchen

Einen technischen Marketer aus dem Tracking — nicht den reinen Analysten, nicht den Entwickler.

Das brauchst du auf jeden Fall

  • Du hast Tracking-Setups mit GA4 und Google Tag Manager selbst gebaut — nicht nur Reports daraus gelesen.

  • Du verstehst, wie eine Website funktioniert: JavaScript kannst du lesen und kleine Skripte selbst schreiben, HTML und CSS sind dir vertraut, und du weißt, was ein CMS, ein Frontend oder React ist.

  • Du sprichst gern mit Kunden, gibst Informationen von dir aus weiter und suchst Lösungen statt Gründe, warum etwas nicht geht.

  • Du organisierst dich selbst und brauchst niemanden, der dir hinterherläuft.

  • Du wohnst im Raum Hamburg oder willst hierher ziehen und bist gern regelmäßig im Office.

Das ist ein Plus, aber kein Muss

  • Erfahrung in einer Agentur, bei einem Dienstleister oder in einem jungen Scale-up

  • Server-Side Tagging, BigQuery oder SQL

  • Erste Berührung mit Consent-Management-Plattformen

  • Kunden aus den USA oder anderen Ländern betreut

  • Du warst schon selbstständig oder freiberuflich unterwegs

  • Du hast Lust, in ein bis zwei Jahren ein Team zu führen

Privacy Tech musst du nicht mitbringen — das bringen wir dir bei. Wenn du die Tracking-Seite kannst und beim Rest sicher bist, dass du schnell lernst: melde dich.

Die Vorteile für dich

  • Ein Spezialgebiet, das kaum jemand hat. Privacy Tech lernst du bei uns von Grund auf — Wissen, das am Markt selten ist.
