title: Senior Sales Manager, Regional Enterprise
description:
About Wolt

At Wolt, we create technology that brings joy, simplicity and earnings to the neighborhoods of the world. In 2014 we started with delivery of restaurant food. Now we're building the delivery of (almost) everything and you'll find us in over 500 cities in 30 countries around the world. In 2022 we joined forces with DoorDash and together we keep on dreaming big and expanding across the globe.

Working at Wolt isn't always easy, but it's definitely exciting. Here you'll learn more, build more, and ship more than in most other companies. You'll be challenged a lot, but also have a lot of fun on the way. So, if you're a self-starter with drive and entrepreneurial spirit, this could be the ride of your life.

Senior Sales Regional Enterprise Manager

At Wolt, we create technology that brings local communities, merchants and customers closer together. What started with restaurant delivery has grown into a broader local commerce platform, helping customers discover and access more of what their cities have to offer.

As our Retail business continues to grow, we're looking for a Senior Sales Regional Enterprise Manager to expand our selection of high-value regional retail partners. You'll join our Sales team and take ownership of some of the most important regional acquisition opportunities across priority retail verticals, helping shape what customers can find on Wolt in their cities. This role can be based in Berlin, Cologne, Frankfurt, Hamburg or Munich .

What you'll be doing

In this role, you'll own the acquisition and development of high-value regional Enterprise retail partners in Germany, from identifying and engaging the right prospects through commercial negotiations, signing and initial rollout. You'll combine strong commercial execution with a strategic view on which partners can have the greatest impact on Wolt's selection, coverage and long-term growth.

Day-to-day in this role you'll:

  • Own the end-to-end sales cycle for regional Enterprise retail opportunities, from prospecting and qualification through negotiation, contracting and signing.
  • Build and manage a high-quality pipeline of larger regional retailers and multi-location partners across priority verticals such as grocery, convenience, pet, pharmacy and beauty.
  • Develop a deep understanding of prospective partners' businesses and create compelling commercial propositions that demonstrate the value of partnering with Wolt.
  • Lead complex commercial negotiations, balancing partner needs with sustainable economics and Wolt's long-term business objectives.
  • Build strong relationships with senior decision-makers and act as a trusted commercial partner throughout the sales process.
  • Work closely with internal teams including Operations, Account Management, Finance, Legal, Marketing and Product to structure partnerships and enable successful launches.
  • Take ownership beyond the signature, ensuring a strong handover and initial rollout so that newly acquired partners can successfully go live and scale.
  • Use market insights, pipeline data and commercial learnings to identify opportunities, prioritize the highest-impact accounts and continuously improve our regional Enterprise sales approach.
  • Contribute to sharing best practices and raising the bar for Enterprise sales execution across the wider team.

Our humble expectations

  • You have significant experience in B2B sales, business development or strategic partnerships, ideally working with Enterprise or other complex, multi-stakeholder customers.
  • You have a strong track record of independently managing and closing complex commercial opportunities from initial outreach through contract signature.
  • You're an excellent negotiator and understand how to build partnerships that create sustainable value for both sides.
  • You're comfortable engaging and influencing senior stakeholders, both externally and across cross-functional internal teams.
  • You combine a hands-on, results-oriented sales mindset with strong commercial judgment and the ability to prioritize opportunities based on their strategic impact.
  • You're highly structured and comfortable managing multiple opportunities and stakeholders simultaneously while maintaining strong attention to detail.
  • You're comfortable working with data and commercial metrics to evaluate opportunities, build business cases and inform decisions.
  • You communicate clearly and persuasively and are fluent in German and English. 

What we offer

This is an opportunity to play a meaningful role in the next phase of Wolt's Retail growth. You'll have direct ownership of high-impact regional partnerships and the autonomy to take opportunities from first conversation all the way through to launch.

You'll work at the intersection of sales, strategy and operations, collaborating with experienced colleagues across Wolt while building relationships with some of the most important retailers in the market. The role offers substantial commercial ownership and exposure while giving you the opportunity to develop further in Enterprise sales and contribute to how we scale our Retail business.

You'll also join a fast-moving international environment where good ideas can quickly turn into action, with the tools, support and trust to take ownership of your work and make a visible impact.

Next steps

If this sounds like an opportunity you'd be excited about, we'd love to hear from you.

After you apply, our Talent Acquisition team will review your application and get in touch with selected candidates for an initial conversation. The process will typically include interviews with the hiring team and relevant stakeholders, giving you the opportunity to learn more about the role, team and business while we get to know your experience and approach.

Depending on the role and location, the process may also include a practical case or commercial exercise. We'll share the exact interview steps and expectations with you as you progress through the process.

Our Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion

We're committed to growing and empowering a more inclusive community within our company, industry, and cities. That's why we hire and cultivate diverse teams of people from all backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives. We believe that true innovation happens when everyone has room at the table and the tools, resources, and opportunity to excel.

title: (Senior) Flight Control & State Estimation Engineer (m/f/d)
description:
About the Role

Our flight-control system is already flying Skyron400. Now we want to make it faster, sharper and more capable. 

As our Senior Flight Control & State Estimation Engineer, you will take technical ownership of the control and estimation capabilities that determine how precisely our interceptor estimates its state, how quickly it reacts and how aggressively it can operate without compromising stability or robustness. 

From advanced estimation and control algorithms to embedded Rust optimization and flight-test analysis, you will set technical direction, make decisions based on real flight data and drive measurable improvements in aircraft performance. 

What is your Day to Day Mission:

  • Take technical ownership of flight-control and state-estimation architecture, priorities and validation. 

  • Improve state estimation using Kalman filters, IIM, particle filters and model based approaches. 

  • Fuse IMU, radar, camera and ToF data into robust vehicle and target-state estimates. 

  • Increase the accuracy of velocity and position estimation in GPS-denied environments. 

  • Optimize sensor filtering, synchronization, outlier rejection and latency compensation. 

  • Own the design, implementation and tuning of flight-control algorithms for maximum agility, precision and stability. 

  • Identify real flight dynamics from recorded data and use them to improve models, estimators and controllers. 

  • Improve sensor and vehicle models used in simulation, SIL and HIL environments. 

  • Profile and optimize flight-critical Rust code for deterministic execution and minimum latency. 

  • Plan and lead flight-test analysis, identify performance limits and turn every flight into the next improvement. 


What You Bring to the Team

This is a senior flight-control role. We are looking for deep expertise in flight-control design and tuning, together with a strong understanding of how control, state estimation, sensing and embedded implementation interact as one complete system. 

  • At least four years of professional experience developing and tuning flight-control systems, including implementation and testing on real systems. Experience with drones or other UAVs is strongly preferred. 

  • Exceptional candidates coming directly from university may be considered only if they can demonstrate at least three years of substantial hands-on flight-control experience through projects, research programs, student teams or comparable work, including implementation and testing on real systems. 

  • Deep foundations in control theory, state estimation, sensor fusion and flight dynamics. 

  • Hands-on experience with Kalman filters, nonlinear estimation or probabilistic filtering. 

  • A proven track record of designing, tuning and validating controllers for highly dynamic systems. 

  • Strong implementation skills in Rust, C++ or another systems programming language. 

  • A strong understanding of real-time execution, numerical stability, sensor timing and latency. 

  • Hands-on experience with simulation, system identification, flight-log analysis and flight testing. 

  • The drive to challenge existing performance limits, test ideas quickly and keep iterating until the data proves the improvement. 

Note: We operate in an industry where women, as well as other minority groups, are systematically under-represented. We encourage you to apply even if you dont meet all the listed qualifications; ability and impact cannot be summarised in a few bullet points.

From then on, planners and shift leads juggle dependencies by hand. That is expensive, rarely optimal, and wastes much of what these factories were built for.

We are building the layer that takes over when the plan gets disrupted. It connects to factory data, models production, detects disruptions and bottlenecks as they emerge, simulates responses and recommends the best one.

We have the runway to build deliberately and the experience of people who have built and scaled successful companies before. On the technical side, we combine deep algorithmic and software-engineering competence with modern optimization methods, GenAI-assisted development and fast, pragmatic iteration. We are in stealth and very early, which means you can shape much of what comes next.

What you'll own

  • The product layer: Turn complex optimization systems into software planners can actually use.

You set your own priorities and structure your work toward clear goals. No ticket queue, no micromanagement.

How we build

Our product sits at the boundary between algorithms, software systems, and real industrial operations.

We care about building systems that are easy to integrate, responsive, understandable, and maintainable as both the product and the underlying algorithms evolve.

We use GenAI extensively to prototype, implement, and explore alternatives. But generating code is not the hard part. The value lies in designing the right system, choosing good abstractions, validating behavior, and knowing what is worth building.

title: Founding Optimization Engineer
description:
Founding Optimization Engineer

Build the algorithmic core of planqor.ai: the real-time decision layer that steers discrete manufacturing when production plans get disrupted. Born on the shop floor, co-founded by senior production experts, and with direct access to high-impact industry problems. Work directly with our CTO and shape the optimization architecture on a greenfield: custom algorithms, heuristics, OR and simulation, fast C++ with Python on top. Backed by investors who have built and scaled successful companies. Remote-first or from our office in Munich, competitive pay + VSOP, no puzzle interviews.

The opportunity

Factories have invested billions in automation, yet production is still steered largely by people. Every night, a plan is computed for the next day, and the first disruption makes it obsolete. From then on, planners and shift leads juggle dependencies by hand. That is expensive, rarely optimal, and wastes much of what these factories were built for.

We are building the layer that takes over when the plan gets disrupted. It connects to factory data, models production, detects disruptions and bottlenecks as they emerge, simulates responses and recommends the best one.

About us

planqor.ai was born on the shop floor. Our founding team brings deep production expertise, strong industry networks. We have the runway to build deliberately and the experience of people who have built and scaled successful companies before. On the technical side, we combine deep algorithmic and software-engineering competence with modern optimization methods, GenAI-assisted development and fast, pragmatic iteration. We are in stealth and very early, which means you can shape much of what comes next.

What you'll own

  • The algorithmic core: Design how planqor.ai represents, propagates and optimizes schedules, resources and constraints, and how it repairs them when disruptions hit.

  • Performance: Make it fast. Profile and optimize the C++ core and expose it cleanly.

  • Evidence: Build the benchmarks, instances and experiments that show what actually works and where it fails.

  • The path to production: Work with our systems engineer to turn algorithms into decisions planners trust.

  • The team: Grow into leading optimization at planqor.ai as we scale: hiring, mentoring, setting direction.

You set your own priorities and structure your work toward clear goals. No ticket queue, no micromanagement.

How we build

Our goal is not to build the most impressive optimization algorithm on paper. It is to build decision systems that remain useful when the real world changes. A strong solution that can be updated, repaired and explained quickly beats closing the last optimality gap on a static model.

So we are neither a solver wrapper nor a research lab. We use whatever works (MIP, CP, heuristics, local search, simulation, learning or something purpose-built) and let the evidence decide.

Generative AI makes this loop dramatically faster. We use it to implement ideas, explore alternatives and evolve algorithms against our benchmarks. But speed only counts if the methodology holds: representative data, adversarial tests, meaningful metrics, rigorous validation.

There are no points for cleverness. The simplest system that reliably solves the real problem wins.

What you'll bring

  • Strong modern C++ and performance engineering. You are comfortable building performance-critical algorithms, profiling them, choosing appropriate data structures, and reasoning about runtime, memory, and scalability.

  • Real experience solving optimization problems. This may come from Operations Research, combinatorial optimization, scheduling, MIP/CP, heuristics, local search, simulation, optimization under uncertainty, or related fields. You do not need to be an expert in all of them. Big plus for Sequential Decision Analytics.

  • Systems thinking. You think beyond individual models and algorithms: how state is represented, how changes propagate, how components interact, and how the complete decision system behaves under real-world disruptions.

  • Python for experimentation and data analysis. You can build benchmark pipelines, analyze data, visualize results, and quickly investigate why an approach succeeds or fails.

  • Empirical engineering judgment. You design experiments, challenge assumptions, measure performance, and abandon approaches when the evidence says they are wrong.

  • Independence. You can turn an underspecified operational problem into working software without waiting for a detailed spec.

  • Fluent English. German and experience in manufacturing or industrial planning are useful but not required.

What you'll get

  • Ownership: shape the optimization architecture from line one, working directly with our CTO.

description:

Unsere Mission für dich

trawa baut Europas führende B2B-Plattform für saubere Energie auf. Unsere Mission ist es, Industrieunternehmen mit nachhaltigen Energielösungen zu versorgen. Mit unserem integrierten Ansatz aus Energieversorgung, moderner Energiemanagementsoftware und intelligenter Optimierung des Energieverbrauchs helfen wir Unternehmen dabei, wettbewerbsfähig zu bleiben und den Weg in eine klimafreundliche Energiezukunft zu ebnen.

Du sorgst für eine reibungslose Betreuung, koordinierst wichtige Prozesse und trägst dazu bei, dass unsere Kund:innen langfristig erfolgreich mit trawa arbeiten.


Das Team

Deine Aufgaben

Dabei stellst du sicher, dass alle benötigten Informationen vorliegen und die richtigen Ansprechpartner:innen eingebunden sind.

  • Teamübergreifend arbeiten: Gemeinsam mit unseren Kolleg:innen aus Product und Sales gestaltest du eine Customer Experience, die unsere Kund:innen begeistert.

  • Kundenanfragen bearbeiten: Du bearbeitest und priorisierst eingehende Kundenanfragen, löst Probleme zeitnah und eigenständig oder leitest sie strukturiert an die zuständige Customer Success Managerin weiter.

Nach wem wir suchen

Dein Hintergrund

  • Du hast ein Studium in einem relevanten Fachbereich oder eine vergleichbare Ausbildung mit guten Leistungen abgeschlossen.

  • Erste Erfahrungen in der Betreuung von B2B-Kund:innen, in analytischen Tätigkeiten oder in koordinativen Rollen sind von Vorteil.

Deine Fähigkeiten

  • Du bist ein Organisationstalent, arbeitest strukturiert, behältst den Überblick und kannst Aufgaben effizient priorisieren.

  • Du verfügst über exzellente kommunikative Fähigkeiten und gehst professionell sowie serviceorientiert auf Kund:innen zu – schriftlich und mündlich.

  • Du denkst analytisch, fühlst dich im Umgang mit Zahlen wohl und kannst datenbasierte Erkenntnisse sicher und verständlich kommunizieren.

Dein technisches Verständnis

  • Du bist technologieaffin. CRM-Systeme und digitale Tools sind für dich keine Hürde, sondern eine spannende Herausforderung.

  • Erste Erfahrungen in der Energiebranche sind ein Plus. Idealerweise interessierst du dich für erneuerbare Energien und möchtest dich in diesem Bereich weiterentwickeln.

Deine Sprachkenntnisse

  • Du sprichst Deutsch auf muttersprachlichem Niveau.

  • Du verfügst über fließende Englischkenntnisse.

  • Du lernst trawas Produkte, Prozesse und den Energiemarkt kennen.

  • Du verstehst, wie Kundenbeziehungen bei trawa funktionieren – vom Onboarding bis zum QBR.

Monat 2: Erste Verantwortung übernehmen

Monat 3 und danach: Eigenständige Kundenbetreuung

  • Du erkennst Upselling- und Cross-Selling-Potenziale.

  • Du bringst eigene Ideen ein, wie wir unsere Kund:innen noch besser betreuen und ihre Erfahrungen mit trawa weiter verbessern können.

Warum wir?

Gestalte mit uns die Zukunft der Energiewirtschaft und treibe eigenverantwortlich Projekte voran, die echten Einfluss auf unsere Produkte, unsere Kund:innen und die Umwelt haben.

  • Dein Impact: Du übernimmst Verantwortung in unserem dynamischen Team und gestaltest aktiv innovative Produkte und Kundenerlebnisse, die die Energiewende vorantreiben und zur Dekarbonisierung des Mittelstands beitragen. Dein Beitrag hat direkten Einfluss, und du kannst stolz auf deine Ergebnisse sein.

  • Flexibles Arbeiten: In unserem schönen Büro fördern wir eine lebendige Unternehmenskultur, in der wir gerne gemeinsam arbeiten. Homeoffice ist ebenfalls möglich. Mit flexiblen Arbeitszeiten, 30 Urlaubstagen und bis zu zehn Workation-Tagen unterstützen wir deine Work-Life-Balance.

  • Attraktive Benefits: Neben einem wettbewerbsfähigen Gehalt erhältst du Essensgutscheine, eine Urban-Sports-Mitgliedschaft, reichlich kostenlose Snacks und ein persönliches Weiterbildungsbudget.

  • Persönliche Entwicklung: Du wirst Teil eines tollen Teams, in dem Coaching und Mentoring großgeschrieben werden. Außerdem arbeitest du mit modernen Technologien und lernst von erfahrenen Expert:innen aus der Branche.

  • Vielfalt und Inklusion: Bei uns sind alle willkommen. Wir setzen uns für einen inklusiven Arbeitsplatz ein, der Vielfalt wertschätzt, und ermutigen Menschen unabhängig von Geschlecht, Alter, sexueller Orientierung, ethnischer und sozialer Herkunft sowie körperlicher oder neurodiverser Vielfalt zur Bewerbung.

Wenn du strategisch denkst, operativ stark bist und gerne Verantwortung übernimmst, dann bewirb dich jetzt! Auch wenn du nicht alle Anforderungen zu 100 % erfüllst: Wir sind offen für Persönlichkeiten mit Potenzial und Leidenschaft.

Über uns

Willkommen im trawa-Universum! Wir haben es uns zur Aufgabe gemacht, das grüne Versorgungsunternehmen der Zukunft von Grund auf aufzubauen. Wie machen wir das? Wir schaffen einen direkten Zugang zu erneuerbarer Energie für B2B-Industrieunternehmen. Wir entwickeln Software und Technologie, um die Volatilität des Energiemarktes zu bewältigen. Wir professionalisieren die Energiebeschaffung auf der Käuferseite.

title: Optical Engineer (m/f/d)
description:
Focused Energy is a fusion energy startup with the goal of generating unlimited clean energy to responsibly meet future global demand. With the use and commercialization of laser-induced inertial fusion, a clean and highly efficient power generation technology is coming within reach, suitable to ensure a secure and scalable future energy supply.

We are seeking a skilled and driven Optical Engineer to design, analyze, and help realize the next generation of high-energy and high-average-power laser systems that underpin Focused Energy’s fusion program. In this role, you will be responsible for turning advanced optical concepts into robust, manufacturable, and operable experimental and production laser systems.

Your work will directly enable the performance, stability, and scalability of our fusion laser infrastructure — ensuring that optical designs meet extreme power, precision, and reliability requirements while remaining practical to build, integrate, and operate.

What you’ll do

  • Optical System Design: Design, model, and optimize complex optical systems for high-energy and high-average-power laser applications, balancing performance, robustness, and manufacturability.

  • Simulation & Analysis: Use advanced optical modeling tools (e.g., Zemax / OpticStudio) to perform ray tracing, tolerance analysis, stray light analysis, and wavefront propagation to predict and validate system behavior.

  • Performance Specification: Define detailed optical specifications including component selection, materials, coatings, and tolerances to meet demanding power, fluence, and stability requirements.

  • Integration & Commissioning: Partner closely with technicians, laser engineers, and mechanical and electrical teams during assembly, alignment, testing, and commissioning of optical systems, troubleshooting issues as they arise.

  • System Optimization: Identify and resolve performance limitations related to aberrations, thermal effects, alignment sensitivity, and stray light to ensure stable, repeatable operation at high power.

  • Documentation & Communication: Produce high-quality technical documentation, analyses, and design reviews to support internal development, knowledge sharing, and external collaboration.

  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Work across disciplines to ensure optical designs integrate cleanly into larger laser, mechanical, electrical, vacuum, and control system architectures.

Who you are

  • A degree in Optical Engineering, Physics, Electrical Engineering, or a related field, with professional experience designing and analyzing optical systems for laser or photonics applications.

  • Deep hands-on experience with Zemax (OpticStudio) or comparable optical design and simulation tools, including tolerance and stray light analysis.

  • Strong understanding of classical optics, Gaussian beam propagation, laser physics, and material behavior under high-intensity or high-fluence conditions.

  • Comfortable moving between modeling and the lab — supporting alignment, testing, debugging, and iteration of real optical hardware.

  • You bring rigor to your designs, anticipate failure modes, and care deeply about accuracy, documentation, and long-term reliability.

  • You can work effectively with scientists, engineers, and technicians and communicate complex optical concepts clearly across disciplines.

  • Preferred: Experience with MATLAB, Python, or similar tools for analysis, modeling, or automation of design workflows.

  • Preferred: Familiarity with cleanroom practices, vacuum-compatible optical design, large-aperture optics, or advanced components such as adaptive or deformable optics.

Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender perception or identity, national origin, age, marital status, protected veteran status, or disability status.

Pursuant to the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, Focused Energy will consider for employment qualified applicants with arrest and conviction records.

Compensation offered will be determined by factors such as location, level, job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. Certain roles may be eligible for incentive compensation, equity, benefits.

title: Meridial – Senior Research Software Engineer – Image Processing
description:
About Meridial

Meridial is a Focused Research Organisation (FRO) with a mission to bring connectomics into the living brain. We are building a platform for longitudinal, synapse-resolution mapping of functional neural circuitry in preclinical models. Our aim is to deploy this platform for translational projects and improve drug development outcomes for disorders of the central nervous system.

Meridial is a new not-for-profit FRO in the Convergent Research Ecosystem and funded by the Advanced Research and Invention Agency (ARIA).

The technical challenge

Our imaging platform records the activity of neurons and synapses in the living brain. The scientific value of these recordings depends on converting raw images into reliable, quantitative data.

This is a demanding image processing problem. Fluorescence signals are faint, noisy and spatially overlapping; residual tissue motion and other imaging artefacts must be corrected; in addition to conventional planar frames, data may be acquired from arbitrarily shaped 3D regions or several depths at once; properties vary between signal types and experimental configurations; and the same cells and synapses must be reliably matched across imaging sessions spanning weeks. You will build a software package that addresses these challenges in two modes: real-time processing and visualisation, with latencies of tens to hundreds of milliseconds, that inform experimental decisions at the microscope, and offline pipelines that deliver maximum accuracy for scientific analysis and serve as the benchmark for the real-time methods.

The impact of this work is direct and visible: your software will be used at the microscope as experiments unfold, and your pipelines will generate the data underpinning new insights into how neural circuits function and how they change in disease.


Key responsibilities

You will own Meridial’s image processing software end to end, starting from the interface with microscope control and acquisition all the way to processed results prepared for biological analysis. This is a role with a high degree of autonomy: you will make the main design and technology decisions, set priorities with the people who use the software, and work out what to build as requirements emerge.

Who you will work with

  • Experimental team. The neuroscientists running experiments are the main users of the real-time tools. You will work with them at the microscope, understand their problems and turn joint solutions into reliable tools.
  • Senior Software Engineer. Develops the microscope control and image acquisition software, mostly in Rust. Your real-time code exchanges data with that software but need not be part of it. Together, you will decide how the two systems connect.
  • Neuroscience Data Scientist. Owns Meridial’s database and the downstream scientific analysis. You will ensure processed results reach the database with a full record of how they were produced.
  • Reporting line. You will join the Computational Team and report to its Head once appointed, and to the Director of Experimental Research until then.

    • What you will do

  • Build robust pipelines for motion and artefact correction, segmentation of cells and synapses, separation of overlapping signals and extraction of activity over time, adapted to different signal types.
  • Register data from flexible 3D imaging modes to reference volumes, and build tools that find the same field of view and match cells and synapses across sessions, both live at the microscope and offline at high resolution.
  • Develop real-time versions of these methods that keep up with streaming data, including fast identification of cells as stimulation targets.
  • Build live visualisations and summary measures, such as rolling averages, response histograms and noise metrics, that help scientists steer experiments.
  • Define, with the Senior Software Engineer, the interface between acquisition and processing, with a focus on throughput and low latency.
  • Evaluate and adapt existing open-source tools, develop new methods where needed, and validate them against ground truth, using offline results as the benchmark for the real-time processing.
  • Optimise for speed and scale, using multi-threading, GPUs or compiled languages where needed, so that processing keeps up with large and growing datasets.
  • Write clean, tested and documented code, and set up version control, continuous integration and documentation practices for the codebase.
  • Use AI coding assistants to work efficiently, while keeping code correct and maintainable.
  • Plan and track work in Jira or another project management system, in short iterations with the experimental team.
  • Turn prototypes into reproducible tools that scientists can use and that can be released as open source.

    • The person we are looking for

    You are an experienced software engineer with a background in image analysis or computer vision. You enjoy hard technical problems and set high standards for correctness, performance and code quality. You like working directly with the people who use your software: understanding their problems, trying out ideas with them and turning the best into reliable tools.

    You enjoy building from scratch and are comfortable with the ambiguity of an early-stage organisation. As the main developer of our image processing software, you will work independently and shape how it evolves.

    Experience in any of these areas would help you hit the ground running, but none is required: real-time or streaming data processing, microscopy or scientific image analysis, statistics, or machine learning for image analysis. A background in biology, biophysics or neuroscience would also help.


    Essential experience
  • Experience with image analysis or computer vision, such as segmentation, motion correction, registration or denoising, including image quality measures like signal-to-noise ratio.
  • 5+ years of software development experience, in industry or research (for example, PhD or postdoctoral work where software was a main output).
  • Strong proficiency in Python, with good engineering practice: Git, automated testing and well-documented code.
  • Experience with performance optimisation, such as multi-threading or GPU programming, and with a compiled language such as C/C++ or Rust (if not Rust, a willingness to learn it).
  • Experience building interactive, high-performance data visualisations.
  • Experience building data-intensive pipelines for large datasets, from requirements through to deployment.
  • Experience working directly with end users who are not developers, gathering requirements and turning feedback into improvements.
  • Hands-on experience using AI coding assistants in your day-to-day development.

  • Ability to move light-to-moderately heavy items (typical lab supplies/equipment); may include occasional lifting/carrying with appropriate equipment (e.g., carts/dollies)

Payward - the parent company behind Kraken, NinjaTrader, Breakout, xStocks, Payward Services and CF Benchmarks - has spent the last 15 years building one of the most modern and globally accessible financial infrastructure platforms in the industry, built to advance an open, global financial system.

Founded in 2011, Kraken is one of the world's longest-standing crypto platforms, trusted by over 10 million individuals and institutions across the globe. It offers spot trading, margin, futures, staking, and OTC services, with products built for both individual investors and institutional clients.

 

The opportunity

As a Sr. MarTech Specialist for Attribution and Performance, you will support attribution and performance measurement at Payward by owning the data and processes that keep it accurate, and by acting as the bridge between our engineers and our performance marketing team. You will form part of a wider MarTech team and partner closely with finance and compliance so that measurement stays accurate and follows our safety and compliance practices. You will also use AI as a core part of how you work, moving quickly and sharing what you learn with the team. Key responsibilities include:

  • Attribution:

    • Drive attribution across web and app, covering conversion definitions, touchpoint credit and journeys stitched together across 3rd party vendors and our inhouse data platforms.

    • Investigate discrepancies caused by vendor configuration, attribution methodology, fraud or bugs in our own apps.

    • Contribute to the roadmap for the next level of attribution, such as incrementality testing, LTV-based optimisation and marketing mix modelling.

    Engineering partnership:

    • Turn performance marketing needs into clear specs and tickets for engineering, covering event design, deep links, SDK changes and server-side tracking, and review what ships.

    • Work with engineers and data owners to keep the signals ad platforms optimise on (Meta, Google and TikTok conversion APIs and postbacks) complete, deduplicated and consent-compliant.

    • Audit and standardise event naming, properties and volume, with monitoring in place to catch breakages early.

    Performance and cross-functional support:

    • Run a regular rhythm with performance marketing on attribution health, discrepancies and test readouts.

    • Put a measurement plan in place before spend goes live on new channels, launches and tests, and own the readout afterwards.

    • Support weekly and monthly reporting cycles, maintain the attribution dashboards the performance team relies on, and support spend and invoice reconciliation with finance.

    • Work directly with MMP and ad platform reps and vendor support, escalating with evidence.

    • Work with compliance to keep tracking, conversion signals and reporting aligned with Payward's safety and compliance practices, including consent, privacy (GDPR, CCPA) and financial promotion rules.

    • Set up monitoring and alerts for tracking breakages, fraud and volatility-driven spikes in traffic and conversions, such as sharp market moves, and escalate per policy.

    • Participate in cross-functional discussions with product, compliance, finance, design, data and performance marketing, and prioritise requests openly.

 

What you bring

  • 5+ years of experience in MarTech, performance marketing technology, growth analytics or a related digital marketing field.

  • Comfortable working with data: SQL and a data warehouse, able to read an event schema and trace a discrepancy back to its source.

  • Experience working within safety and compliance practices in a regulated environment, such as consent and financial promotion rules, and monitoring data and alerts through volatile periods when traffic and conversions swing quickly.

  • Strong stakeholder management and written communication skills, with experience aligning performance marketers, engineers, data, finance and compliance around a number they might not align on.

  • Able to write a clear spec, work with engineers to deliver it and review the result.

  • Detail-oriented and process-driven, able to manage multiple workstreams and prioritise the problems that move spend decisions.

  • Genuine interest in the crypto or fintech industry.

 

Nice to haves

  • Exposure to incrementality testing or marketing mix modelling.

  • Experience building AI-assisted workflows or lightweight automations, for example with LLM APIs, scripts or agents, for reporting, QA or monitoring.

title: Applied AI - Member of Technical Staff
description:
About Us

We’re living through a Cambrian explosion of intelligence: new models and new chips, each specialised for different tasks, are arriving all at once. The result is a new era for AI, one of radical heterogeneity.

Callosum is the Intelligent Systems Company. We believe the next generation of AI won't be defined by any single model or chip, but by intelligent systems in which hardware and intelligence co-evolve. We are building the infrastructure that unifies heterogeneous compute across the full stack. This opens a new axis of scaling intelligence: a dynamic system that tailors itself to what each workload actually needs, whether that's speed, cost, precision, or whatever unit comes next.

The last era scaled on a different bet: one bigger model, more of the same chip, more data. That bet is running into structural limits. Frontier models offer extraordinary capability at unsustainable cost, one that today's monolithic infrastructure was never designed to serve.

Our founding principle is that intelligence comes from many specialised systems working together, not from any single component. We build the software orchestration layer that co-evolves models, workflows and silicon into one system, delivering inference tailored to every workload, and demonstrating orders-of-magnitude leaps in capability and cost.

Because our software spans the full stack, our engineering team works directly with heterogeneous accelerators and frontier silicon, including Cerebras, d-Matrix, Intel, NVIDIA, AMD, Normal Computing, Tenstorrent, GreatSky, and Mixx. We are not stopping at today's chips: each new generation of silicon unlocks algorithms that couldn't run before, and we intend to be first to them, every time. If we get it right, it will belong to everyone building on it - not to any single vendor.

In our latest funding round, we raised $100M, led by Atomico with participation from Plural, DCVC and the UK Sovereign AI Fund’s first investment. With this, we are building the infrastructure for the next era of intelligence.

We are engineers and scientists based in London, working across the full depth of the stack. We are curious, intellectually honest, and building what doesn't exist yet. If you thrive on uncharted territory and are energised by the scale of the challenge, we'd love to hear from you.

About the Role

Applied AI Research at Callosum discovers the methods that make real AI workloads faster, cheaper and better, and turns them into systems that run in production. You will study how agentic workflows, retrieval pipelines and code intelligence stacks actually behave, then invent ways to optimise them at a systems level.

A single optimisation can touch agent and workflow design, context and prompting, model choice, the serving stack and the silicon underneath. So we don't hire specialists in one layer. We hire researchers who can reason across the whole system, from agentic design down to the specifics of the model, and who have a feel for how inference and hardware shape what is possible.

The role is research-led and engineering-heavy. You will need first-principles judgment to see what kind of system a problem needs, the rigour to prove that it works, and the engineering skill to build it yourself.

You will sit across our research and platform functions. What you discover becomes product capability, and what you see in real workloads sets the research agenda. We run a flat Member of Technical Staff structure. Responsibility and scope grow with what you demonstrate, including leadership of the Applied AI Research function as the team scales.

What You'll Work On

Our research tries to construct optimal inference systems from the silicon layer all the way up to the harness: the system will learn from the actual deployment profile and tasks it is used on and optimise itself. Open problems you will own include:

•⁠ ⁠Reverse-engineering agentic systems. Infer the structure of agentic systems from minimal data, and find where it spends compute it doesn't need to.

•⁠ ⁠Routing. Build robust routers that send each request to the cheapest or fastest path that strictly matches or beats the incumbent model on quality.

•⁠ ⁠Proving there is no regression. Design layered proxy evaluations, that bound quality ever more tightly, from coarse checks down to a granular understanding of the system.

•⁠ ⁠New optimisation surface area. Extend the same automatic, detection to new optimisation techniques, and help decide which ones we pursue next.

•⁠ ⁠Research that ships. Run rigorous experiments, write up what you learn, and work with our platform team to turn what works into general product capability.

•⁠ ⁠Shared research infrastructure. Build the evaluation harnesses, benchmarks and experiment tooling the team runs on.

title: Clinical Data & Quality Manager (CDD 18 mois)
description:
🏨 The Company

Resilience Care, a leading player in remote medical monitoring and a partner in clinical research, is a French company founded in 2021 with a single mission: to provide better care.

Our company offers remote monitoring solutions in oncology, gastroenterology, and psychiatry, based on the collection of ePROs combined with AI technologies. These solutions rely on a monitoring platform for healthcare professionals—enabling the early detection of side effects for continuous and proactive care—and a mobile app for patients, empowering them to measure and manage their symptoms using tailored resources.

Our solutions optimize patient care, continuously enrich our understanding of patients throughout their healthcare journey, and accelerate clinical research through the collection, structuring, and in-depth analysis of real-world data. Today, our solutions are deployed in routine care for 35,000 patients across more than 200 healthcare facilities, as well as within the framework of around twenty academic and industrial clinical trials.

Through this, we put data at the service of healthcare and therapeutic innovation, driven by the ambition to enable every patient to benefit from personalized medicine.

📝 Your Role

In a few words

Within QARA, you oversee Good Clinical Practice compliance across Resilience’s sponsored studies and studies conducted with pharmaceutical partners. You combine clinical quality, data integrity and system qualification, working closely with the teams running studies and building data workflows.

Your impact

You help keep studies inspection-ready, data reliable and traceable, and compliance embedded in everyday work. Your role is to safeguard the framework and help teams apply it, rather than produce the data yourself.

Your day-to-day work

  • Oversee study GCP compliance, manage deviations and corrective and preventive actions (CAPAs), and conduct quality and Trial Master File (TMF) reviews.

  • Maintain inspection readiness and support CRO oversight in line with ICH E6(R3).

  • Qualify systems, assess test environments and review data extractions, audit trails and Data Management Plans.

  • Work with Data and Clinical teams to build compliance into data workflows from the outset.

  • Maintain clinical quality procedures, train teams and monitor regulatory developments.

This is not a site-monitoring, data-engineering, study-project-management or routine clinical data-production role.

✨ Your Team

Here, we don’t work in silos. You’ll join an agile structure where compliance is truly a team sport:

  • Your Manager: Yasmine, the guardian of regulatory compliance for our medical devices. She will share her strategic vision of the healthcare sector with you and will be your go-to for the most sensitive decisions.

  • Your core team: A trio of passionate experts. They’re your daily contacts for everything related to the quality management system, technical files, and audit preparation.

  • The team’s little extra: A unique context where safety, clinical, and regulatory aspects come together to better serve patients, led by a team that combines rigor and kindness.

You join QARA and report directly to Yasmine. You work with Clinical Operations, Clinical Scientists, Data and Translational Research, as well as the DPO, CROs and pharmaceutical partners.

👤 Candidate Profile

⚙️ You are the right person if you know how to

  • Apply ICH E6(R3), Annex 11 and 21 CFR Part 11 to clinical studies and systems.

  • Manage deviations, CAPAs, audits and inspection preparation, beyond data cleaning alone.

  • Qualify systems using CSV/CSQ approaches and apply ALCOA+ principles.

  • Work with EDC systems and ePRO/eCOA solutions, translating their requirements into practical controls.

  • Communicate and write fluently in English.

🙂 You are the right person if you have

  • A rigorous approach that takes operational constraints into account.

  • Practical judgement to turn requirements into workable processes.

  • The ability to influence and train colleagues rather than impose rules.

  • Confidence working across clinical and technical teams and with external partners.

📃 You are the right person if you have already

  • Gained at least five years of relevant experience in Clinical Data Management and GCP compliance within a pharmaceutical company or CRO.

  • Handled clinical quality topics such as deviations, audits, inspections or procedures.

  • Contributed to computerised system qualification.

  • Worked with EDC systems, such as Medidata Rave, Veeva or Oracle, and ePRO/eCOA solutions.

It’s a plus if you

  • Understand pipelines, ETL and databases, without needing to be a developer.

  • Know CDISC standards for regulatory submissions.

  • Want to move from data production to compliance oversight and help build quality practices.

💛 Why join us?

  • Contribute to reliable studies and data that support clinical research in oncology.

  • Combine clinical quality, data integrity and collaboration with technical teams.

  • Work remotely from France and meet colleagues at internal company events.

  2. Interview with Yasmine, your future manager.

  3. Case study with Sarah and Yasmine from QARA.

  4. Team conversation with Nicoleta, Bertille and Alric.

  5. Strategic interview with Raph.

title: Projektmanager (m/w/d)
description:
Vujadé ist eine Online-Marketing-Beratung für den Mittelstand. Unsere Kunden tun im Marketing selten zu wenig, meist zu viel: zu viele Kanäle, zu viele Reports, zu viele Dienstleister. Wir messen,welche Maßnahmen tatsächlich Geschäft bringen, streichen den Rest und automatisieren, was sich wiederholt. Erst danach skalieren wir. Unser Leitsatz: weniger Geschäftigkeit, mehr Geschäft.

Am Ende eines Projekts haben unsere Kunden Steuerungs-Dashboards, klare Kennzahlen und Routinen, die dafür sorgen, dass das Richtige regelmäßig passiert. Dafür nutzen wir Daten, KI, Automatisierung und gesunden Menschenverstand.

Seit 2011 beraten wir Unternehmen mit 50 bis 5.000 Mitarbeitenden aus Industrie, Energie, Handel, Finanzdienstleistung, Medien und Bildung, darunter EDEKA, tesa, ENTEGA, Endress+Hauser und die Haspa.

Du verstärkst unser Kernteam. Für jedes Projekt holen wir genau die Spezialisten dazu, die es braucht, etwa Entwickler, SEOs, Designer, Texter, Strategen oder Data Scientists. Die meisten bringen viele Jahre Erfahrung mit, und von jedem nimmst du fachlich etwas mit.

Aufgaben

  • Projekte steuern: Du führst deine Projekte von der Planung bis zum Ergebnis – Timings, Budgets, Qualität. Wenn es hakt, merkst du es früh und handelst.
  • Kunden verantworten: Du bist erster Ansprechpartner, übersetzt Strategie in Maßnahmen und misst die Ergebnisse an den vereinbarten Zielen.
  • Analysen in Entscheidungen verwandeln: Du wertest Daten aus (Webanalytics, Search, Social Media und mehr), leitest Empfehlungen ab und vertrittst sie vor Kunden und Team.
  • Projektteams führen: Du steuerst ein Projektteam aus erfahrenen Spezialisten, briefst sie,nimmst Ergebnisse ab und diskutierst fachlich auf Augenhöhe.
  • Automatisieren: Mit n8n, Airtable und KI baust du Tools und Workflows, die wiederkehrende Arbeit ersetzen, bei uns und bei unseren Kunden.
  • Vertrieb mitgestalten: Du steuerst unsere Sales-Automatisierungen, sprichst Leads an und bereitest Pitches vor.

Qualifikation

  • Ein abgeschlossenes Studium (oft BWL, Wirtschaftsingenieurwesen, Informatik oder fachnah zur Branche) oder eine vergleichbare Qualifikation
  • Ein bis zwei Jahre Erfahrung im Projektmanagement, idealerweise in einem Umfeld mit klaren Prozessen und messbaren Zielen: Tech-Unternehmen, Start-up, Unternehmensberatung, Konzern oder eine datengetriebene SEO- oder Performance-Marketing-Agentur
  • Analytisches Denken: Komplexe Themen strukturierst du schnell, Prioritäten setzt du selbst
  • KI-Erfahrung jenseits des Chatfensters: Du hast schon mit APIs gearbeitet, weißt, wofür MCP-Server gut sind, hast verschiedene Prompting-Techniken ausprobiert und kennst aus eigenen Versuchen die Stellen, an denen Modelle unzuverlässig werden
  • Du verstehst, wie Online-Marketing-Kanäle zusammenspielen, und willst tiefer einsteigen
  • Deutsch und Englisch sprichst und schreibst du so sicher, dass du in beiden Sprachen Abstimmungen führst, Konzepte schreibst und präsentierst

Wie du arbeitest

Du sagst klar, was Sache ist, gegenüber Kunden, Spezialisten und Geschäftsführung. Mit gutenArgumenten widersprichst du, bei besseren änderst du deine Meinung. Fehler sprichst du an, deine eigenen zuerst. Direktes Feedback nimmst du als Abkürzung, nicht als Angriff. Du willst schneller lernen, als es dir die meisten Arbeitgeber erlauben. Eine glatte Vita interessiert uns weniger als das, was du in den letzten Jahren dazugelernt hast.

Wofür du bei uns falsch bist

Du willst vor allem kreativ arbeiten, Kampagnen entwickeln oder Markenwelten gestalten? Dann bist du in einer Agentur besser aufgehoben. Falsch bist du auch, wenn du Zahlen eher lästig findest, auf klare Ansagen wartest, bevor du loslegst, oder Konflikten mit Kunden lieber aus dem Weg gehst.

Benefits

  • Eigene Kunden nach kurzer Einarbeitung. Was du verantwortest, gehört dir
  • Zusammenarbeit mit Spezialisten, die zu den Besten ihres Fachs gehören und von denen du in jedem Projekt lernst
  • Aktuelle KI-Modelle, n8n und Airtable gehören zum Arbeitsalltag, intern wie im Kundenprojekt.
  • Neue Tools testest du direkt an echten Aufgaben, und was sich nicht bewährt, fliegt wieder raus
  • Kurze Entscheidungswege: Meist reicht ein Gespräch
  • Enge Zusammenarbeit mit der Geschäftsführung und direktes Feedback
  • Büro in einer alten Eppendorfer Brotfabrik und flexible Arbeitszeiten, abgestimmt auf Kundentermine und Team

Ein Anschreiben brauchen wir nicht. Schick uns deinen Lebenslauf, deinen möglichen Starttermin und eine kurze Antwort (maximal 200 Wörter) auf diese Frage: Welchen wiederkehrenden Arbeitsschritt hast du mit KI automatisiert oder vereinfacht, wie bist du vorgegangen, und was hat es gebracht?

If you want to work on meaningful problems, grow with the company, and be part of a flexible, hybrid work environment, spotixx offers the opportunity to do just that.

Tasks: what you will do

  • Own the infrastructure as code. Define and maintain every environment in code so they are reproducible and consistent.

  • Secure the delivery pipeline. Keep CI/CD trustworthy end to end - from keyless authentication to verified, attested deployments.

  • Run the cloud and network security controls. Manage edge protection, private networking, and segmentation across the platform.

  • Operate vulnerability management. Keep scanning and posture checks running, triaged, and turned into tracked, time-bound work.

  • Detect, monitor, and respond to threats. Run monitoring and alerting across the platform, investigate security and reliability incidents, and drive them to root-cause analysis and lasting fixes.

  • Support security testing. Enable penetration tests and configuration reviews, and act on what they find.

This is a DevSecOps role, not a DevOps role with a security title. You own the controls, not just the infrastructure:

  • Shift-left by default. Scanning, attestation, and policy run in the pipeline; an unsafe artifact fails the build, not a review.

  • Vulnerability management. Findings become tracked tickets with severity-based SLAs; you keep the queue moving and the control demonstrably operating.

⚠️ Google Cloud Platform is the one fixed requirement - this is a GCP-first role. Beyond that, we expect fluency with the standard DevSecOps toolchain: infrastructure as code, CI/CD, container and image security, cloud and edge protection, identity and secrets management, and posture and vulnerability scanning. We use well-established tools in each area, and equivalent experience transfers - we care more that you know the category than any specific product.

  • 4+ years in DevOps, SRE, platform, or cloud security, with real production ownership.

  • Proven experience running production services, including on-call, incident response, and backup and recovery.

  • Understanding of production change management, so that every change is reviewed, approved, traceable.

title: Customer Education
description:
About Peec AI

AI search is changing how brands are discovered and chosen. People now ask ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude and Google’s AI answers what they used to search for, and AI assistants increasingly shape the journey from discovery to purchase. Winning customers now means winning over the AI systems that influence their decisions.

Peec AI is an AI search platform that helps marketing teams understand and improve how their brands are discovered, represented, and recommended. We show them where they stand, what’s shaping it, and where to act. Since launching in January 2025, Peec AI has passed $20M ARR and 4,000+ paying customers. We’re a Series A company backed by 20VC and Singular, with 100+ people across our Berlin HQ and our New York office.

About the role

Peec ships something new almost every week. Most customers hear about it late, and some never do. We're hiring a Customer Education Manager to own how customers learn Peec. You'll own the product docs, the changelog, product updates and in-app communication, and turn every release into something a busy marketer understands in a minute.

You'll sit in product marketing and report to our founding product marketer. You'll work every day with product managers and engineers to understand what's shipping, with customer success to see where customers get stuck, and with the growth team to see what actually changes how people use the product.

What you'll do

  • Own the product docs. Rebuild them around the jobs customers come to do, not around the menu. Keep them current with every release, and make them easy to read for people and for the AI assistants our customers now ask first.

  • Run the changelog and product updates. Every release gets a clear entry the day it ships. You write the regular product update and the announcement for bigger launches, and decide what deserves which.

  • Write in-app communication. You write the copy for announcements, tooltips, empty states, onboarding steps and feature nudges. The growth team runs the nudges themselves (who sees what, when, and the tests); you make sure every message is clear, accurate and sounds like one product.

  • Make product content that teaches. Short how-to videos, walkthroughs, use-case guides and templates that get a new user from signup to their first useful insight, and an existing customer to the feature they're missing.

  • Get in early. Sit with product and engineering before launch, early enough to shape naming, setup and the first-run experience, not just document them afterwards.

  • Fix questions at the source. Read support tickets and customer calls, find the questions we keep answering, and make sure the product, docs or messaging answer them before anyone has to ask.

  • Measure what you ship. Track docs usage, support deflection and feature adoption after each update. Keep what works, cut what doesn't.

What we're looking for

  • You come from product. Product management, product ops, technical writing, solutions or support engineering, or customer success with a strong product bent. You learn software deeply by using it and can get a straight answer from a busy engineer.

  • You've owned docs, a help center or release communication for a B2B SaaS product. Show us a before and after.

  • You write simply. You can explain a complex feature in three sentences to someone who has never seen it, and cut a page in half without losing anything. We'll ask for recent work where your part is clear.

  • You like to ship a lot. Many small, useful pieces over one perfect one, and you care as much about keeping them up to date as about publishing them.

  • You're comfortable with data. Given adoption numbers, you can say whether a piece of content worked.

  • You use AI to draft, research and keep content in sync with the product. You build the systems that other teams can plug into to ensure consistency across every touchpoint.

  • You work well across product, engineering, customer success and marketing, make decisions and ship.

Bonus points

  • You built a docs or customer education function from scratch, first in seat.

  • You've worked in martech, SEO, analytics or a data platform, so you already know our customers' world.

  • You make short product videos and screen recordings yourself.

  • You've written in-app messages or product emails in tools like Customer.io, Intercom, Appcues or Pendo.

  • You know how to structure docs so AI assistants read and cite them correctly.

  • You write well in German or French as well as English.

Dein Profil

title: Design Engineer (w/m/d)
description:
Heartworking in Hannover. In Voll- oder Teilzeit. Hybrid.

Wir suchen jemanden, der/die Interfaces gestaltet und baut – und Verantwortung für das Produkt übernimmt, bis es im Browser genauso gut funktioniert wie in der Vorstellung. Tarifrechner, Kundenportale, Antragsflows, Konfiguratoren, Websites – Anwendungen, bei denen hunderttausende Menschen nicht merken sollen, wie komplex "das unter der Haube" ist. Die WordPress-Landingpage von der Stange gibt's woanders.

Aufgaben

So sieht dein Alltag aus

  • Du entwirfst und baust Interfaces – vom Konzept über den visuellen Entwurf bis in den funktionierenden Code. Du kannst ein Feature von der Idee bis in den Browser bringen, ohne es abgeben zu müssen. Das heißt nicht, dass du alles alleine machst – im Team arbeiten Entwickler:innen mit dir im selben Codebase. Aber du bist nicht abhängig davon, dass jemand anderes deinen Entwurf interpretiert.
  • Du arbeitest mit modernen Tools, die die Grenze zwischen Design und Code auflösen – Nordcraft, Cursor, v0 und was sonst in der Praxis taugt. Genauso selbstverständlich schreibst du eigenen Code, wenn das die bessere Lösung ist. Du evaluierst neue Ansätze mit Neugier, aber ohne Hype: nicht jedes Tool, das in der Community trendet, verdient deine Zeit.
  • Du baust und pflegst Design-Systeme dort, wo sie hingehören: im Code. Tokens, Komponenten, Varianten, Dokumentation – als lebendiges System, das direkt im Produkt funktioniert.
  • Du sitzt mit den Entwickler:innen zusammen – wirklich, nicht bildlich. Ihr arbeitet im selben Codebase, reviewed euch gegenseitig, diskutiert Architektur und Umsetzung auf Augenhöhe.
  • Du arbeitest in interdisziplinären Kundenteams (ca. 4–8 Personen aus Beratung, PM, Design und Development) – direkt am Kunden. Du bist nicht nur für deinen Teil zuständig, sondern denkst über den gesamten Produktkontext mit. Auch nach dem Go-Live.
  • Du denkst in messbarer Wirkung: Analytics, Heatmaps, Conversion-Daten – du nutzt sie, um deine Designentscheidungen zu validieren und das Produkt kontinuierlich besser zu machen.
  • Du machst andere besser: Design-Reviews, Code-Reviews, ehrliches Feedback, Wissenstransfer. Du bewegst dich zwischen Design- und Dev-Welt und bringst beide Seiten näher zusammen – durch gemeinsame Sprache, nicht nur durch Tools.
  • AI ist für dich Werkzeug im Alltag. Du nutzt Cursor für Code-Generierung, v0 für schnelle UI-Exploration, Claude oder ChatGPT für Prototyping und Konzeptvalidierung. Und du weißt, dass gute AI-Ergebnisse davon abhängen, wie präzise du den Kontext definierst: Design-System-Regeln, technische Constraints, Markensprache. Sauber denken, bevor du loslegst.

Qualifikation

Das bringst du mit

  • Mehrjährige Erfahrung an der Schnittstelle von Design und Frontend-Entwicklung. Du kommst entweder aus dem Design und hast dir Code beigebracht, oder aus der Entwicklung und hast ein starkes Gespür für Gestaltung entwickelt. Beides ist willkommen.
  • Du kannst Interfaces entwerfen UND bauen: HTML, CSS/SCSS, JavaScript/TypeScript. Du fühlst dich in Figma genauso wohl wie in VS Code oder Cursor.
  • Konzeptionelles Denken: Du verstehst, wie Informationsarchitekturen und User Flows funktionieren, und kannst diese in deinen Entwürfen und deinem Code gleichermaßen abbilden.
  • Du arbeitest sicher mit modernen Frontend-Technologien – React/Next.js bevorzugt, aber wenn du aus einem anderen Ökosystem kommst und schnell lernst: gerne. Erfahrung mit Nordcraft oder vergleichbaren visuellen Development-Plattformen ist ein Plus.
  • Design-Systeme lebst du im Code: Tokens, Komponenten, Varianten – aufbauen, dokumentieren, weiterentwickeln.
  • Visuelles Gespür: Typografie, Farbe, Spacing, Responsive Design, Animationen – du erkennst, wenn etwas nicht stimmt, und du kannst es selbst fixen. Accessibility (WCAG) gehört für dich zur Grundhaltung.
  • Kommunikation: Du kannst Designentscheidungen gegenüber dem Team und Kunden argumentieren. Und du sprichst die Sprache beider Seiten – du erklärst Entwickler:innen, warum ein Detail wichtig ist, und Designer:innen, warum eine technische Einschränkung kein Kompromiss sein muss.
  • Du hast echte Erfahrung mit AI-Tools im Arbeitsalltag – nicht als Experiment, sondern als festen Teil deines Workflows. Du weißt, wo sie echten Mehrwert bringen und wo du besser selbst baust. Und du verstehst, dass die Qualität der Ergebnisse von der Qualität deines Denkens abhängt – nicht vom Tool.
  • Du kannst dich in komplexe Fachlichkeiten einarbeiten und bleibst auch bei langfristigen Kundenbeziehungen neugierig, statt auf Autopilot zu schalten.
  • Deutsch auf C1-Niveau – unsere Kunden und Workshops sind deutschsprachig. Englisch im Code und in der Dokumentation ist selbstverständlich

Du entsprichst nicht zu 100% allen Anforderungen, aber die Chemie stimmt? Kein Problem! Richtig Bock auf Digitales ist uns wichtiger als ein shiny Lebenslauf.

Benefits

Darauf kannst du dich bei uns freuen

  • Gehalt: Wir zahlen marktgerecht und transparent – den konkreten Gehaltsrahmen besprechen wir offen im Erstgespräch. Kein Pokern, kein Rätselraten.
  • Gelebte Work-Life-Integration. Viele von uns haben Familie oder zeitintensive Hobbys. Wir sind überzeugt, dass nachhaltige Ausgeglichenheit uns viel weiter bringt als Mitarbeiter:innen mehr Zeit abzuverlangen.
  • Hybrides Arbeiten: 3 Tage remote, 2 Tage gemeinsam vor Ort am Hanomaghof. Nicht wegen Kontrolle, sondern weil wir glauben, dass echte Kreativität vom Austausch in einem Raum lebt – vom Miteinander zwischen Menschen, das kein Call ersetzen kann. Jeden zweiten Dienstag: Agentur-Standup und gemeinsames (veganes) Mittagessen mit Catering.
  • Das, was andere nur „flache Hierarchien" nennen – und wir tatsächlich meinen: Dein Team Lead hat immer eine offene Tür, du sprichst direkt mit Kunden statt über drei Ecken, und wenn du eine Idee hast, brauchst du kein Ticket dafür.
  • Fort- und Weiterbildung ohne Deckel: Konferenzen, Kurse, Bücher, Zertifizierungen – du suchst aus, wir zahlen.
  • Moderne Tools: GitHub, Linear, Slack, Figma. Und ja, wir setzen AI-Tools im Arbeitsalltag ein – kein Verbot, kein Hype, sondern pragmatischer Einsatz.
  • Mitdenken und Mitgestalten. Du hast von Anfang an die Möglichkeit, Verantwortung zu übernehmen und Dinge zu verändern.
  • Ob macOS oder Linux – du suchst dir deine Hard- und Software selbst aus. Auch für den privaten Gebrauch.
  • Mobilität: Deutschlandticket (geht auf uns) und Jobrad-Leasing.
  • Und sonst: Siebträger-Espresso, frisches Obst, Softdrinks, betriebliche Altersvorsorge, VWL, Sommerfest, Weihnachtsfeier, Teamevents und Agentur-Offsite.

Dein Weg zu uns

  • Bewirb dich mit deinem Lebenslauf und optional einem Portfolio, Case Studies oder Arbeitsproben. Kein Anschreiben nötig.
  • Unser erstes Kennenlerngespräch geht auch per Video – aber persönlich ist netter, und unser Kaffee ist wirklich sehr gut. ☕ Mit dabei: Du, jemand aus dem Design-Team und Jan-Christoph (Geschäftsführer).
  • It's a match? Beim Kennenlerntag lernst du das Team, die Projekte und den Hanomaghof kennen. Gemeinsames Mittagessen, offene Fragen, echtes Beschnuppern.
  • Ein „JA!" von allen Beteiligten? Dann schicken wir dir den Entwurf für deinen Arbeitsvertrag rüber und besprechen alle Details.
  • Ab Tag 1: persönliches Onboarding mit fachlicher Einarbeitung, Buddy-System und regelmäßigem Feedback durch die ersten Monate. 🥳

title: Warehouse Specialist
description:
WHO WE ARE

Proxima Fusion is Europe’s fastest-growing fusion company and the continent’s best-funded fusion player, as well as the first spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics (IPP). Backed by over €650M and powered by a growing team across Munich, Zurich, and Oxford, we are developing the hardware and infrastructure needed to deliver the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion power plant.

Our concept advances the most mature fusion technology out there, the Wendelstein 7-X stellarator, through two next-generation machines: Alpha and Stellaris. Our work combines stellarator optimization, advanced computation, machine learning, and high-temperature superconducting magnets to unlock higher-performance designs that were previously out of reach.

Turning these designs into a functioning fusion power plant requires excellence and ownership across every discipline, from physics and engineering to software, manufacturing, law, and business functions.

WHY JOIN PROXIMA FUSION

  • You will get to work on some of the most complex tech challenges to bring abundant, safe, clean energy to the world.

  • You'll get to join and learn from an exceptional selection of accomplished and driven individuals.

  • Do your life’s best work and enjoy the journey.

  • Get to show that big things are possible in Europe when you assemble the best talent.

YOUR IMPACT

At Proxima Fusion, we are building the future of clean energy - and we need an experienced Warehouse Specialist who thrives in a fast-paced, hands-on environment. In this role, you will ensure the smooth and efficient flow of materials and equipment, supporting our engineering, R&D, and operational ambitions. You’ll be responsible for managing incoming and outgoing goods, maintaining accurate inventory records, coordinating shipments, and ensuring the safe handling and storage of materials. With a strong focus on reliability, precision, and continuous improvement, you’ll play a key role in building efficient and scalable warehouse operations that support our mission to make fusion energy a reality.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

  • Goods receipt and inspection: Receive deliveries from suppliers, carriers and couriers. Check each one against the purchase order and delivery note for quantity, part number and condition. Look for transport damage, moisture, contamination or tampering. Verify labels, batch and serial numbers, and shelf life.

  • Non-conformance and claims: Photograph and document any findings. Move non-conforming goods to blocked or quarantine stock and raise non-conformance reports. File claims with carriers, inform Purchasing, and hand parts that need detailed inspection to Quality. Release or return them based on Quality’s decision.

  • System accuracy (ERP/WMS): Post goods receipts and goods issues accurately and on time, including labels, barcodes, and batch and serial numbers. Book goods in only after they pass the receipt checks. Keep physical stock and system stock in sync.

  • Dispatch and shipping documents: Pick, pack and prepare shipments according to packing instructions. Create delivery notes, labels, CMR consignment notes and packing lists. For non-EU shipments, prepare proforma invoices and export documents with the logistics team. Prepare ADR transport documents for hazardous goods.

  • Carrier coordination and returns: Book and coordinate pickups, and track shipments until they’re delivered. Handle returns and re-shipments to suppliers through the RMA process.

  • Loading, unloading and transport: Load and unload trucks and vans safely with forklifts and pallet jacks, and secure loads correctly. Handle heavy, bulky, sensitive or high-value components with care. Run scheduled milk runs between company sites and local suppliers using company vehicles.

  • Storage, replenishment and inventory: Sort, label and store goods in the correct locations. Replenish production and line-side stock (Kanban or min/max) in time for manufacturing. Take part in the annual stocktake and resolve stock differences. Manage packaging materials: stock levels, reordering, reuse and recycling.

  • Housekeeping and safety: Keep receiving, storage and dispatch areas clean and organised with a 5S mindset. Separate and dispose of waste according to German recycling rules. Follow health and safety rules and wear PPE. Report hazards, near-misses and accidents, and carry out daily checks on forklifts and handling equipment.

  • Cross-functional coordination: Work with Purchasing, Production, Quality, Engineering and Finance on material availability, priorities and urgent shipments, and keep internal customers informed.

  • Continuous improvement and travel: Suggest and support improvements to warehouse processes, layout and digital tools. Travel within the EU when needed, for example to suppliers, partner sites or with special shipments.

WHO YOU ARE

  • Completed vocational training as Fachkraft für Lagerlogistik, Fachlagerist/in or a comparable qualification, or equivalent hands-on experience.

  • At least 5 years of experience in goods receipt, dispatch or warehousing, ideally in a manufacturing environment.

  • Valid EU/German driving licence, class B.

  • Valid forklift licence (Staplerschein per DGUV Grundsatz 308-001) and confident operation of counterbalance forklifts.

  • Fluent German and English, spoken and written (at least B2 in both).

  • Tech-savvy: confident with ERP/WMS systems (e.g. SAP or similar), barcode scanners, Google Workspace, and email.

  • Good knowledge of shipping documents and processes (delivery notes, CMR, Incoterms basics).

  • Knowledge of load securing and safe handling of goods.

  • Willingness to travel within the EU when required.

INTERVIEW PROCESS

  • Recruiter Interview (30-60 min)

  • Technical Screening (30 min)

  • Technical Panel (3x60 min)

title: Hands-on Engineering Manager (C#/Vue)
description:
Location: 100% remote (EMEA + South America)

Classification: Full-time

Pay Range: €82,000–140,000; determined by several factors, including location

Miaplaza is looking for two Engineering Managers to lead two of our software development teams. We’re hiring for one existing team of 7 engineers and one new team that we will hire developers into.

This is a management role for someone who wants to grow as a manager while still remaining hands-on with code. You'll split your time roughly 50/50 between leading your team and doing hands-on work alongside them.

About Miaplaza

Miaplaza is dedicated to making education engaging and accessible through innovative online learning platforms. We develop personalized learning experiences for students, helping them grow in a supportive and interactive environment. Our vision is to elevate online learning by applying the most successful approaches in virtual education to create an accessible and inclusive education curriculum platform where all students can be successful!

As an engineering manager at Miaplaza, your team will build technology with a direct impact on the lives of hundreds of thousands of students. Every step of the way, you will have the opportunity to influence our direction. Through our platforms, we create engaging, safe, and thoughtfully designed learning experiences that help children grow academically, creatively, and personally. Every feature we ship, every system we scale, and every improvement we make contributes to shaping how the next generation learns and discovers their potential. If our platform is down, a child might not go to school that day. We’re looking for leaders who want their work to matter in classrooms and homes, who care about access to quality education, and who are excited to craft technology that makes a difference in young people’s lives. Here, your impact doesn’t just power a product; it shapes future generations!

What you’ll work on

We’re a C# and Vue.js platform growing towards a scale that no longer matches our legacy architecture. You’ll need to work with your team balancing both product and engineering initiatives. You’ll report to our head of engineering and be expected to split your time roughly 50/50 between people management and hands-on development. Prioritization always goes to leading and supporting your engineers.

How management works at Miaplaza

We're a US-based company, so this may differ from what you've done before:

  1. You start as an engineer. You’ll onboard as a senior engineer on your own team for two months, begin manager onboarding in month two, and take over the team at around week 10. Both phases matter equally, and this isn’t negotiable.

  2. You stay hands-on. Around 50% of your time stays hands-on after onboarding, but leading and supporting your engineers always comes first.

  3. You teach. Growing your engineers and those around you is a core responsibility. You'll have full oversight of your direct reports' work, because you can't teach well without seeing the process behind the output.

  4. Feedback is the norm. You'll give specific reinforcement and constructive feedback whenever you notice something, and you'll receive it too.


What you must bring

We can only move forward with candidates who meet these requirements:

  • 7+ years of experience in software development in one or more object-oriented programming languages

  • 3+ years of experience with front-end software development in a reactive front-end framework

  • 3+ years of experience with software architecture

  • 3+ years of experience operating at a Senior, Staff, or Principal Engineer level

  • 2+ years of experience being a mentor/leader

  • 1+ years leading a team, formally or as a tech lead

  • Experience working directly with product and design on scoping and prioritization

  • Experience being on-call and resolving production incidents

  • A bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience

What makes you stand out

  • Experience leading a team through a significant architectural migration

  • Experience with consumer platforms at scale

  • Experience building in regulated environments

  • Experience with DevOps technologies (eg K8s, IaC, sysadmin, build pipelines, etc.)

  • Extensive senior front-end development experience

Responsibilities

  • Work with your teams to design, develop, and maintain scalable and reliable web applications using primarily C# and Vue.js

  • Collaborate with your product trio (PM, UX, EM), product leadership team, and other EMs to scope, prioritize, and deliver features that matter to students and families

  • Set the quality bar for your team. You'll have dedicated capacity for reliability and architecture work rather than fitting it around feature delivery, and a strong say in where that capacity goes.

  • Manage, lead, and mentor your team while working side by side with them in code quality, clean architecture, soft skills, best practices, etc

  • Lead team trainings, set SMART goals, hold performance reviews, and provide individual feedback recurrently to each of your devs

Our hiring process

As a remote company, we receive a large number of applicants, so our process is longer than usual. At every stage we try to respect your time.

  1. Application and CV review. We review your application answers and CV, then follow up with an update.

  2. Initial technical screen (20 min). A few administrative questions and short technical questions related to the role.

  3. Behavioral interview (1 hour). With a member of our HR team, about your experience and approach so far.

  4. 1st technical interview (1 hour). With a member of the engineering team to answer technical questions tailored to our work.

  5. 2nd technical interview (1 hour). With a member of the engineering team to dive into a hypothetical scenario and how you’d tackle it.

  6. Leadership interview (1 hour). With our Head of Engineering or executive leadership.

  7. Reference check. We contact the 3 references you provide, including at least one former or current manager, a colleague, and a former or current direct report.

  8. Offer and background check. Once you sign your offer, we run a background check in accordance with applicable law.
