description:
At Gigaton, we’re on a mission to cut gigatonnes of carbon emissions from the world’s biggest emitting industries (like cement, steel and glass), by building autonomous AI control and optimisation systems that learn and leverage the physics of manufacturing. Our products run heavy industrial plants more efficiently, more stably, and with lower emissions in real time - laying the foundation for the next industrial revolution.

We are a team of scientists, engineers, builders, and operators who love hard problems, have high standards, and want to make change happen in the physical world. We care about deep tech, but we care even more about whether it delivers cost and carbon impact in a live plant, with real people, under real constraints.

With Gigaton, you’ll solve really tough problems in places few people ever get close to, and build something that actually helps the planet. Are you up for the challenge?

About the role

We are looking for a sales engineer to join our sales team and drive the frontline of industrial decarbonisation.

This role bridges the technical and commercial worlds. You'll need interpersonal and technical skills to build relationships with process engineers in cement plants and understand their challenges. Analytical skills will be essential to delve deep into complex plant data and work out how Gigaton's AI products can solve their most critical issues.

Building on that, you'll need strategic thinking and commercial awareness to turn your findings into concise, compelling proposals for decision-makers at our customers, from the C-suite down.

Ultimately, you'll build clarity from uncertainty, making sure we agree a shared roadmap with our customers that puts our solutions on track for significant real-world benefits before a contract is signed.

Over time, you’ll help us evolve our sales approach and shape the product by feeding insights and needs from the plant back to the product team, building the foundation for scaling across industries.

Your main responsibilities

  • Be the technical expert on sales calls and visits with cement plants.

  • Build trust with process engineers and plant teams by understanding their specific plant issues and linking them to how we can help.

  • Analyse plant data to identify and evaluate opportunities, then use this analysis to create compelling sales proposals.

  • Lead technical discovery and identify early when a plant does not meet our ICP (ideal customer profile) criteria.

  • Make sure relationships and plant understanding are handed over successfully to the deployment team.

  • Act as a feedback loop into Gigaton’s product and machine learning teams, providing field insights that help shape our product roadmap.

  • Develop and iterate the pre-sales technical process, making it more impactful and more automated each time.

  • Travel to plants and conferences, around one week per month, to understand customer environments and explain the product.

What a great fit looks like

  • Exposure to physical sciences, controls, or heavy industry, such as cement, steel, energy, manufacturing, or similar.

  • Strong analytical skills and an outcome-oriented mindset. You can dig into industrial data, identify root causes, generate potential solutions, and explain their value in dollars and tonnes of CO2.

  • Excellent communication skills. You can build credibility and trust in complex industrial environments with both engineers and board-level stakeholders.

  • Comfortable being the technical voice in the conversation, presenting to senior plant leaders and operators, handling objections, and being challenged on your findings by people who have run kilns for 30 years.

  • Naturally curious and keen to learn about the industry, the technology, and each individual plant. You want to understand the root cause behind every question and objection so you can solve the right problem.

  • Confident in ambiguity and able to field very specific technical questions without getting flustered. You know when you can give your understanding, when you need to go and find the answer, and how to maintain customer confidence in both situations.

  • Willingness to travel regularly.

You’ll excel if

  • You build trust easily. You can connect with plant engineers, listen deeply, and align solutions to their priorities.

  • You’d rather diagnose than pitch. Your first instinct in a plant is to ask a better question, not to open the deck.

  • You thrive in dynamic environments. Fast-paced, ambiguous settings excite you, and you’re motivated by high-impact, mission-driven work.

  • You have experience working in heavy industry, particularly cement, steel, energy, heavy manufacturing, or similar.

Success in This Role Means

  • Plants say yes because the technical case is clear. You build customer confidence that Gigaton can deliver high ROI, helping us hit our revenue goals without losing deals because customers don’t understand or believe in our product and capabilities.

  • Deployments are set up to succeed. We haven’t overpromised to sign a contract, and our pre-contract analysis holds up once the system is live.

  • Process engineers trust and rely on you as a partner in solving problems.

  • Deals don’t stall waiting on a technical answer. Objections get handled quickly, and customers get the answers they need in good time.

    💡 You are not expected to check every box, and we’d love to hear from you even if your experience isn’t an exact match.

    We’re building a team that reflects the world we want to change. Our people come from all walks of life, with different countries, cultures, and experiences, and we think that’s one of our biggest strengths.

    We’re committed to creating a workplace where everyone feels safe, respected, and celebrated. No matter your background, if you’re excited by what we do, we want to hear from you.

The interview process

  1. Talent Partner Screen Call: Meet our talent partner and learn more about Gigaton and the role.

  2. Hiring Manager Screen: Meet our VP of Sales and discuss if this role is a good fit for you.

  3. Technical Onsite (completed on the same day):

    1. Technical interview

    2. Data analysis & presentation

  4. Operating Principles Interview: Understand how we work and whether Gigaton and you are a good fit for each other.

  5. Meet with the CEO: Every new potential hire meets Josh.

We believe hiring is a two-way process. Just as we’ll reference-check candidates before making a final offer, we encourage you to reference-check us by chatting to team members you haven’t yet met. Ask anything. We’ll answer with Concrete Honesty.

Once interviews are done, we’ll move quickly to a decision, and we’re always happy to give feedback at any stage.

In return for your hard work, we’ll give you

📈 Equity in the company: When we win, you win. You’ll get share options, so you’re part of our journey from the inside.

🕰️ Flexible working We trust you to know how and when you work best and to work that out with your team.

🌴 30 days of holiday (plus bank holidays). Rest is productive. Take the time you need to recharge

🪙 A generous pension scheme. We’re planning for the future in more ways than one.

Our Operating Principles

↗️ Go Gig or Go Home: High Bar, All In. What we do matters to humanity, to our customers and to each other. We hold ourselves to an extraordinarily high bar and bring the urgency this mission requires.

🏭 Concrete Honesty: Be honest. As concrete forms the foundation of our world, genuine honesty and transparency are the bedrock of our culture.

🦾 Autonomous Ownership: High agency, high ownership. We build systems that take control and make things better. We do the same: see it, own it, drive it.

😄 Cement it with Kindness & Fun: Have fun, be kind. We're here to extend Earth's life, but ours is still limited. We want to enjoy the ride. To see these in full, go to Gigaton’s Operating Principles Notion page.

title: Functional Architect – AI-Driven Engineering
description:
Ready to be part of the Legal Tech revolution? 

Vision: 

As a global software-as-a-service (SaaS) provider, DiliTrust offers an integrated suite of legal and governance solutions. Our vision is to digitize legal departments worldwide. With an annual growth rate of over 40% since 2020, our ambition is to become the world’s leading Legal Tech company. 

Our Impact: 

From generating General Meeting reports to leveraging AI-assisted contract lifecycle management, our teams across 12 offices in France, the United States, Mexico, Dubai, Morocco, Germany, Spain, Italy and Canada are the driving force behind our global success. We proudly support 2,400 customers in 64 countries, with 80% of our clientele comprising listed companies in major markets such as Europe, North America and the Middle East. 

Our Recognition: 

DiliTrust has been at the forefront of Legal Tech innovation, being the first Legal Tech with AI features since 2022. The company is renowned for providing a positive and entrepreneurial work environment. We are honored to have received the “Happy at Work” and “Tech at Work” labels every year since 2019. 

The role 

DiliTrust’s R&D organization is undergoing a deep transformation toward AI-driven engineering across every role, from Product and QA to DevOps, Engineering and Architecture. In this context, business knowledge becomes a strategic asset: it must be explicit, structured and shared so that both our teams and our AI agents can consistently build the right product. 

Reporting to the Head of Architecture, you will be responsible for the functional coherence of the entire DiliTrust platform, covering all business modules and internal services. You will map our business domains, define functional design standards and ensure they are applied—including by building the AI agents that automate functional validation. 

This is a role with real authority and a progressive mandate. You will start as a trusted advisor to Product and Engineering teams, then progressively become the approval authority for functional design across the platform. Your ability to simplify complex systems and connect business knowledge with technical execution will be central to your impact. 

Missions: 

  • Map the platform’s business domains: Build and maintain a comprehensive model of capabilities, processes, business rules and data entities across all business modules and internal services, starting with priority areas and expanding progressively. 

  • Simplify and rationalize the functional landscape: Apply Domain-Driven Design to define bounded contexts, establish a ubiquitous language and map relationships between contexts. Identify overlaps, gaps and inconsistencies, and clarify shared concepts such as users, entities, documents, workflows, permissions and audit trails. 

  • Establish functional design governance: Define principles, standards and reusable patterns; review and approve functional designs and specifications against the global model. Build a clear decision-making framework through documented rules, decision records and review rituals. 

  • Make business knowledge usable by people and AI: Maintain a living, machine-readable source of truth comprising domain models, a business glossary and precise specifications. Support spec-driven development and embed this knowledge into the context, skills and tooling used by AI agents across R&D. 

  • Build AI-driven functional validation: Design, build and maintain your own AI agents to check specifications, user stories and designs against the domain model and design rules. Assess and improve the functional quality and reliability of AI outputs across coding, testing and review. 

  • Align functional and technical architecture: Work with technical architects on APIs, events and data models, ensuring that DDD bounded contexts translate into well-isolated domains within a hexagonal architecture, with business logic independent of infrastructure. 

  • Drive cross-functional alignment: Partner closely with Product Managers, Product Designers, Engineering Managers, QA and technical architects to resolve functional inconsistencies and ensure that product and engineering decisions remain coherent across the platform. 

  • Coach teams and champion functional practices: Act as a reference on functional topics, onboarding and coaching teams on the domain model, design standards and ways of working. 

Requirements 

  • Based in France with full working rights. 

  • Fluent in French and English. 

Experience & seniority: 

  • 10+ years of experience in software, including significant experience in system modeling and functional or solution design on complex B2B SaaS platforms. 

  • Proven experience mapping and rationalizing a complex, multi-product platform with a long history. 

  • Demonstrated ability to connect business needs, functional models and engineering decisions. 

  • Legal Tech experience is not required. 

Technical expertise: 

  • Strong command of strategic and tactical Domain-Driven Design: bounded contexts, ubiquitous language, context mapping, aggregates, entities, value objects and domain events. 

  • Proficiency in process and system modeling using approaches such as BPMN, UML, C4 and event storming. 

  • Ability to write precise specifications, business rules and acceptance criteria, including formats such as Gherkin. 

  • Solid understanding of hexagonal architecture, APIs, data models and event-driven architectures, enabling you to engage as a peer with technical architects. 

  • Daily use of LLM assistants and AI agents, with the ability to quickly master new tools. 

  • Hands-on ability to build and iterate on AI agents through prompting, context engineering, skills, MCP, scripting or low-code approaches as needed. 

  • Good understanding of how to evaluate and improve the functional accuracy and reliability of AI outputs. 

Leadership & collaboration: 

  • Strong systems thinking: you understand the whole, recognize interactions and design for coherence over time. 

  • A proven ability to simplify rather than add complexity, favoring clear concepts, clean boundaries and minimal models. 

  • Structured, concise thinking and the ability to make complex topics understandable to others. 

  • The ability to build trust and influence first, then hold a firm line on standards when needed. 

  • Excellent communication, teaching and coaching skills across business and technical teams. 

Education: 

Your background may be functional—business analysis, product or functional architecture—or technical, such as software engineering or architecture. What matters is your ability to model complex systems and bridge business and technology.

L’Institut Mines-Télécom fédère les grandes écoles françaises autour des défis industriels majeurs, numériques, énergétiques et écologiques. Ensemble, nous imaginons et construisons un avenir durable, en formant les acteurs qui façonneront les transitions de demain.

Bienvenue dans l’univers des matériaux du futur !

Au centre Science des Matériaux et des Structures (SMS), rattaché au Laboratoire Georges Friedel (unité mixte de recherche CNRS), on décortique la matière pour mieux la maîtriser. Alliages métalliques, céramiques, composites… ici, on explore le lien entre procédés, microstructures et propriétés des matériaux.

Grâce à des outils de caractérisation avancée et des modèles multi-échelles, nos enseignants-chercheurs inventent le concept de « Material by design » : concevoir les matériaux dès l’atelier de recherche, pour une performance sur-mesure.

🧠 Vous aimez la science fondamentale qui change le réel ? C’est ici que ça se passe.

🎯 Description du poste - ce que nous attendons de vous

Le Laboratoire Georges Friedel (LGF) est une Unité Mixte de Recherche du CNRS (UMR 5307). Situé à l’École des Mines de Saint-Étienne et porté par deux tutelles (Mines Saint-Étienne et CNRS), le laboratoire regroupe tout le potentiel de recherche de Mines Saint-Étienne dans les domaines des matériaux, de la mécanique et des procédés.

Le centre SMS - Sciences des Matériaux et des Structures - est l’un des cinq centres d’enseignement et de recherche de Mines Saint-Etienne. Au sein du LGF, il développe des recherches en science des matériaux, mécanique et procédés avancés de fabrication, pour le transport et la production d'énergie, avec un objectif d’accroître la durabilité des matériaux.

Ce post-doc s'inscrit dans le cadre de la chaire « SIRA », un partenariat de quatre ans entre Mines Saint-Etienne et les sociétés Framatome et EDF, co-financé par l'Agence Nationale de la Recherche, portant sur le vieillissement des aciers faiblement alliés (16MND5) utilisés dans les composants du circuit primaire des réacteurs nucléaires à eau pressurisée.

Ce post-doc est organisé selon quatre axes de travail.

Le premier axe de travail concernera l’utilisation de l’hydrogène pour favoriser la rupture intergranulaire, préalable indispensable à la spectrométrie Auger sur fracture. Ceci permettra d’accéder à des niveaux de ségrégation faibles, insuffisants pour provoquer une fragilité intergranulaire « intrinsèque ». L’hydrogène est connu pour exacerber, dans certains cas, la fragilité intergranulaire. Il s’agira ici d’explorer les conditions dans lesquelles on peut obtenir pour l’acier de cuve des ruptures intergranulaires assistées par l’hydrogène. On pourra notamment étudier l’effet de la concentration d’hydrogène (introduit par chargement cathodique par exemple) et de la vitesse de sollicitation mécanique. La chaire pourra bénéficier ici des compétences du laboratoire sur la fragilisation par l'hydrogène.

Le deuxième axe de travail porte sur le développement d'un modèle quantitatif pour l'analyse par Auger de la ségrégation intergranulaire des éléments d'alliages. Il s'agira d'une approche similaire à celle déjà développée pour le phosphore et le soufre, avec la difficulté supplémentaire de soustraire la contribution du volume, ici non-négligeable.

Les troisième et quatrième axes de ce post-doc s'appuient sur le spectromètre Auger installé en décembre 2025. Cet équipement de dernière génération présente une résolution latérale inférieure à 10 nm. Ceci ouvre de nouvelles perspectives d'analyses que nous souhaitons explorer dans le cadre de la chaire, en particulier concernant l'analyse du carbone et des carbures, qui constitue le troisième axe de travail de ce post-doc. L'analyse Auger de la surface des carbures nanométriques devient possible avec le nouvel instrument et permet d'accéder à la composition chimique des interfaces carbures-matrice. De plus, l'analyse Auger des facettes intergranulaires pourra être faite en-dehors des carbures et permettra d'accéder à la quantification du carbone ségrégé dans le joint.

Enfin, le dernier axe de travail consistera à développer une méthode de quantification de la ségrégation intergranulaire sans rupture. Il s’agira de travailler ici sur une coupe polie du matériau à étudier et à réaliser des analyses locales, par exemple des profils de concentrations à travers les joints de grains.

Compte tenu de l'excellente résolution latérale, on peut ainsi espérer détecter la ségrégation par cette méthode. Une méthode de traitement des données devra être développée pour accéder à des concentrations intergranulaires de solutés. Une telle méthode a déjà été mise au point pour des analyses réalisées par nanoSIMS et pourrait être transposée sur la spectrométrie Auger. Elle permettrait de s’affranchir de la nécessité d'obtenir une rupture intergranulaire (particulièrement limitante en spectrométrie Auger), tout en conservant une préparation d’échantillon très simple (coupe polie) et une productivité potentiellement importante (grand nombre de joints analysables dans un échantillon donné).

description:

Contexte :

École sous tutelle du Ministère de l’Économie, des Finances et de la Souveraineté industrielle, énergétique et numérique, et école de l’Institut Mines Télécom, IMT Nord Europe a 3 missions principales : former des ingénieurs responsables aptes à résoudre les grandes problématiques du XXIème siècle ; mener des recherches débouchant sur des innovations à haute valeur ajoutée ; soutenir le développement des territoires notamment en facilitant l’innovation et les créations d’entreprises. Son objectif est de former les ingénieurs de demain, maîtrisant à la fois les technologies numériques et les savoir-faire industriels. Idéalement située au carrefour de l’Europe, à 1 heure de Paris, 30 minutes de Bruxelles et 1H30 de Londres, IMT Nord Europe a l’ambition de devenir un acteur majeur des grandes transformations industrielles, numériques et environnementales du XXIème siècle en combinant, tant dans ses enseignements et que dans sa recherche, les sciences de l’ingénieur et les technologies du digital.

 

Localisée sur 2 sites principaux d’enseignement et de recherche, à Lille et à Douai, IMT Nord Europe s’appuie sur plus de 20000m² de laboratoire pour développer un enseignement de haut niveau et une recherche d’excellence dans les domaines suivants :

  • Systèmes Numériques

  • Energie Environnement

  • Matériaux et Procédés

 

Pour plus de détails, consulter le site internet de l’École : www.imt-nord-europe.fr.

 

Le stage est à pourvoir au sein du Centre d’Enseignement, de Recherche et d’Innovation Energie Environnement (CERI EE) de l’IMT Nord Europe. Une partie des missions du CERI EE (https://recherche.imt-nord-europe.fr/energie-environnement-ceri/) est de réaliser des travaux techniques et scientifiques pour le Ministère chargé de l’Environnement dans le cadre du Laboratoire Central de Surveillance de la Qualité de l’Air (LCSQA, https://www.lcsqa.org/fr) et de l’observatoire de Mesure et Évaluation en zone Rurale de la pollution Atmosphérique à longue distance (MERA, https://www.lcsqa.org/fr/le-dispositif-mera). En concertation avec les Associations Agréées de Surveillance de la Qualité de l'Air (AASQA), le CERI EE est chargé de proposer et qualifier les méthodes de mesure à déployer, de définir les protocoles, d’évaluer la qualité des données et de piloter l’observatoire MERA intégré au dispositif français de surveillance réglementaire de la qualité de l’air.

 

Contexte :

L'ammoniac (NH3) est un polluant atmosphérique nocif pour la santé humaine, les écosystèmes et l'environnement, mais aussi un précurseur de particules fines inorganiques notamment responsables de forts épisodes de pollution printaniers en Europe. En France, la source dominante d'ammoniac (environ 95%) est attribuée aux activités agricoles (épandage de fumier, utilisation d'engrais azotés, élevage). À partir de 2027, la directive européenne 2024/2881 exige que le NH3 soit mesuré spécifiquement sur les supersites implantés dans des lieux caractéristiques de la pollution de fond rurale. La France répond à cette obligation en déployant 6 supersites de surveillance de typologie fond rural, répartis dans des zones représentatives de la pollution longue-distance, et sélectionnés au sein des stations de l’observatoire MERA. Ces supersites sont équipés d’analyseurs automatiques en continu pour mesurer le NH3 à une très haute résolution temporelle. Ces méthodes permettent une mesure en temps réel, pour capturer la variabilité temporelle du NH3. Cependant, le NH3 est un polluant particulièrement complexe à mesurer notamment en raison de difficultés métrologiques (absence de méthode standardisée, interférences etc.) et de ses propriétés physico-chimiques (grande réactivité avec les surfaces, volatilisation, formation de particules etc.).

 

Objectif :

L'objectif de ce stage est d’apporter des éléments méthodologiques qui permettront d’établir des recommandations nationales concernant la sélection et les pratiques de mise en œuvre des préleveurs automatiques, afin d’améliorer la fiabilité et l’harmonisation des mesures de l’ammoniac.

 

Livrables :

·         Synthèse bibliographique ciblée sur les difficultés métrologiques de la mesure du NH₃ et les solutions à évaluer

·         Production d’un plan d’expériences détaillé à suivre durant le stage et d’un protocole d’assurance et de contrôle qualité des données.

·          Jeu de données documenté, fichiers ou scripts de traitement reproductibles et bilan des performances observées.

·         Présentation des résultats au groupe de travail national pour la mesure de NH3

·         Projet de note de recommandations pour le prélèvement de NH₃ en zone rurale, soumis à la validation des encadrants et du groupe de travail national. Les conclusions distingueront les points établis des points restant à confirmer.


Profil du candidat :

Ce stage est destiné à un.e étudiant.e en dernière année d’école d’ingénieur ou M2 universitaire avec un profil en analyses physico-chimiques, en instrumentation, mesure et assurance qualité appliquées à l’environnement, avec un goût prononcé pour les approches expérimentales.

De grandes qualités d’analyse, de rédaction, d’organisation, de communication et d’autonomie sont attendues.

Curiosité scientifique, rigueur et aptitude au travail en équipe sont recherchées. Un bon niveau d’anglais scientifique est souhaité pour la lecture bibliographique. Des compétences en traitement de données (Python, R ou Matlab) seront appréciées. Une première pratique de la chimie analytique et des notions de métrologie et d’assurance qualité seront des atouts.

title: Senior Site Reliability Engineer - Ceph / On-Prem Cloud Storage (m/f/d)
description:
Your Role

You will help us build, operate and industrialize the storage foundation of our on-premise cloud platform. As part of a small, experienced team, you will own the Ceph clusters behind our block, object and file storage services – essentially the storage every customer workload eventually lands on. The platform is still actively being built, which means you will have real influence on the storage architecture, hardware lifecycle, automation strategy and technical direction. The role goes beyond Ceph itself: you will regularly work across bare metal, networking, OpenStack, Kubernetes and GitOps. As a Senior Engineer, you take ownership of your area and help make storage predictable, durable and highly automated as we scale into the petabytes

Unser Tech Stack 🚀

· Ceph · OpenStack · Kubernetes · KVM · Linux · Bare Metal · Ansible · Terraform · Go · Cinder ·Neutron · Nova · RBD · Cilium
· RGW/ S3 · Prometheus/ Grafana · FluxCD / ArgoCD · Git· Python · Claude Code · Cursor · Agentic Coding Tooling

Your Responsibilities

  • Design, operate and evolve our Ceph clusters for block, object / S3 and file storage - from CRUSH topology and failure domains to pool design, placement groups, erasure coding, capacity headroom and performance.

  • Own the storage hardware lifecycle end to end – from qualification and burn-in through firmware, controller and disk health to OSD add/drain/replace, node retirement and hardware refresh. A key part of the job is automating these processes without creating tenant-visible impact.

  • Automate the provisioning of storage nodes on OpenStack-managed bare metal, working with Ironic, RAID and disk configuration, SEDs, provider networks and VLANs. You will also own the artefact path around images, package mirrors, certificates and other dependencies needed to bring up clusters in environments with tightly controlled external connectivity.

  • Run upgrades, rebalancing and reconfigurations as routine production operations, evolve our Infrastructure as Code and GitOps setup with Ansible, Terraform and FluxCD / ArgoCD, and make sure storage integrates cleanly with both OpenStack and Kubernetes.

  • Own capacity planning and growth forecasting, use telemetry to understand real consumption, and build out monitoring, testing and failure-injection around performance, durability and security.

  • AI-assisted engineering is simply part of how we work today. You use LLMs and agentic tools where they genuinely help – across development, testing, reviews, incident triage, knowledge retrieval or automation - and help us push further into self-healing and auto-remediation.

  • Act as a technical reference and sparring partner across Ceph, storage, automation and AI tooling, document technical decisions and share your knowledge with the team.

The role in one line

Customers trust us when things go wrong. We're the software reliability platform built to investigate, respond to and prevent incidents. As a Commercial CSM, you're the partner to our mid-market engineering teams - getting them onboarded, embedded and expanding their usage, and maturing their incident management and reliability as they grow.

What that looks like day to day

Our Customer Success organisation is at the heart of incident.io. We're the team closest to our customers' hardest problems, and we're trusted to solve them. We believe in a customer-led product approach, working hand in hand with Product to uncover and address what each customer really needs. Our goal goes beyond satisfaction: we want to delight customers at every stage of their journey, and build long-term relationships grounded in trust, shared success and mutual growth.

You'll look after 70–80 Commercial customers: growth-oriented tech companies, mostly under 1,000 people, between $30k and $150k ARR each. Industry leaders like Vanta, Monday.com and Loom sit in this segment. Some are steady, some are scaling fast, and much of the job is knowing which is which, and what each one needs from you.

Most of your time goes to mid-market customers on our top-tier plan, where you're their dedicated CSM leading onboarding and adoption. You'll blend 1:1 time with scalable programmes to get teams to value quickly: best-practice sessions, end-user training, partnership and roadmap reviews. You'll also cover a subset of smaller customers in a low-touch capacity, leaning on usage data to spot risk and opportunity early.

Day to day, this is a high ownership role. You'll help customers navigate the product, unpick problems when they hit them, and keep everyone pointed at the outcomes their team actually cares about. You are responsible for proactively identifying expansion and upsell opportunities, and partnering with Sales and Expansion Account Managers to grow revenue within your accounts. Internally, you're the voice of the Commercial customer with Product, Engineering, Sales, Marketing and Support.

There's still a lot to build and a ton of opportunity for you to shape this segment. The Commercial motion works, but scaling and automating the customer journey is live work we're ramping up now - refining playbooks, automating the repeatable stuff, building the tooling and content that makes a portfolio this size easier to serve. We're AI-forward in how we approach it, so you'd be shaping this rather than inheriting it.

Who you are

  • You've carried a book of 40 to 100+ accounts and worked out how to be present across all of them without going quiet on half.

  • You've sold to, or supported, technical people, whether that's engineering teams, on-call rotations or developer tools. You can hold your own in a technical conversation without needing to escalate every one of them.

Bienvenue dans l’univers des matériaux du futur !

Au centre Science des Matériaux et des Structures (SMS), rattaché au Laboratoire Georges Friedel (unité mixte de recherche CNRS), on décortique la matière pour mieux la maîtriser. Alliages métalliques, céramiques, composites… ici, on explore le lien entre procédés, microstructures et propriétés des matériaux.

Grâce à des outils de caractérisation avancée et des modèles multi-échelles, nos enseignants-chercheurs inventent le concept de « Material by design » : concevoir les matériaux dès l’atelier de recherche, pour une performance sur-mesure.

🧠 Vous aimez la science fondamentale qui change le réel ? C’est ici que ça se passe.

🎯 Description du poste - ce que nous attendons de vous

Le Laboratoire Georges Friedel (LGF) est une Unité Mixte de Recherche du CNRS (UMR 5307). Situé à l’École des Mines de Saint-Étienne et porté par deux tutelles (Mines Saint-Étienne et CNRS), le laboratoire regroupe tout le potentiel de recherche de Mines Saint-Étienne dans les domaines des matériaux, de la mécanique et des procédés.

Le centre SMS - Sciences des Matériaux et des Structures - est l’un des cinq centres d’enseignement et de recherche de Mines Saint-Etienne. Au sein du LGF, il développe des recherches en science des matériaux, mécanique et procédés avancés de fabrication, pour le transport et la production d'énergie, avec un objectif d’accroître la durabilité des matériaux.

Ce post-doc s'inscrit dans le cadre de la chaire « SIRA », un partenariat de quatre ans entre Mines Saint-Etienne et les sociétés Framatome et EDF, co-financé par l'Agence Nationale de la Recherche, portant sur le vieillissement des aciers faiblement alliés (16MND5) utilisés dans les composants du circuit primaire des réacteurs nucléaires à eau pressurisée.

Ce post-doc est organisé selon quatre axes de travail.

Le premier axe de travail concernera l’utilisation de l’hydrogène pour favoriser la rupture intergranulaire, préalable indispensable à la spectrométrie Auger sur fracture. Ceci permettra d’accéder à des niveaux de ségrégation faibles, insuffisants pour provoquer une fragilité intergranulaire « intrinsèque ». L’hydrogène est connu pour exacerber, dans certains cas, la fragilité intergranulaire. Il s’agira ici d’explorer les conditions dans lesquelles on peut obtenir pour l’acier de cuve des ruptures intergranulaires assistées par l’hydrogène. On pourra notamment étudier l’effet de la concentration d’hydrogène (introduit par chargement cathodique par exemple) et de la vitesse de sollicitation mécanique. La chaire pourra bénéficier ici des compétences du laboratoire sur la fragilisation par l'hydrogène.

Le deuxième axe de travail porte sur le développement d'un modèle quantitatif pour l'analyse par Auger de la ségrégation intergranulaire des éléments d'alliages. Il s'agira d'une approche similaire à celle déjà développée pour le phosphore et le soufre, avec la difficulté supplémentaire de soustraire la contribution du volume, ici non-négligeable.

Les troisième et quatrième axes de ce post-doc s'appuient sur le spectromètre Auger installé en décembre 2025. Cet équipement de dernière génération présente une résolution latérale inférieure à 10 nm. Ceci ouvre de nouvelles perspectives d'analyses que nous souhaitons explorer dans le cadre de la chaire, en particulier concernant l'analyse du carbone et des carbures, qui constitue le troisième axe de travail de ce post-doc. L'analyse Auger de la surface des carbures nanométriques devient possible avec le nouvel instrument et permet d'accéder à la composition chimique des interfaces carbures-matrice. De plus, l'analyse Auger des facettes intergranulaires pourra être faite en-dehors des carbures et permettra d'accéder à la quantification du carbone ségrégé dans le joint.

Enfin, le dernier axe de travail consistera à développer une méthode de quantification de la ségrégation intergranulaire sans rupture. Il s’agira de travailler ici sur une coupe polie du matériau à étudier et à réaliser des analyses locales, par exemple des profils de concentrations à travers les joints de grains.

Compte tenu de l'excellente résolution latérale, on peut ainsi espérer détecter la ségrégation par cette méthode. Une méthode de traitement des données devra être développée pour accéder à des concentrations intergranulaires de solutés. Une telle méthode a déjà été mise au point pour des analyses réalisées par nanoSIMS et pourrait être transposée sur la spectrométrie Auger. Elle permettrait de s’affranchir de la nécessité d'obtenir une rupture intergranulaire (particulièrement limitante en spectrométrie Auger), tout en conservant une préparation d’échantillon très simple (coupe polie) et une productivité potentiellement importante (grand nombre de joints analysables dans un échantillon donné).

description:
Unité : CERI Energie Environnement - DEMO MERA/LCSQA

Responsables : Emmanuel TISON, Anthony LAGACHE

Catégorie : Stagiaire de Master 2 ou de fin d’études ingénieur (6 mois)

Lieu de travail : Douai – Bourseul, Bâtiment Curie

 

Contexte :

École sous tutelle du Ministère de l’Économie, des Finances et de la Souveraineté industrielle, énergétique et numérique, et école de l’Institut Mines Télécom, IMT Nord Europe a 3 missions principales : former des ingénieurs responsables aptes à résoudre les grandes problématiques du XXIème siècle ; mener des recherches débouchant sur des innovations à haute valeur ajoutée ; soutenir le développement des territoires notamment en facilitant l’innovation et les créations d’entreprises. Son objectif est de former les ingénieurs de demain, maîtrisant à la fois les technologies numériques et les savoir-faire industriels. Idéalement située au carrefour de l’Europe, à 1 heure de Paris, 30 minutes de Bruxelles et 1H30 de Londres, IMT Nord Europe a l’ambition de devenir un acteur majeur des grandes transformations industrielles, numériques et environnementales du XXIème siècle en combinant, tant dans ses enseignements et que dans sa recherche, les sciences de l’ingénieur et les technologies du digital.

 

Localisée sur 2 sites principaux d’enseignement et de recherche, à Lille et à Douai, IMT Nord Europe s’appuie sur plus de 20000m² de laboratoire pour développer un enseignement de haut niveau et une recherche d’excellence dans les domaines suivants :

  • Systèmes Numériques

  • Energie Environnement

  • Matériaux et Procédés

 

Pour plus de détails, consulter le site internet de l’École : www.imt-nord-europe.fr.

 

Le stage est à pourvoir au sein du Centre d’Enseignement, de Recherche et d’Innovation Energie Environnement (CERI EE) de l’IMT Nord Europe. Une partie des missions du CERI EE (https://recherche.imt-nord-europe.fr/energie-environnement-ceri/) est de réaliser des travaux techniques et scientifiques pour le Ministère chargé de l’Environnement dans le cadre du Laboratoire Central de Surveillance de la Qualité de l’Air (LCSQA, https://www.lcsqa.org/fr) et de l’observatoire de Mesure et Évaluation en zone Rurale de la pollution Atmosphérique à longue distance (MERA, https://www.lcsqa.org/fr/le-dispositif-mera). En concertation avec les Associations Agréées de Surveillance de la Qualité de l'Air (AASQA), le CERI EE est chargé de proposer et qualifier les méthodes de mesure à déployer, de définir les protocoles, d’évaluer la qualité des données et de piloter l’observatoire MERA intégré au dispositif français de surveillance réglementaire de la qualité de l’air.

 

Contexte :

L'ammoniac (NH3) est un polluant atmosphérique nocif pour la santé humaine, les écosystèmes et l'environnement, mais aussi un précurseur de particules fines inorganiques notamment responsables de forts épisodes de pollution printaniers en Europe. En France, la source dominante d'ammoniac (environ 95%) est attribuée aux activités agricoles (épandage de fumier, utilisation d'engrais azotés, élevage). À partir de 2027, la directive européenne 2024/2881 exige que le NH3 soit mesuré spécifiquement sur les supersites implantés dans des lieux caractéristiques de la pollution de fond rurale. La France répond à cette obligation en déployant 6 supersites de surveillance de typologie fond rural, répartis dans des zones représentatives de la pollution longue-distance, et sélectionnés au sein des stations de l’observatoire MERA. Ces supersites sont équipés d’analyseurs automatiques en continu pour mesurer le NH3 à une très haute résolution temporelle. Ces méthodes permettent une mesure en temps réel, pour capturer la variabilité temporelle du NH3. Cependant, le NH3 est un polluant particulièrement complexe à mesurer notamment en raison de difficultés métrologiques (absence de méthode standardisée, interférences etc.) et de ses propriétés physico-chimiques (grande réactivité avec les surfaces, volatilisation, formation de particules etc.).

 

Objectif :

L'objectif de ce stage est d’apporter des éléments méthodologiques qui permettront d’établir des recommandations nationales concernant la sélection et les pratiques de mise en œuvre des préleveurs automatiques, afin d’améliorer la fiabilité et l’harmonisation des mesures de l’ammoniac.

 

Livrables :

·         Synthèse bibliographique ciblée sur les difficultés métrologiques de la mesure du NH₃ et les solutions à évaluer

·         Production d’un plan d’expériences détaillé à suivre durant le stage et d’un protocole d’assurance et de contrôle qualité des données.

·          Jeu de données documenté, fichiers ou scripts de traitement reproductibles et bilan des performances observées.

·         Présentation des résultats au groupe de travail national pour la mesure de NH3

·         Projet de note de recommandations pour le prélèvement de NH₃ en zone rurale, soumis à la validation des encadrants et du groupe de travail national. Les conclusions distingueront les points établis des points restant à confirmer.


Profil du candidat :

Ce stage est destiné à un.e étudiant.e en dernière année d’école d’ingénieur ou M2 universitaire avec un profil en analyses physico-chimiques, en instrumentation, mesure et assurance qualité appliquées à l’environnement, avec un goût prononcé pour les approches expérimentales.

De grandes qualités d’analyse, de rédaction, d’organisation, de communication et d’autonomie sont attendues.

Curiosité scientifique, rigueur et aptitude au travail en équipe sont recherchées. Un bon niveau d’anglais scientifique est souhaité pour la lecture bibliographique. Des compétences en traitement de données (Python, R ou Matlab) seront appréciées. Une première pratique de la chimie analytique et des notions de métrologie et d’assurance qualité seront des atouts.

  • Care
    We care deeply about our customers, our teammates, and the quality and reliability of what we ship.

  • Bias for Action
    We move fast, test in the real world, and iterate quickly rather than over-optimizing in theory.

  • Ownership
    We take responsibility end to end, from identifying problems to delivering outcomes and learning from results.

About the role

When your product is the front door to someone else’s product, security isn’t a feature, it’s the product. Every login and every signup that goes through Prelude is a moment where our customers trust us with their users, their phone numbers, and their reputation.

As our first dedicated Security Engineer, you’ll own security across Prelude: our cloud infrastructure, our codebase, our APIs and SDKs, and the way we handle the sensitive data that flows through them. You’ll start from solid ground: a certified ISO 27001 and SOC 2 program, short-lived credentials across our cloud environment, and a 24/7 on-call rotation. You’ll run that foundation day to day and take it further, with direct support from Engineering leadership and the founders.

This is a hands-on IC role: you’ll write code, ship guardrails, and fix things yourself, and set the standard for how every engineer at Prelude thinks about security.

What you’ll do

Own the security of our cloud infrastructure. Harden our AWS and ClickHouse environments and make the secure path the default for every service we deploy.

Build security into how we ship. Run threat modeling and design reviews with engineers, review critical code paths, and extend our automated checks in CI/CD (adding dependency scanning, secrets detection, and container and IaC security scanning) without slowing the team down.

Protect our customers’ users and their data. Personal data is at the heart of our product. Design and enforce the controls that protect it (encryption, access control, retention, and auditability) in line with GDPR and our customers’ expectations.

Mature detection and incident response. Extend our logging, alerting, and runbooks to spot abuse and compromise early, lead incident response when something goes wrong, and write honest post-mortems the next morning.

Drive compliance and customer trust. Maintain and mature our SOC 2 and ISO 27001 certifications through surveillance and recertification audits. Own our answers to enterprise security questionnaires, and be the technical voice of Prelude’s security posture with our largest customers.

Partner with our anti-fraud team. Fraud here isn’t theoretical. Work alongside the engineers fighting SMS pumping, toll fraud, bot traffic, and account takeover attempts in production, bringing an attacker’s mindset to the problems at the core of our product.

Use AI to multiply your impact. AI is already part of how we build. Make it part of how we defend: automate triage, log analysis, questionnaire answers, and code review so a team of one can operate like a team of five.

Join the on-call rotation for the systems you secure.

  • Strong software engineering skills: you can read and write production code, ideally in Go or TypeScript, and fix vulnerabilities yourself rather than just filing tickets

  • Solid knowledge of web and API security (OWASP Top 10, authentication and authorization flows, rate limiting, abuse prevention)

  • Experience building or running security programs pragmatically: you know which 20% of controls cover 80% of the risk at a company our size

  • Experience with incident response and with setting up logging, monitoring, and alerting

  • A builder’s mindset: you prefer guardrails and automation over gatekeeping, and engineers see you as a partner, not a blocker

Nice to have

renerco plan consult gestaltet die Energiewende aktiv mit. In den Bereichen Windenergie, Photovoltaik, Netzanschluss und Sektorkopplung. Deutschlandweit und in Europa.

Unser stetiger Anspruch ist es, unseren Kunden in Planung und Beratung Lösungen in höchster Qualität zu liefern. Nachhaltig, effizient, vertrauensvoll.

Wir sind Teil der Natural-Power-Gruppe, einem internationalen Ingenieursdienstleister im Bereich der Erneuerbaren Energien mit weiteren Niederlassungen in UK, Irland, Frankreich, Italien und den USA.

Ihre Mission bei uns

Sie begleiten nationale und internationale Investoren, Projektentwickler sowie Windparkbetreiber bei der Bewertung und Weiterentwicklung von Windenergie- und Batteriespeicherprojekten in Deutschland und Europa.

Dabei übernehmen Sie Verantwortung in technisch-wirtschaftlichen Prozessen und unterstützen anspruchsvolle Transaktions- und Beratungsprojekte.

title: Applikationsingenieur/ -techniker (m/w/d) industrielle Bildverarbeitung
description:
Endlich wieder auf Montag freuen!

Willkommen bei senswork, wo spannende Aufgaben, ein gutes Arbeitsklima und eine ausgewogene Work-Life-Balance nicht nur Versprechen sind, sondern unserer Unternehmenskultur prägen. Werde Teil eines Teams, das sich gegenseitig unterstützt und inspiriert.

Unsere Lösungen zur Automatisierung und Qualitätssicherung werden täglich in zahlreichen Branchen wie der Automobilindustrie, dem Maschinenbau oder der Medizintechnik eingesetzt. Von unseren Standorten Burghausen und München aus betreuen wir namhafte Kunden aus Industrie und Forschung. Wir analysieren Aufgaben im Detail und gehen auf individuelle Vorgaben ein, um ein passgenaues Kamerasystem, den perfekten Prüfplatz oder das ideale Prüfgerät zu entwickeln. So ist jedes Projekt anders, jeder Arbeitstag bietet neue Herausforderungen. Bist auch Du der neuesten Technik gerne einen Schritt voraus, dann freuen wir uns auf Dich.

Als Applikationsingenieur/in in der industriellen Bildverarbeitung bist Du für die Entwicklung und Implementierung von Bildverarbeitungslösungen in verschiedenen industriellen Anwendungen verantwortlich. Deine Hauptaufgabe besteht darin, kundenspezifische Anforderungen zu analysieren, Lösungskonzepte zu erstellen und die Umsetzung von Bildverarbeitungsprojekten zu begleiten. Du arbeitest eng mit Kunden, Vertriebsteams, Produktmanagern und internen Entwicklungsabteilungen zusammen.



Deine Aufgaben:


  • Anforderungsanalyse: Du führst Gespräche mit Kunden, um ihre spezifischen Anforderungen an die Bildverarbeitung zu verstehen und zu dokumentieren. Dabei ermittelst du die technischen und funktionalen Anforderungen und berücksichtigst die individuellen Rahmenbedingungen der Kundenprojekte.
  • Lösungsentwicklung: Auf Basis der Anforderungsanalyse entwickelst du maßgeschneiderte Bildverarbeitungslösungen. Du evaluierst geeignete Kamerasysteme, Optiken, Beleuchtungstechniken und Bildverarbeitungsalgorithmen, um die besten Ergebnisse zu erzielen.
  • Systemintegration: Du bist verantwortlich für die Integration der Bildverarbeitungslösung in die bestehende Kundeninfrastruktur. Dazu gehört die Anbindung an Steuerungen, Robotersysteme oder andere Automatisierungskomponenten.
  • Prototypentwicklung und Tests: Du erstellst Prototypen der Bildverarbeitungssysteme und führst umfangreiche Tests durch, um die Funktionsfähigkeit und die Leistungsfähigkeit sicherzustellen. Dabei optimierst du die Systeme, um eine hohe Genauigkeit und Zuverlässigkeit zu gewährleisten.
  • Kundenschulungen und Support: Du schulst die Kunden im Umgang mit den Bildverarbeitungssystemen und bietest technischen Support während der Implementierungs- und Betriebsphase. Bei auftretenden Problemen bist du für die Fehleranalyse und -behebung zuständig.
  • Technologie-Trends und Weiterentwicklung: Du verfolgst aktuelle Entwicklungen und Trends in der industriellen Bildverarbeitung und bringst dein Wissen in die Optimierung der bestehenden Lösungen sowie die Entwicklung neuer Produkte ein.




Dein Profil:


  • Erfolgreich abgeschlossene Ausbildung oder Studium in den Bereichen Elektronik, Informatik oder Automatisierung
  • Kenntnisse im Umgang mit Softwareprodukten, optional Erfahrungen in der Softwareentwicklung mit C/ C++, C#
  • Ausgeprägtes analytisches Denken sowie aktive, eigenverantwortliche und strukturierte Arbeitsweise
  • Interesse an der Mitarbeit in Projekten
  • Idealerweise: Kenntnisse im Bereich Kameratechnik/Bildverarbeitung/Automatisierung
  • Führerschein Klasse B

title: Teamleitung Forderungsmanagement (m/w/d)
description:
Schwerpunkt Teamsteuerung & Organisation
**DICH suchen wir**

Du bist ein Organisationstalent und verstehst es, Menschen zu motivieren? Bei der VITASERV AG suchen wir eine Teamleitung, die unser Team im Forderungsmanagement (Insolvenzen) operativ steuert. Aufgaben

Du bist verantwortlich für

  • Operative Teamsteuerung: Du planst und koordinierst die täglichen Aufgaben im Bereich Insolvenzsachbearbeitung und stellst eine gleichmäßige Auslastung & Abarbeitung sicher.

  • Mitarbeiterführung & Entwicklung: Du führst regelmäßige Feedbackgespräche, förderst die Talente in deinem Team und sorgst für ein motivierendes Arbeitsklima.

  • Monitoring & Reporting: Du behältst die Kennzahlen (KPIs) und Fristen im Blick und berichtest über den Fortschritt und die Performance an die Bereichsleitung.

  • Schnittstellenmanagement: Du bildest die Brücke zwischen deinem Team und der Fachbereichsleitung sowie mit den Kunden.

  • Ressourcenplanung: Du verantwortest die Urlaubs- und Vertretungsplanung, damit der Betrieb auch in Stoßzeiten reibungslos läuft.Prozessoptimierung: Du identifizierst Engpässe im Arbeitsablauf und entwickelst gemeinsam mit dem Team Lösungen für effizientere Workflows

  • Führungspersönlichkeit: Du hast bereits Erfahrung in der Führung oder Koordination von Teams gesammelt – idealerweise in einem kaufmännischen Umfeld oder Dienstleistungssektor.

  • Organisationstalent: Du liebst Struktur, behältst auch bei hohem Arbeitsaufkommen den Überblick und kannst Prioritäten klar setzen.

  • Standfestigkeit: Souveräner Umgang auch bei wechselnden Anforderungen und Zeitdruck.

  • Proaktives Handeln: Du packst Probleme aktiv an und sorgst für ein lösungsorientiertes Umfeld.

Benefits

Wir bieten dir

  • Attraktives Gehaltspaket, das deine Führungserfahrung würdigt.

  • Monatsgehalt.

  • 30 Urlaubstage pro Jahr sowie am 24.12. und 31.12. frei.

  • Fachspezifische Weiterbildungen.

  • Betriebliche Benefits (z. B. Gesundheitsmanagement, JobRad, monatlicher Sachbezug, Altersvorsorge, Teamevents).

  • Corporate Benefits

  • Mitarbeiter-Werben-Mitarbeiter Prämie

  • Kostenloses Wasser

Dein Arbeitsumfeld

  • Teamspirit: Ein eingespieltes Team im Forderungsmanagement, das auf deine Unterstützung wartet.

  • Flexibilität: Flexible Arbeitszeiten und hybrides Arbeiten nach erfolgreicher Einarbeitung

  • Rückhalt: Fachliche Unterstützung durch einen erfahrenen Fachexperten, damit du dich voll auf die Steuerung konzentrieren kannst.

title: Forward-Deployed CRM Architect
description:
RevOps is changing fast, and so is the way GTM processes get built and maintained inside the CRM. This role puts you on the front edge of it: forward-deployed in our clients' RevOps teams, building and running their GTM systems in a genuinely AI-first environment.

GTMBase is an AI-first GTM engineering and RevOps agency. We help post-PMF B2B companies (€8M to €50M ARR, 5+ reps) whose go-to-market is over-performing their systems. Reps do manually what should be automated, sales and marketing data doesn't connect, and leadership can't trust the reporting.

We combine strategic GTM thinking with hands-on technical build, and we fix the foundation before running campaigns.

We deliver across Four Pillars:

  1. Data Foundation: list building and enrichment so reps win with better data (Clay, Apollo, custom scrapers, AI research)
  2. RevOps & CRM: building the right GTM process inside the client's CRM, including architecture, lifecycle, pipelines, routing, and reporting (HubSpot, Salesforce)
  3. Agentic Workflows: building agentic GTM workflows with Anthropic Managed Agents and Hermes, getting the org ready for Agentic GTM
  4. GTM Strategy & Plays: recommending and executing the highest-impact campaigns

We've done this for clients including Groupon, Blinkist, Booksy, and Sendify. We work in small pods, with a Strategist, a CRM Architect, and a GTM Engineer.

How We Operate

We run the company on Claude Code. It's our operating system: client context, playbooks, automations, and delivery all live in it, and AI is the default way we work rather than a bolt-on. You'll work this way too, and get very good at it.

Why This Role Matters

You're the person who turns our GTM strategy into a CRM that actually works. Most clients run their entire revenue motion on HubSpot or Salesforce, and the quality of that system runs through this role: how clean the data is, how well leads route, whether leadership can trust the reporting.

Here, "Architect" means architecting inside the CRM: the object model, pipelines, workflows, and automations. The GTM and revenue strategy is set with you in your pod, not by you alone, and you build it with real craft.

You're forward-deployed: you embed with clients' RevOps and sales teams and build inside their live CRM.

The Role

You'll build and maintain GTM process and automation inside our clients' CRMs, mostly HubSpot. Working from the direction set in your pod, you turn requirements into a clean, well-built system the sales team can rely on.

One week you're building a client's lead lifecycle and routing. The next you're debugging a broken automation, untangling duplicate deals, or shipping a dashboard a CRO asked for. You move across several client instances at once without dropping threads.

You're a builder with an admin's discipline. You know the object model, not just the UI. You sweat the details others miss, you test before you ship, and you document what you build so the rest of the pod can run it. When something breaks, you find the root cause and fix it properly.

How This Differs From a GTM Engineer

Your pod is you (CRM Architect), a Strategist who sets direction and hands you requirements, and a GTM Engineer. You and the GTM Engineer are both builders, but you own different layers:

  • You (CRM Architect, Pillar 2): the GTM process inside the CRM. HubSpot/Salesforce architecture, lifecycle, routing, deal logic, automation, reporting, data integrity. You live in HubSpot, Salesforce, Operations Hub, and n8n.
  • GTM Engineer (Pillar 1): the data layer. Enrichment, scraping, signal detection, list building, custom research agents. They live in Clay, Apify, custom scrapers, and data APIs.

Think of it as the data into the CRM (GTM Engineer) versus the system it lands in and the process the sales team runs on (you). You don't need to be a Clay or Apify expert. You just need a solid working understanding of what a GTM Engineer does, enough to spec what you need, integrate their output cleanly, and know what's possible.

What You'll Do

  • Architect and build in client HubSpot instances: information architecture (objects, associations, lifecycle stages, pipeline structure), workflows, deal logic, lead scoring, routing, properties, and permissions
  • Build and debug automations across the GTM stack: HubSpot workflows, n8n, APIs, and webhooks. When an automation breaks, you find the root cause rather than just toggling features
  • Guard data integrity: deduplication, field validation, association hygiene, and import discipline so reporting and forecasting can be trusted
  • Build the reporting leadership relies on: pipeline coverage and velocity, stage-by-stage conversion, and full-funnel dashboards. You know where HubSpot's platform and paywall limits force a different approach
  • Design integrations and data flows between HubSpot and the rest of the stack (Clay, Aircall, telephony, billing, enrichment pipelines)
  • Turn requirements into working builds: take a brief like a 15-minute lead-response SLA and ship the routing system that delivers it
  • Keep multiple client instances healthy at once, with fast turnaround and nothing falling through the cracks
  • Work client-facing: you can talk through a data question with a technical lead and walk a frustrated AE through a new flow in the same afternoon
  • Codify what works into our library of reusable plays and patterns, so every client build sharpens the whole team

What We're Looking For

Must-have

  • Deep HubSpot expertise: hands-on across Sales, Marketing, Service, and Operations Hubs. You know HubSpot well enough to know what is and isn't possible at the platform level, and to choose native functionality over a workaround when it's the right call.
  • Strong CRM and RevOps fundamentals: lead lifecycle and qualification, routing and assignment, pipeline and deal-stage setup, the data model, and the governance that keeps it clean.
  • An admin's discipline: precise, reliable, and detail-obsessed. You test before you ship, you keep data clean, and you don't let things fall through the cracks.
  • A builder's instinct: you build workflows and integrations, debug them when they break, and aren't intimidated by APIs, webhooks, or a tool you haven't used yet.
  • AI-first, and we mean it literally: AI is your default operating mode, not a novelty. Your first move on a problem is to reach for an agent, a prompt, or a workflow before a manual process. If you're not already using AI tools daily, this isn't the right fit. (If your CRM fundamentals are deep but your GTM-tooling experience like Clay or Claude Code is light, that part is learnable and we'll back you on it. The fundamentals and the AI-first instinct are not.)
  • Forward-deployed temperament: comfortable building across multiple clients in parallel, client-facing, proactive, and able to move fast without waiting for perfect requirements.
  • Full-time availability with reliable overlap to CET hours.

Nice-to-have

  • Salesforce: admin or build experience, especially HubSpot to Salesforce sync and migrations (relevant to Groupon and enterprise work)
  • A working understanding of the GTM Engineer's toolkit: Clay, Apify, enrichment providers (ZoomInfo, Apollo, Clearbit), scraping. Enough to collaborate, spec, and integrate. Your pod's GTM Engineer owns the deep builds.
  • n8n orchestration and custom API integrations
  • Scripting (Python, SQL, or JavaScript) for data manipulation and custom connectors
  • German: a good chunk of our client base is DACH
  • HubSpot certifications: a plus, never a gate. Demonstrated depth matters more.

What You'll Get

  • Real client build work from day one, with no busy work and no hand-holding
  • A front-row seat in a genuinely AI-first environment: Claude Code as the operating system, Clay, and the full modern GTM stack
  • Direct collaboration with one of the most experienced RevOps leaders in Europe
  • Exposure to a wide range of B2B companies, stacks, and GTM problems
  • A seat at the table in a growing practice, not a cog in a machine

title: Product Marketing Lead
description:
Product Marketing Lead

Reporting to: CMO

Location: London (hybrid, 4 days a week in the office)

Salary: £80,000-£100,000 + equity

About Electric Twin

Most organisations make their biggest decisions on a thin slice of evidence - a handful of customer calls, one survey, instinct when the data runs out. Electric Twin changes that. We build synthetic audiences: simulations of real groups of people, grounded in research data. Teams ask them questions, test ideas and explore how people might respond, and get answers in minutes that would otherwise take weeks.

The work is grounded, and the science is real. We've run over 40,000 evaluations across populations covering 155 countries. Independent academic research with Professor Michael Muthukrishna at the LSE found our outputs come back roughly 10,000x faster than traditional methods, at 95% accuracy. Customers including The Times, Sage, Virgin, Vodafone and Wingstop use Electric Twin to bring customer insight into decisions about campaigns, products, pricing and strategy.

Electric Twin was founded by Dr Ben Warner (former Chief Data Advisor to the UK Prime Minister) and our CEO, Alex Cooper (a former senior military commander and Director of Mass Covid Testing in the pandemic). We're backed by Atomico, LocalGlobe, Mercuri and angels including Marc Andreessen. We're a team of engineers, AI researchers, behavioural scientists and operators - careful with the science, careful with the responsibility.

The role

We're hiring a Product Marketing Lead to own product marketing at Electric Twin, from the strategy through to the sales deck.

Our ambition is to make understanding people a normal part of making decisions. Product marketing is central to that. It's how we decide who Electric Twin is for, what we compete against and why a buyer should choose us, and how that story reaches the market through our product, our website and our sales team.

Next year is a big one. We're launching in new markets, taking Electric Twin to more parts of a business, and bringing more products to market. We need someone who has operated at this level before, and who can join the dots between sales, marketing and product.

Product marketing here covers four areas: insights, storytelling, go-to-market and enablement. You'll own all four, and decide where to lean in as the company grows.

You'll work closely with our CMO, our VP Product and our sales team. Our Growth Lead runs the engine - the channels and programmes that reach and convert our audience. Product marketing and content provide the fuel. You'll own positioning and messaging. Our Content Lead will turn it into stories and get them out across every channel.

This is a hands-on role. You'll set the strategy, and you'll also write the launch plan, the value proposition brief and the sales deck yourself.

What’s exciting - you’re the founding PMM and get to build out and lead this function as we expand.

What you'll do

Insights

  • Be the expert on our customer. We have strong customer research, a map of what customers want to use the product for and a regular round-up of the questions they ask. Build on it, keep it current and make sure the rest of the business uses it.

  • Understand the buyers we're growing into. Our buyer today is the insights team. Marketing, product and commercial teams come next. Speak to them, define who they are and work out what they need to hear from us.

  • Know the market. This is a fast-moving category, with research incumbents launching their own products and a new batch of innovators arriving. Track it, and keep a clear, committed point of view on how Electric Twin is different.

  • Bring an opinion to product strategy. Work with our VP Product on the value proposition, and bring the customer and the market into decisions about what we build.

Storytelling

  • Own our positioning and messaging. Keep one consistent way of describing what Electric Twin is, who it is for and why a buyer should choose it, used by sales, product and marketing.

  • Own the trust story. Trust is central to how buyers choose us. Own how we prove it: the evidence, the customer stories and the guidance for prospects who want to evaluate us for themselves.

  • Turn the product into language a buyer would use. Take what we build and describe it in the customer's words, across the website, the product and our sales materials.

  • Shape the story for new markets and buyers. Build and adjust the narrative for our new market launches, and for the teams beyond insight and research that we want to reach.

Go-to-market

  • Set the product narrative. Agree a product narrative each quarter with our VP Product, so every launch adds up to a bigger story.

  • Run our launches. Build a tiered launch process so the effort matches the size of the release, and run it with product, sales and marketing.

  • Take Electric Twin to new buyers and markets. Plan how we go to market in the US, in new verticals and with new teams inside our customers.

  • Improve the buyer journey on our website. Work with growth, content and design so the site shows the product and has something for visitors who aren't yet ready to talk to sales.

Enablement

  • Equip our sales team. A sales deck built on our positioning, battlecards for the alternatives that come up most, ROI material for the economic buyer and a pack our champions can take to their senior stakeholders.

  • Build a working relationship with sales. Agree priorities together, with one route in for requests and a short brief for each.

  • Train sales and CX. Run onboarding and regular training on our positioning, product, use cases and objection handling, so both teams can explain our value and help customers get the most from Electric Twin.

  • Build feedback loops across teams. Create regular workflows that bring sales objections, win/loss insights and CX feedback into product priorities, positioning and enablement. Take updates back to those teams and check whether they solve the problems raised.

  • Be an advocate inside the business. Present to the company, and represent the customer and the product in the conversations that matter. You need to be the central point between Sales, Marketing and Product and drive the strategy proactively to each - ultimately for the benefit of the customer.

  • Build our product marketing operating system. Bring our research, positioning and messaging into one managed source of truth that feeds the tools used across product, sales, customer success and internal comms. Use AI to build repeatable workflows on top of it and keep it updated.

Your first six months

  • Take our positioning and messaging and get it into the website, sales enablement and our core external-facing materials.

  • Agree the first quarterly product narrative with our VP Product, and get a tiered launch process running.

  • Rebuild sales enablement, with battlecards, ROI material and a pack for champions.

  • Define the marketing buyer and build the narrative for our new market launches.

  • Get the product marketing operating system up and running.

What we're looking for

Experience

  • At least five years in product marketing alone. You've done this role before, ideally growing a product in a similar space or selling to an enterprise audience.

  • You've owned positioning and messaging, and taken it through to a website and sales materials that people used.

  • You've run product launches with a product team, and worked closely with a sales team on what they need to win deals.

  • You've partnered with senior product and commercial leaders, and you're as comfortable having an opinion on product strategy as on sales and commercial strategy.

  • You understand the tools and techniques of the trade, including Jobs-to-be-done and know how to define messaging and positioning.

Skills and approach

  • Autonomous. You can own the strategy and ship the copy without much steering. .

  • A good writer, and strong at the content specific to product marketing, such as sales decks and value proposition briefs.

  • A strong communicator. You can present internally and be an advocate for the customer and the product.

  • Curious and proactive. You know what you don't know, you read up or ask for help, and you act on problems once you've spotted them.

  • You've used AI to build repeatable workflows, and you can judge when the output is good enough and when it isn't.

  • You can operate in a fast-paced environment that has ambiguity.

  • You work with a sense of urgency, you raise issues as they arise and you anticipate problems

  • Careful with the details. You're comfortable getting to grips with AI, research and technical subjects, you ask good questions and you check claims carefully.

What we offer

  • £80,000-£100,000 base

  • Meaningful equity in a high-potential seed-stage company

  • Unlimited leave. Take the time you need

  • Generous matched pension contributions

  • Private healthcare

  • Cycle to work scheme

  • Ownership of product marketing, with real influence over how the function is built

  • Direct access to and collaboration with world-class founders

  • Hybrid working from our London office (4 days in office a week)

  • Flexible working around life commitments. We value outcomes over presenteeism

When you apply, please share examples of your product marketing work, such as positioning, a launch or sales materials, explaining your contribution and what it achieved.

description:

Industrial labor is one of the most acute bottlenecks in the global economy. Operators are expensive, hard to retain, and working in environments that are increasingly unsafe. The shortage is structural. The window to solve it is now.

Already live across multiple sites and customers in Europe - spanning logistics and warehousing, industrial manufacturing, and large-scale chemical production - with a US expansion underway.

The vision: one operator managing hundreds of machines simultaneously. Productive machine-hour cost dropping by 80x, and unlocks the next productivity revolution in physical work.

The mission is to make productivity limitless. Come and help us build it.

 

The role

We are looking for a pragmatic, field-oriented Operational Safety Advisor whose mission is to enable safe, efficient and repeatable deployments of autonomous industrial machines. Working within the Deployment team, you will help customers and Deployment Managers identify operational risks early, agree practical mitigations and remove blockers. Your role is to simplify how safety is addressed, not add bureaucracy, complexity or new approval gates.


Key responsibilities

Site visits and operational assessments

  • Visit customer sites to understand working practices, machine movements, pedestrian interfaces, traffic management, visibility and exclusion zones.

  • Identify operational risks early and work with customers and Deployment Managers to propose proportionate, practical actions that keep deployments moving safely.

  • Support early site feasibility (pre / post contract signing) and readiness discussions, using existing deployment milestones rather than creating additional approval stages.

Operational safety advisory

  • Advise customers on operational risk assessments, safe systems of work, emergency arrangements, access controls, training and supervision.

  • Recommend simple, workable operational mitigations and help customer HSE and site management teams implement them.

  • Escalate product-related or technical safety issues to Engineering rather than owning their design or approval.

Standards, checklists and continuous improvement

  • Continuously simplify Hive’s operational safety checklists, site assessment templates and practical advisory guidance; keep them risk-based, concise and reusable.

  • Record only the essential findings, decisions, actions and owners needed to support safe execution and clear handover.

  • Turn lessons learned into fewer recurring blockers, better standard practices and faster repeatable deployments.

Deployment collaboration

  • Work proactively with Deployment Managers and Commercial to resolve operational safety dependencies early, before they delay site mobilisation or go-live.

  • Support customer-led operational readiness and handover within the existing deployment process; do not establish a separate Hive operational-safety approval gate.

  • Communicate concerns clearly, propose solutions and escalate material risks promptly; enable decisions rather than becoming a bottleneck.

Essential experience and skills

  • Practical operational HSE / safety experience in industrial, construction, quarrying, ports, logistics or heavy-equipment environments.

  • Proven experience conducting site inspections and operational risk assessments and recommending workable controls.

  • Understanding of mobile machinery interfaces with people, vehicles and site operations.

  • Ability to produce short, actionable, risk-based checklists and guidance without unnecessary documentation.

  • Confident communication with site managers, operators, customer HSE teams and deployment personnel.

  • Willingness to travel frequently and work independently in active industrial environments.

Desirable

Experience with heavy mobile plant, remote operations or automation; familiarity with UK/EU workplace safety requirements and relevant industry qualifications (e.g. NEBOSH or IOSH).


Success in the first six months

  • A lean, risk-based operational safety assessment approach is embedded in existing deployment workflows without additional approval gates.

  • Operational risks and blockers are identified early, with practical mitigations, clear owners and timely resolution.

  • Deployment Managers have concise, reusable guidance that reduces rework and accelerates safe site mobilisation.

  • Lessons learned are converted into simpler standards and more predictable deployments across regions.

In joining us, you will be helping to create cutting-edge technologies that will improve how we diagnose and treat brain disorders, ultimately improving and saving the lives of patients across the world.

The Role

The Data Science team at CoMind develops the algorithms and machine learning systems that transform raw optical interference signals from CoMind One into continuous, clinically meaningful measurements of cerebral blood flow, intracranial pressure, and autoregulation. Working at the frontier of photonics, physiology, and applied ML, the team's work directly determines what CoMind One can measure, how accurately, and under what clinical conditions.

As Principal Data Scientist, you will be a technical authority for CoMind's data science function, setting methodological direction for signal condition and extraction, personally driving the most complex and highest-impact problems, and providing expert guidance on data science best practice across the team. This is a senior individual contributor role: you will not manage people directly, but your technical leadership will shape how the entire team approaches its most challenging problems. You will work closely with R&D, Clinical, and Software Engineering.

At CoMind, all team members work at least 4 days per week from our new Kings Cross offices, plus a flexible work-from-home day.

Responsibilities:

  • Act as the technical authority for the end-to-end signal processing and inference chain for CoMind’s technologies: from raw optical data through to clinical measurements

  • Set the methodological direction for estimation, signal extraction and ML modelling across the team: which approaches suit which problems, how they are evaluated, and what evidence is required before a method is trusted.
